# Builtin reference (the text HELP "NAME" shows)

[ABS]
Syntax: ABS(numeric_expression)
Description: Returns the absolute value of a number or an array of numbers.

[ACOS]
Syntax: ACOS(x)
Description: Inverse cosine in radians. Vectorizes element-wise over arrays.

[AI.ARGMAX]
Syntax: AI.ARGMAX(vec) -> index
Description: Returns the index of the largest element.

[AI.CHAT$]
Syntax: AI.CHAT$(id, prompt$) -> response$
Description: Multi-turn chat using the model's chat template plus its running history.

[AI.CHAT]
Syntax: AI.CHAT(id, prompt$) -> response$
Description: Old name of AI.CHAT$, still accepted for one release; --lint, jdb_check and -c name AI.CHAT$, and tools/jdb-fix.jdb rewrites it.

[AI.CHAT_JSON]
Syntax: AI.CHAT_JSON(id, prompt$) -> object
Description: One-shot JSON generation: temporarily enables JSON mode, generates, and returns the parsed object.

[AI.CHAT_RAW$]
Syntax: AI.CHAT_RAW$(id, raw_prompt$) -> text$
Description: Bypasses the chat template and history; sends a raw prompt and returns raw text.

[AI.CHAT_RAW]
Syntax: AI.CHAT_RAW(id, raw_prompt$) -> text$
Description: Old name of AI.CHAT_RAW$, still accepted for one release; --lint, jdb_check and -c name AI.CHAT_RAW$, and tools/jdb-fix.jdb rewrites it.

[AI.CHAT_STREAM$]
Syntax: AI.CHAT_STREAM$(id, prompt$, callback) -> response$
Description: Like AI.CHAT but streams tokens to a callback FUNC OnToken(piece$); returning FALSE aborts generation.

[AI.CHAT_STREAM]
Syntax: AI.CHAT_STREAM(id, prompt$, callback) -> response$
Description: Old name of AI.CHAT_STREAM$, still accepted for one release; --lint, jdb_check and -c name AI.CHAT_STREAM$, and tools/jdb-fix.jdb rewrites it.

[AI.CHAT_TOKENS]
Syntax: AI.CHAT_TOKENS(id, prompt$, [capacity=64]) -> chan
Description: Channel-flavoured streaming chat: returns a CHAN handle that yields generated token strings. Works in interpreter and native -c.

[AI.CLASSIFIER_ADD]
Syntax: AI.CLASSIFIER_ADD(cls_id, text$, label$) -> count
Description: Adds and embeds a single training sample.

[AI.CLASSIFIER_ADD_BATCH]
Syntax: AI.CLASSIFIER_ADD_BATCH(cls_id, texts_arr, labels_arr) -> count
Description: Batch-imports two equal-length arrays of texts and labels.

[AI.CLASSIFIER_BUILD_INDEX]
Syntax: AI.CLASSIFIER_BUILD_INDEX(cls_id, [M=16], [ef_construction=200])
Description: Builds an HNSW index over the training samples for fast prediction on large datasets.

[AI.CLASSIFIER_CREATE]
Syntax: AI.CLASSIFIER_CREATE(embed_llm_id) -> cls_id
Description: Creates an empty k-NN text classifier bound to an embedding model.

[AI.CLASSIFIER_FREE]
Syntax: AI.CLASSIFIER_FREE(cls_id)
Description: Releases a classifier.

[AI.CLASSIFIER_INFO]
Syntax: AI.CLASSIFIER_INFO(cls_id) -> object
Description: Returns {samples, embed_dim, num_labels, labels, index}.

[AI.CLASSIFIER_LOAD]
Syntax: AI.CLASSIFIER_LOAD(path$, embed_llm_id) -> cls_id
Description: Loads a saved classifier; must use the same embedding model.

[AI.CLASSIFIER_PREDICT]
Syntax: AI.CLASSIFIER_PREDICT(cls_id, text$, [k=5]) -> object
Description: Predicts a label, returning {label, confidence, neighbors, votes}.

[AI.CLASSIFIER_SAVE]
Syntax: AI.CLASSIFIER_SAVE(cls_id, path$)
Description: Serializes a classifier to a binary file (magic JCLF), including the HNSW graph.

[AI.CLEAR_GRAMMAR]
Syntax: AI.CLEAR_GRAMMAR(id)
Description: Removes the active GBNF grammar.

[AI.CLEAR_HISTORY]
Syntax: AI.CLEAR_HISTORY(id)
Description: Resets the chat history.

[AI.COSINE_SIM]
Syntax: AI.COSINE_SIM(a, b) -> number
Description: Cosine similarity of two vectors.

[AI.DETOKENIZE$]
Syntax: AI.DETOKENIZE$(id, tokens) -> text$
Description: Converts token ids back into text.

[AI.DETOKENIZE]
Syntax: AI.DETOKENIZE(id, tokens) -> text$
Description: Old name of AI.DETOKENIZE$, still accepted for one release; --lint, jdb_check and -c name AI.DETOKENIZE$, and tools/jdb-fix.jdb rewrites it.

[AI.EMBED]
Syntax: AI.EMBED(text$) -> array
Description: Fallback TF-IDF embedding that needs no loaded model, as [[word, weight], ...].

[AI.EMBED_LLM]
Syntax: AI.EMBED_LLM(id, text$) -> array
Description: Returns the dense embedding vector for text$ using a loaded model.

[AI.FREE]
Syntax: AI.FREE(id)
Description: Releases a loaded ONNX model.

[AI.FREE_LLM]
Syntax: AI.FREE_LLM(id)
Description: Releases an LLM and frees its GPU memory.

[AI.GET_HISTORY]
Syntax: AI.GET_HISTORY(id) -> array
Description: Returns the raw chat history as [{role, content}, ...].

[AI.INFO]
Syntax: AI.INFO(id) -> object
Description: Returns {inputs, outputs}, each with name, shape and type, describing what an ONNX model expects.

[AI.LIST]
Syntax: AI.LIST() -> array
Description: Returns the ids of all currently loaded ONNX models.

[AI.LLM_INFO]
Syntax: AI.LLM_INFO(id) -> object
Description: Returns LLM metadata {n_ctx, n_vocab, n_embd, ...}.

[AI.LOAD]
Syntax: AI.LOAD(path$) -> id
Description: Loads an .onnx model file and returns a model id (ONNX build flag).

[AI.LOAD_EMBEDDINGS]
Syntax: AI.LOAD_EMBEDDINGS(path$, [n_ctx=512], [n_gpu_layers=99]) -> id
Description: Loads an embedding GGUF model in encoder mode (mean pooling over the sequence).

[AI.LOAD_LLM]
Syntax: AI.LOAD_LLM(path$, [n_ctx=2048], [n_gpu_layers=99]) -> id
Description: Loads a generative GGUF model (llama.cpp). n_gpu_layers=99 offloads the whole model to GPU, 0 = pure CPU.

[AI.NORMALIZE]
Syntax: AI.NORMALIZE(vec) -> vec
Description: L2-normalizes a vector.

[AI.RAG_ADD]
Syntax: AI.RAG_ADD(rag_id, text$, [source$="inline"]) -> chunks
Description: Adds a text, splitting it into overlapping chunks tagged with source$.

[AI.RAG_ADD_DIR]
Syntax: AI.RAG_ADD_DIR(rag_id, dirpath$, [pattern$], [recursive=1]) -> stats
Description: Indexes a directory by glob pattern; returns {files_added, files_failed, total_chunks}.

[AI.RAG_ADD_FILE]
Syntax: AI.RAG_ADD_FILE(rag_id, filepath$) -> chunks
Description: Adds a file's contents; .pdf files are parsed with the built-in PDF extractor.

[AI.RAG_BUILD_INDEX]
Syntax: AI.RAG_BUILD_INDEX(rag_id, [M=16], [ef_construction=200])
Description: Builds an HNSW index for fast approximate search (dense mode). Adding chunks afterwards marks it stale.

[AI.RAG_CLEAR]
Syntax: AI.RAG_CLEAR(rag_id)
Description: Empties a RAG store.

[AI.RAG_CREATE]
Syntax: AI.RAG_CREATE(llm_id, [chunk_size=500], [overlap=50], [embed_llm_id=0]) -> rag_id
Description: Creates a RAG store. Dense mode if an embedding model is given, otherwise TF-IDF.

[AI.RAG_FREE]
Syntax: AI.RAG_FREE(rag_id)
Description: Destroys a RAG store.

[AI.RAG_INFO]
Syntax: AI.RAG_INFO(rag_id) -> object
Description: Returns store statistics: chunks, num_labels, mode, embed_dim, chunk_size, index.

[AI.RAG_LOAD]
Syntax: AI.RAG_LOAD(path$, [llm_id], [embed_llm_id]) -> rag_id
Description: Loads a saved RAG store; dense stores need the matching embedding model.

[AI.RAG_QUERY$]
Syntax: AI.RAG_QUERY$(rag_id, question$, [top_k=3]) -> answer$
Description: Full RAG pipeline: search, build the prompt, and generate an answer.

[AI.RAG_QUERY]
Syntax: AI.RAG_QUERY(rag_id, question$, [top_k=3]) -> answer$
Description: Old name of AI.RAG_QUERY$, still accepted for one release; --lint, jdb_check and -c name AI.RAG_QUERY$, and tools/jdb-fix.jdb rewrites it.

[AI.RAG_QUERY_FULL]
Syntax: AI.RAG_QUERY_FULL(rag_id, question$, [top_k=3]) -> object
Description: Like AI.RAG_QUERY but returns {answer, sources} with the chunks used.

[AI.RAG_QUERY_STREAM$]
Syntax: AI.RAG_QUERY_STREAM$(rag_id, question$, callback, [top_k=3]) -> answer$
Description: Streaming RAG query; tokens are delivered to the callback as they are generated.

[AI.RAG_QUERY_STREAM]
Syntax: AI.RAG_QUERY_STREAM(rag_id, question$, callback, [top_k=3]) -> answer$
Description: Old name of AI.RAG_QUERY_STREAM$, still accepted for one release; --lint, jdb_check and -c name AI.RAG_QUERY_STREAM$, and tools/jdb-fix.jdb rewrites it.

[AI.RAG_SAVE]
Syntax: AI.RAG_SAVE(rag_id, path$)
Description: Writes a RAG store to a binary file (magic JRAG), including any HNSW graph.

[AI.RAG_SEARCH]
Syntax: AI.RAG_SEARCH(rag_id, query$, [top_k=3]) -> array
Description: Raw similarity search returning [{score, text, source, index}, ...].

[AI.RUN]
Syntax: AI.RUN(id, input[, input2, ...]) -> result
Description: Runs ONNX inference. The return shape matches the model output (scalar, flat or nested arrays).

[AI.SET]
Syntax: AI.SET(id, key$, value)
Description: Sets a generation parameter: temperature, top_p, top_k, min_p, max_tokens, seed, or system (system prompt).

[AI.SET_GRAMMAR]
Syntax: AI.SET_GRAMMAR(id, gbnf$)
Description: Constrains all subsequent generation to match a GBNF grammar.

[AI.SET_JSON_MODE]
Syntax: AI.SET_JSON_MODE(id)
Description: Installs the built-in JSON grammar so the model can only emit valid JSON.

[AI.SIMILARITY]
Syntax: AI.SIMILARITY(text1$, text2$) -> number
Description: Quick text similarity using TF-IDF.

[AI.SOFTMAX]
Syntax: AI.SOFTMAX(vec) -> vec
Description: Applies softmax to a probability vector.

[AI.TENSOR]
Syntax: AI.TENSOR(data, [shape])
Description: Creates a tensor value from nested arrays, optionally reshaping.

[AI.TOKENIZE]
Syntax: AI.TOKENIZE(id, text$) -> array
Description: Returns the token ids for text$.

[AI.TOKEN_COUNT]
Syntax: AI.TOKEN_COUNT(id, text$) -> number
Description: Counts the tokens in text$ without generating.

[AI.TOOL_ADD]
Syntax: AI.TOOL_ADD(id, name$, params$, description$, funcref)
Description: Registers a jdBasic function as an LLM-callable tool. params$ is a human-readable argument description.

[AI.TOOL_CHAT$]
Syntax: AI.TOOL_CHAT$(id, prompt$, [max_rounds=5]) -> response$
Description: Like AI.CHAT but executes tool calls automatically, looping up to max_rounds.

[AI.TOOL_CHAT]
Syntax: AI.TOOL_CHAT(id, prompt$, [max_rounds=5]) -> response$
Description: Old name of AI.TOOL_CHAT$, still accepted for one release; --lint, jdb_check and -c name AI.TOOL_CHAT$, and tools/jdb-fix.jdb rewrites it.

[AI.TOOL_LIST]
Syntax: AI.TOOL_LIST(id) -> array
Description: Returns the registered tools as [{name, params, description}, ...].

[AI.TOOL_REMOVE]
Syntax: AI.TOOL_REMOVE(id, name$)
Description: Unregisters a tool.

[AI.TOPK]
Syntax: AI.TOPK(vec, k) -> array
Description: Returns the top-k {index, score} pairs.

[ALL]
Syntax: ALL(array) or ALL(matrix, dimension)
Description: Returns TRUE if all elements in an array are true, otherwise FALSE.

[AND]
Syntax: expression AND expression
Description: Performs a logical AND operation.

[ANDALSO]
Syntax: expression ANDALSO expression
Description: Performs a short-circuiting logical AND operation.

[ANY]
Syntax: ANY(array) or ANY(matrix, dimension)
Description: Returns TRUE if any element in an array is true, otherwise FALSE.

[APPEND]
Syntax: APPEND(array, value)
Description: Appends a value or another array to an array, returning a new flat 1D array.

[AS]
Syntax: DIM variable AS type
Description: Specifies the data type of a variable in a DIM statement.

[ASC]
Syntax: ASC(char$)
Description: Returns the ASCII code of a character.

[ASIN]
Syntax: ASIN(x)
Description: Inverse sine in radians. Vectorizes element-wise over arrays.

[ASYNC]
Syntax: ASYNC FUNC function_name(args)
Description: Marks a function as asynchronous, allowing it to be used with AWAIT.

[ATAN]
Syntax: ATAN(x)
Description: Inverse tangent in radians. Vectorizes element-wise over arrays.

[ATAN2]
Syntax: ATAN2(y, x)
Description: Two-argument arctangent returning the angle in the correct quadrant.

[AUDIO.CLOSE]
Syntax: AUDIO.CLOSE
Description: Frees all loaded chunks and music and shuts down the audio subsystem.

[AUDIO.FREE]
Syntax: AUDIO.FREE(sfx_id)
Description: Releases a loaded chunk's memory.

[AUDIO.FREEMUS]
Syntax: AUDIO.FREEMUS(music_id)
Description: Releases the music memory.

[AUDIO.INIT]
Syntax: AUDIO.INIT
Description: Initialises the audio subsystem (mixer opens at 44.1 kHz, stereo). Must be called before any other AUDIO.* function.

[AUDIO.LOADMUS]
Syntax: AUDIO.LOADMUS(path$) -> music_id
Description: Loads a streaming music file (MP3, OGG, FLAC, etc.).

[AUDIO.LOADWAV]
Syntax: AUDIO.LOADWAV(path$) -> sfx_id
Description: Loads a short audio file (WAV, OGG, etc.) into a chunk for repeated fire-and-forget playback.

[AUDIO.PAUSE]
Syntax: AUDIO.PAUSE([channel])
Description: Pauses the given channel, or all channels if omitted.

[AUDIO.PAUSEMUS]
Syntax: AUDIO.PAUSEMUS
Description: Pauses the music track.

[AUDIO.PLAY]
Syntax: AUDIO.PLAY(sfx_id, [loops=0], [channel=-1]) -> channel
Description: Plays a loaded chunk; loops=0 plays once, -1 loops forever. Returns the channel index it was scheduled on.

[AUDIO.PLAYMUS]
Syntax: AUDIO.PLAYMUS(music_id, [loops=-1])
Description: Starts playing music; -1 (default) loops forever, 0 plays once.

[AUDIO.RESUME]
Syntax: AUDIO.RESUME([channel])
Description: Resumes the given channel, or all channels if omitted.

[AUDIO.RESUMEMUS]
Syntax: AUDIO.RESUMEMUS
Description: Resumes the music track.

[AUDIO.STOP]
Syntax: AUDIO.STOP([channel])
Description: Halts playback on the given channel, or all channels if omitted.

[AUDIO.STOPMUS]
Syntax: AUDIO.STOPMUS
Description: Halts the current music track.

[AUDIO.VOLUME]
Syntax: AUDIO.VOLUME(level, [channel]) -> previous
Description: Sets the channel volume (0..128), or the master SFX volume if no channel is given. Returns the previous value.

[AUDIO.VOLUMEMUS]
Syntax: AUDIO.VOLUMEMUS(level) -> previous
Description: Sets the music volume (0..128). Returns the previous value.

[AWAIT]
Syntax: AWAIT task_handle
Description: Pauses execution until an asynchronous task is complete and retrieves its result.

[BIN$]
Syntax: BIN$(n) -> string$
Description: Binary string representation of integer n.

[BINREADER$]
Syntax: BINREADER$(filename$)
Description: Reads the entire content of a binary file into a single string (raw bytes, no newline translation).

[PDF.TEXT$]
Syntax: PDF.TEXT$(filename$)
Description: Extracts the text of a PDF file using the built-in extractor (uncompressed, FlateDecode, ASCIIHex/ASCII85 streams). A font embedded as a TrueType subset shows its text as glyph indices; the extractor reads that font's ToUnicode CMap and answers the characters, so an Identity-H page comes back as text and not as glyph bytes. Encrypted or image-only PDFs yield only what is decodable.

[BINWRITER]
Syntax: BINWRITER filename$, data$
Description: Writes a raw string of bytes to a file, overwriting it.

[BAND]
Syntax: expression BAND expression
Description: Performs a bitwise AND operation on two numeric expressions.

[BOOL]
Syntax: DIM variable AS BOOL
Description: A synonym for BOOLEAN. Declares a variable that holds TRUE or FALSE.

[BOOLEAN]
Syntax: DIM variable AS BOOLEAN
Description: Declares a variable that holds TRUE or FALSE.

[CHAR]
Syntax: DIM variable AS CHAR
Description: Declares a variable to hold a single character.

[BOR]
Syntax: expression BOR expression
Description: Performs a bitwise OR operation on two numeric expressions.

[BXOR]
Syntax: expression BXOR expression
Description: Performs a bitwise XOR operation on two numeric expressions.

[BMM]
Syntax: BMM(a, b)
Description: The matrix product per batch: a is [B][M][K], b is [B][K][N], the
answer [B][M][N]. A side that is one matrix meets every batch of the other; two
matrices answer as MATMUL does.

[BNOT]
Syntax: BNOT expression
Description: Unary bitwise NOT (~). Operand is coerced to 64-bit integer; vectorises element-wise over arrays. Example: BNOT 5 = -6, (BNOT $AA) BAND $FF = $55.

[BYTEAT]
Syntax: BYTEAT(str$, index)
Description: Returns the numeric byte value (0-255) at the specified index.

[CALL]
Syntax: CALL subroutine_name
Description: Transfers control to a named SUB procedure.

[CAM.BOUNDS]
Syntax: CAM.BOUNDS(x, y, w, h)
Description: Sets a rectangular boundary that clamps the camera during SPRITE.UPDATE.

[CAM.FOLLOW]
Syntax: CAM.FOLLOW(sprite_id, [smooth])
Description: Makes the camera follow a sprite, with an optional smoothing factor for lerped tracking.

[CAM.SET]
Syntax: CAM.SET(x, y)
Description: Sets the camera position manually and disables sprite following.

[CAM.SHAKE]
Syntax: CAM.SHAKE(intensity, duration)
Description: Starts a camera shake of the given intensity for the given duration in seconds.

[CAM.X]
Syntax: CAM.X() -> number
Description: Returns the camera's current x position including shake offset.

[CAM.Y]
Syntax: CAM.Y() -> number
Description: Returns the camera's current y position including shake offset.

[CASE]
Syntax: CASE value[, value]... | CASE lo TO hi
Description: A block inside a SWITCH statement that executes if any listed value matches the SWITCH expression. Multiple values may be comma-separated, and ranges (lo TO hi, inclusive) can be mixed in: CASE 1, 5 TO 9, 12.

[CATCH]
Syntax: CATCH
Description: The block of code that executes when an error occurs within a TRY block. It reads ERR (the code), ERL (the line), ERRMSG$ (the message) and STACK$.

[CBOOL]
Syntax: CBOOL(x)
Description: Converts any value to a boolean integer: returns 0 for zero, 1 for any non-zero value.

[CD]
Syntax: CD "path"
Description: Changes the current working directory.

[CDATE]
Syntax: CDATE(date_string$ [, tz_hours])
Description: Parses a date text into a DateTime value: "YYYY-MM-DD" or "DD.MM.YYYY", optionally followed by a time "HH:MM[:SS]" after a space (or a T for the ISO form). Any other text is an error that names it. Alias for CVDATE. With tz_hours, the string is interpreted as wall-clock time in that UTC offset.

[CHAN.OPEN]
Syntax: CHAN.OPEN(capacity, [policy$]) -> handle
Description: Creates a bounded MP/MC channel. Capacity 0 = unbuffered rendezvous. policy$ is "block" (default, SEND waits for room), "latest" (keeps only the newest value) or "ring" (keeps the newest capacity values); latest and ring drop the oldest value and never block SEND. Returns an i64 handle that can be passed across ASYNC FUNC boundaries.

[CHAN.SEND]
Syntax: CHAN.SEND(handle, value)
Description: Pushes a value into the channel. Blocks while the buffer is full; a latest or ring channel drops its oldest value instead. Throws if the channel is closed.

[CHAN.RECV]
Syntax: CHAN.RECV(handle, [timeout_ms]) -> value
Description: Pops a value from the channel. Blocks while empty; with timeout_ms it waits at most that long and then returns the timeout marker (test with CHAN.IS_TIMEOUT). Returns the EOF marker once the channel is closed AND drained. Use CHAN.IS_EOF to test the result.

[CHAN.CLOSE]
Syntax: CHAN.CLOSE(handle)
Description: Marks the channel as closed and wakes every parked SEND/RECV. Idempotent. Subsequent SENDs throw; RECVs drain the remaining buffer then return EOF.

[CHAN.IS_EOF]
Syntax: CHAN.IS_EOF(value) -> boolean
Description: Returns TRUE if `value` is the channel-EOF marker (a small map with key __chan_eof__). All other values, including TRUE/FALSE/NONE, return FALSE.

[CHAN.TRY_RECV]
Syntax: CHAN.TRY_RECV(handle) -> value
Description: Takes a waiting value without blocking. Returns the timeout marker when the channel is empty, the EOF marker when it is closed and drained.

[CHAN.SELECT]
Syntax: CHAN.SELECT(handles, [timeout_ms]) -> integer
Description: Waits until one of the channels in the array `handles` has a value waiting or is closed and returns its 0-based index, the first such one in array order. Returns -1 when none is ready within timeout_ms; a missing or negative timeout waits indefinitely. It does not take the value: follow with CHAN.TRY_RECV, which can still find the channel empty if another receiver was faster.

[CHAN.IS_TIMEOUT]
Syntax: CHAN.IS_TIMEOUT(value) -> boolean
Description: Returns TRUE if `value` is the timeout marker (a small map with key __chan_timeout__) that CHAN.RECV with a timeout and CHAN.TRY_RECV return when no value came.

[CHAN.IS_CLOSED]
Syntax: CHAN.IS_CLOSED(handle) -> boolean
Description: TRUE if the channel was closed (or the handle is invalid).

[CHAN.LEN]
Syntax: CHAN.LEN(handle) -> integer
Description: Current depth of the channel buffer (queued items waiting for RECV).

[CHAN.CAP]
Syntax: CHAN.CAP(handle) -> integer
Description: Capacity the channel was opened with. 0 means unbuffered rendezvous.

[CHAN.DROPPED]
Syntax: CHAN.DROPPED(handle) -> integer
Description: How many values a latest or ring channel dropped to make room.

[CLAMP]
Syntax: CLAMP(value_or_array, min, max) -> number or array
Description: Clamps the value (or each array element) into the [min, max] range.

[COPYV]
Syntax: COPYV(dst, src) -> dst
Description: In-place bulk copy from src into dst (same-shape memcpy fast path; broadcasts cyclically on shape mismatch; a scalar src fills like FILLV). Returns dst.

[COSH]
Syntax: COSH(x)
Description: Hyperbolic cosine. Vectorizes element-wise over arrays.

[COUNT]
Syntax: COUNT(array, [value]) -> number
Description: Counts occurrences of value in array. Without the second argument, returns the total length.

[CROSS]
Syntax: CROSS(a, b) -> vector
Description: Cross product of two 3D vectors.

[CUMPROD]
Syntax: CUMPROD(array) -> array
Description: Cumulative product along the last axis.

[CUMSUM]
Syntax: CUMSUM(array) -> array
Description: Cumulative sum along the last axis.

[CVDATE]
Syntax: CVDATE(date_string$ [, tz_hours])
Description: Parses a string ("YYYY-MM-DD" or "DD.MM.YYYY", optionally with a time) into a DateTime value; any other text is an error. With tz_hours, the string is interpreted as wall-clock time in that UTC offset (e.g. CVDATE("2024-01-15 14:00:00", 2) yields the same instant as CVDATE("2024-01-15 12:00:00", 0)).

[CDBL]
Syntax: CDBL(x)
Description: Converts explicitly to a double-precision floating-point number. A numeric string is parsed (CDBL(" 2.5 ") is 2.5); other text is a type error.

[CEIL]
Syntax: CEIL(numeric_expression)
Description: Rounds a number up to the nearest integer.

[CHR]
Syntax: CHR(ascii_code)
Description: Old name of CHR$, still accepted for one release; --lint, jdb_check and -c name CHR$, and tools/jdb-fix.jdb rewrites it.

[CHR$]
Syntax: CHR$(code)
Description: Returns the character for a code. 0 to 255 give that single byte;
a code above 255 gives the Unicode character in UTF-8 (CHR$(8364) is the euro
sign).

[CHUNK]
Syntax: CHUNK(array, size)
Description: Splits array into sub-arrays of length 'size' (last chunk may be shorter). size >= 1.

[CINT]
Syntax: CINT(x)
Description: Casts a value to a 32-bit integer, truncating toward zero. Overflow wraps. A numeric string is parsed (CINT("7") is 7); other text, also an empty string, is a type error, as in VB. An array is converted element by element.

[CIRCLE]
Syntax: CIRCLE x, y, r, [fill], [r, g, b]
Description: Draws a circle on the graphics screen.

[CIRCLE_SECTOR]
Syntax: CIRCLE_SECTOR cx, cy, radius, start_angle, end_angle, [fill], [r, g, b]
Description: Draws a sector (a pie slice) of a circle. The angles are in degrees.

[CLEARWS]
Syntax: CLEARWS
Description: Clears the current workspace, including all source code, variables, and compiled code.

[CLEAR_RECUR]
Syntax: CLEAR_RECUR(task_id)
Description: Stops and removes a recurring background task started with RECUR.

[CLIPBOARD.GET$]
Syntax: CLIPBOARD.GET$()
Description: Returns the text currently in the system clipboard (Unicode text, as UTF-8).

[CLIPBOARD.SET]
Syntax: CLIPBOARD.SET text$
Description: Sets the system clipboard text (UTF-8 in, Unicode text on the clipboard).

[CLNG]
Syntax: CLNG(x)
Description: Casts a value to a 64-bit integer, truncating toward zero. A numeric string is parsed; other text is a type error. In a compiled program an ISO date string reads as its epoch seconds, as a date does in the interpreter.

[CLS]
Syntax: CLS [r, g, b]
Description: Clears the console screen; with r, g, b the console background takes that color first. While a SCREEN window is open, CLS fills the window instead, black or with the given color.

[CODEC.BASE64_DECODE$]
Syntax: CODEC.BASE64_DECODE$(string$)
Description: Decodes a Base64 encoded string.

[CODEC.BASE64_ENCODE$]
Syntax: CODEC.BASE64_ENCODE$(string$)
Description: Encodes a string into Base64 format.

[CODEC.CRC32]
Syntax: CODEC.CRC32(data$, [running_crc]) -> number
Description: Returns the CRC-32 checksum (the ZIP/PNG/gzip variant) as a number from 0 to 4294967295. Pass the previous result as running_crc to continue over the next piece: CODEC.CRC32(b$, CODEC.CRC32(a$)) equals CODEC.CRC32(a$ + b$). Binary safe.

[CODEC.CRC32$]
Syntax: CODEC.CRC32$(string$)
Description: Returns the CRC-32 checksum of a string as an 8-char hex string (the ZIP/PNG variant).

[CODEC.DEFLATE$]
Syntax: CODEC.DEFLATE$(data$, [level], [format$]) -> string$
Description: Compresses data$ with DEFLATE. level is 0 (stored) to 9 (smallest), default 6. format$ is "zlib" (default), "gzip" or "raw"; it may stand in for the level: CODEC.DEFLATE$(d$, "gzip"). The output is binary and reads back with CODEC.INFLATE$, Python's zlib and gzip, or any other inflater.

[CODEC.HMAC$]
Syntax: CODEC.HMAC$(key$, message$, [algo$])
Description: Returns the HMAC of message$ under key$ as a 64-char hex string. Only "SHA256" (the default) is supported. Binary safe.

[CODEC.INFLATE$]
Syntax: CODEC.INFLATE$(data$, [format$]) -> string$
Description: Decompresses a "raw" DEFLATE stream, a "zlib" stream or a "gzip" member. Without format$ the gzip magic bytes or a valid zlib header select the wrapper, anything else is taken as raw. The zlib Adler-32 and the gzip CRC-32 and length are checked; damaged data raises an error. Several gzip members are decoded one after another into one result; zero bytes after the last member are skipped, other trailing data raises an error.

[CODEC.PBKDF2$]
Syntax: CODEC.PBKDF2$(password$, salt$, iterations, bytes)
Description: Derives a key of bytes length (1 to 65536) from password$ and salt$ with PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256 (RFC 8018) and returns it as hex. Binary safe.

[CODEC.RANDOMBYTES$]
Syntax: CODEC.RANDOMBYTES$(n)
Description: Returns n (0 to 1048576) raw bytes from the operating system's secure random source. Not on boards.

[CODEC.SHA256$]
Syntax: CODEC.SHA256$(string$)
Description: Returns the SHA256 hash of a string (64-char hex).

[CODEC.UUID$]
Syntax: CODEC.UUID$()
Description: Generates a random Version 4 UUID from the secure random source.

[NODE.PACK$]
Syntax: NODE.PACK$(value) -> string$
Description: Encodes any value as a binary JDV1 string (magic "JDV" + version). Kinds, map key order and dates are kept; an array of one numeric kind is stored as one block of raw numbers. Up to 64 levels deep. A UDT becomes a map with "__TYPE__" (interpreter only).

[NODE.UNPACK]
Syntax: NODE.UNPACK(s$) -> value
Description: Decodes what NODE.PACK$ produced. Malformed, cut-off or trailing input raises with the byte offset.

[NODE.JOIN]
Syntax: NODE.JOIN(name$, [scope$], [key$]) -> handle
Description: Joins the Node Bus under name$ and returns the node handle; the first node is the program's default node. scope$ is "local" or "lan"; lan takes key$ or JDB_NODE_KEY. A name in use raises.

[NODE.OPEN]
Syntax: NODE.OPEN(name$, [scope$], [key$]) -> handle
Description: A further node in the same program. The default node stays as it was.

[NODE.LEAVE]
Syntax: NODE.LEAVE [node]
Description: Leaves the bus: links close, the directory entry goes, the node's channels read EOF.

[NODE.NAME$]
Syntax: NODE.NAME$([node]) -> string$
Description: The node's full address, name@host.

[NODE.PEERS]
Syntax: NODE.PEERS([pattern$]) -> array
Description: A map per other node: NAME, ADDR, HOST, PID, SCOPE, TOPICS, SINCE; lan nodes with the same key add IP, OFFSET and ERROR.

[NODE.FIND]
Syntax: NODE.FIND(addr$, [timeout_ms]) -> boolean
Description: Waits until the node exists, at most timeout_ms (default 5000).

[NODE.EVENTS]
Syntax: NODE.EVENTS([node]) -> channel
Description: A channel receiving {"event": "JOIN" or "LEAVE", "addr": name} as other nodes come and go.

[NODE.INBOX]
Syntax: NODE.INBOX([node]) -> channel
Description: The channel direct messages and calls arrive on.

[NODE.SEND]
Syntax: NODE.SEND(addr$, value, [node]) -> boolean
Description: Puts value into another node's inbox. FALSE when it does not exist or cannot be reached.

[NODE.ERROR$]
Syntax: NODE.ERROR$() -> string$
Description: Why the last NODE.SEND or NODE.FIND failed.

[NODE.CALL]
Syntax: NODE.CALL(addr$, method$, arg, [timeout_ms], [node]) -> value
Description: Asks another node and waits for the answer; the timeout marker after timeout_ms (default 5000). A failure raises.

[NODE.CALL_ASYNC]
Syntax: NODE.CALL_ASYNC(addr$, method$, arg, [node]) -> channel
Description: A call without waiting; the answer, or a failure map, arrives on the returned channel.

[NODE.IS_CALL]
Syntax: NODE.IS_CALL(value) -> boolean
Description: Whether an inbox value is a call (a map with METHOD, ARG, FROM).

[NODE.IS_FAIL]
Syntax: NODE.IS_FAIL(value) -> boolean
Description: Whether a CALL_ASYNC answer is a failure.

[NODE.REPLY]
Syntax: NODE.REPLY(call, value) -> boolean
Description: Answers a call taken from the inbox.

[NODE.FAIL]
Syntax: NODE.FAIL(call, message$) -> boolean
Description: Answers a call with an error, which NODE.CALL raises on the other side.

[NODE.SERVE]
Syntax: NODE.SERVE method$, handler@, [node]
Description: Calls of method$ go to the FUNC handler@ (it takes the call map and returns the answer), run by NODE.POLL.

[NODE.POLL]
Syntax: NODE.POLL([timeout_ms], [node]) -> number
Description: Runs the waiting served calls on this thread and returns how many ran; waits up to timeout_ms for the first.

[NODE.TIME]
Syntax: NODE.TIME() -> number
Description: Nanoseconds on the machine's steady clock, the same in every process.

[NODE.TIME_OF]
Syntax: NODE.TIME_OF(addr$, t) -> number
Description: A NODE.TIME of the machine of node addr$, put on this machine's clock.

[NODE.TRACE]
Syntax: NODE.TRACE flag
Description: Writes every Node Bus frame in or out to standard error while TRUE.

[TOPIC.OPEN]
Syntax: TOPIC.OPEN(name$, [mode$], [node]) -> channel
Description: Publishes a topic; CHAN.SEND on the channel publishes. mode$ "drop" (default) or "block" for full queue readers.

[TOPIC.SUBSCRIBE]
Syntax: TOPIC.SUBSCRIBE(pattern$, [policy$], [envelope], [node]) -> channel
Description: Receives every topic matching pattern$. policy$ "queue:N" (default queue:256), "latest" or "ring:N". envelope TRUE wraps values as DATA, FROM, TOPIC, SEQ, T.

[TOPIC.SHARE]
Syntax: TOPIC.SHARE(name$, [capacity], [node]) -> channel
Description: A work queue: each value of the topic reaches one of the channels sharing it.

[TOPIC.UNSUBSCRIBE]
Syntax: TOPIC.UNSUBSCRIBE ch
Description: Ends a subscription.

[TOPIC.RETAIN]
Syntax: TOPIC.RETAIN pub, flag
Description: The topic keeps its last value and hands it to new subscribers first.

[TOPIC.LIST]
Syntax: TOPIC.LIST([pattern$]) -> array
Description: TOPIC and ADDR of every topic on this machine that matches.

[TOPIC.STATS]
Syntax: TOPIC.STATS(ch) -> map
Description: Counters of a publisher (SENT, DROPPED, BYTES, SUBSCRIBERS) or a subscription (RECEIVED, DROPPED, BYTES, PUBLISHERS).


[COLOR]
Syntax: COLOR foreground, background
Description: Sets the text colors for the console.

[COMPILE]
Syntax: COMPILE
Description: Compiles the source code currently in memory into bytecode.

[CONTINUEDO]
Syntax: CONTINUEDO
Description: Skips the rest of the current DO loop iteration and jumps to the condition check.

[CONTINUEFOR]
Syntax: CONTINUEFOR
Description: Skips the rest of the current FOR loop iteration and jumps to the NEXT statement.

[CONTINUELOOP]
Syntax: CONTINUELOOP
Description: Synonym for CONTINUEDO. Skips the rest of the current DO loop iteration.

[CONST]
Syntax: CONST name = expression
Description: Declares a global constant. The value is set once and cannot be reassigned. Any attempt to change a CONST variable will cause a runtime error. Constants are always global, even when declared inside a function. The built-in constants PI and E are also protected this way.
Example: CONST MAX_HEALTH = 100

[CONVOLVE]
Syntax: CONVOLVE(array, kernel, [wrap_mode]) -> array
Description: Slides the kernel over a vector (1-D kernel) or a matrix (2-D kernel), centred on each element, and sums the products; the result has the shape of array. The kernel is not flipped, so strictly this is a correlation; for a symmetric kernel the two agree. wrap_mode TRUE wraps around the edges, FALSE (default) treats cells outside as absent. CONVOLVE([1,2,3,4], [1,1,1]) is [3, 6, 9, 7].

[COS]
Syntax: COS(angle_in_radians)
Description: Returns the cosine of an angle.

[COM.MISSING]
Syntax: COM.MISSING()
Description: A COM argument left out, for an optional parameter before others: VBA's FindControl(, 2578) is FindControl(COM.MISSING(), 2578) (Windows only).

[CREATEOBJECT]
Syntax: CREATEOBJECT(progID$)
Description: Creates an instance of a COM Automation object (Windows only). A call the busy server rejects is tried again for up to 30 seconds; an object assigned to a property goes by reference; a failed call's error carries the HRESULT.

[CSNG]
Syntax: CSNG(x)
Description: Roundtrips a number through 32-bit float precision, useful for forcing single-precision loss on doubles. A numeric string is parsed; other text is a type error.

[CSTR]
Syntax: CSTR(x)
Description: Old name of STR$, still accepted for one release; --lint, jdb_check and -c name STR$, and tools/jdb-fix.jdb rewrites it.

[CSVHEADER]
Syntax: CSVHEADER(filename$, [delimiter$])
Description: Returns the first CSV line as a string array of column names.

[CSVREADER]
Syntax: CSVREADER(filename$, [delimiter$], [has_header], [types])
Description: Reads a CSV file into a 2D array with per-cell type inference (int, double, string). Optional types array forces column types using the AS type names: AUTO, STRING, INTEGER, DOUBLE, DATE, BOOLEAN. A field in double quotes may hold the delimiter, line breaks and "" for a quote (RFC 4180).

[CSVWRITER]
Syntax: CSVWRITER filename$, array, [delimiter$], [header_array]
Description: Writes a 2D array to a CSV file. A text field that holds the delimiter, a quote or a line break is written in double quotes, with "" for a quote.

[CURSOR]
Syntax: CURSOR state
Description: Turns the console cursor on (1) or off (0).

[DATE]
Syntax: DIM variable AS DATE
Description: Declares a variable to hold date and time values.

[DATE$]
Syntax: DATE$
Description: Returns the current system date as a string in "YYYY-MM-DD" format.

[DATEADD]
Syntax: DATEADD(part$, number, date [, tz_hours])
Description: Adds a time interval to a date. part$ is Y, M, W, D, H, N or S, in upper or lower case; any other part$ is an error. Y, M, W and D are calendar units: they move the local calendar and keep the wall clock, so a day added across a daylight saving change is still the same time of day. Y and M are counted from the date given, the day of the month clamped to the length of the month it lands in. H, N and S add elapsed time and take a fraction. Optional tz_hours (numeric UTC offset in hours) is accepted for symmetry but has no effect on the arithmetic.

[DATEDIFF]
Syntax: DATEDIFF(part$, date1, date2 [, tz_hours])
Description: Returns the difference between two dates in a specified time unit: D (days), H (hours), N (minutes), S (seconds). The letter may be upper or lower case; any other part$ is an error. D counts days on the local clock, so two midnights are always a whole number of days apart, also across a daylight saving change; H, N and S count elapsed time, as does subtracting one date from another. To count days use DATEDIFF("D", a, b), not (b - a) / 86400. Optional tz_hours is accepted but has no effect.

[DATERANGE]
Syntax: DATERANGE(start, end [, unit$="D"] [, step=1])
Description: Array of DateTimes from start to end inclusive, stepping by step units. Calendar units D/W/M/Y advance by whole local calendar days/weeks/months/years (DST-safe); clock units H/N/S advance by fixed seconds. Negative step counts down.

[DAY]
Syntax: DAY(date) -> number
Description: Extracts the day of month (1-31) from a DateTime.

[DEBUG.PRINT]
Syntax: DEBUG.PRINT v, [v2, ...]
Description: Writes a diagnostic line to the debug console when a debugger is attached, else to stderr; never to stdout. Arguments are stringified and joined with a space; an array prints as one value.

[DEBUG.ASSERT]
Syntax: DEBUG.ASSERT cond, [message$]
Description: No-op while cond is true, otherwise raises a catchable runtime error "assertion failed: <message>". Uncaught it ends the program with exit code 1.

[DISTANCE]
Syntax: DISTANCE(point1, point2) -> number
Description: Euclidean distance between two points given as coordinate arrays.

[DOT]
Syntax: DOT(a, b) -> number
Description: Dot product of two vectors.

[ENDSWITH]
Syntax: ENDSWITH(str$, suffix$) -> bool
Description: TRUE if str$ ends with suffix$.

[EOMONTH]
Syntax: EOMONTH(date [, offset_months])
Description: Last day (midnight, local) of the month offset_months away from date (Excel-style; offset defaults to 0). Days-in-month = DAY(EOMONTH(d)), leap years handled. Vectorises over a date array.

[DATE.UTC]
Syntax: DATE.UTC(year, month, day [, hour [, minute [, second]]])
Description: Builds a DateTime from UTC components. Month is 1-12, day is 1-31. Omitted time components default to zero.

[DATE.PARTS]
Syntax: DATE.PARTS(date [, tz_hours])
Description: Breaks a DateTime into a map with keys year, month, day, hour, minute, second, weekday (0=Sunday..6=Saturday) and yday (1..366). If tz_hours is given, the wall-clock fields reflect that UTC offset (e.g. 2 for UTC+2, -5 for UTC-5, 5.5 for UTC+5:30).

[DEFAULT]
Syntax: DEFAULT
Description: The block inside a SWITCH statement that executes if no CASE matches.

[DIFF]
Syntax: DIFF(array1, array2) -> array
Description: Set difference: the elements of array1 that do not occur in array2, in array1's order and with array1's repeats kept. Elements compare by their string form, so 2 and "2" match. Not a successive difference; for that use array[1:] - array[:-1] style slicing or SCAN.

[DIM]
Syntax: DIM variable [AS type]
Description: Declares a variable and optionally sets its type.

[DIR]
Syntax: DIR [path_with_wildcard]
Description: Lists files and directories in the current or specified path.

[FILE.LIST]
Syntax: FILE.LIST(wildcard$, [extended_info_bool])
Description: Lists files matching a pattern.
If extended_info is TRUE, returns a 2D matrix: [Name, Size, Type, Date, Attr].
Otherwise, returns a 1D array of filenames.

[DIR$]
Syntax: DIR$(wildcard$, [extended_info_bool])
Description: Old name of FILE.LIST, still accepted for one release; --lint, jdb_check and -c name FILE.LIST, and tools/jdb-fix.jdb rewrites it.

[DECLARE]
Syntax: DECLARE FUNC name LIB "library" ALIAS "export" (p AS type, ...) AS rettype
        DECLARE SUB  name LIB "library" ALIAS "export" (p AS type, ...)
Description: Foreign function interface. Declares a function exported from a
shared library so it can be called from jdBasic. The library name gets the
correct platform extension auto-applied (.dll / lib.so / lib.dylib).
Param types: INTEGER, STRING, RETURN (output buffer; caller passes the desired
size in bytes; 0 = 64 KB default, max 64 MB). Up to 8 parameters.
Return types: INTEGER, STRING, ARRAY, VOID.
When RETURN slots or AS ARRAY are used, the call returns
[EXP]
Syntax: EXP(x)
Description: Natural exponential e^x. Vectorizes element-wise over arrays.

[FILLV]
Syntax: FILLV(arr, value) -> arr
Description: In-place bulk fill of every leaf element of arr with value (recurses into nested arrays). Returns the same array handle. Statement form: FILLV arr, value.

[FLATTEN]
Syntax: FLATTEN(array) -> vector
Description: Flattens a multi-dimensional array into a 1D vector.

[FUNCS]
Syntax: FUNCS
Description: Lists all user-defined FUNCs and SUBs with their parameter signatures (REPL / debugging helper).

[function_result, return_buf_1, ...]. See doc/languages.md for the full FFI
section, jdb/dll_magic.jdb for a Win32 example, jdb/sqlite_demo.jdb for a
bridge-DLL example.

[DO]
Syntax: DO ... LOOP [WHILE/UNTIL condition]
Description: Creates a loop that continues until a condition is met.

[DOUBLE]
Syntax: DIM variable AS DOUBLE
Description: Declares a variable to hold a 64-bit floating-point number.

[DRAWCOLOR]
Syntax: DRAWCOLOR r, g, b, [a]
Description: Set the current draw colour for the 2D primitives (PSET, LINE, RECT, CIRCLE, TEXT). Components are 0-255; alpha defaults to 255.

[DROP]
Syntax: DROP(N, array)
Description: Returns a new array with the first N (or last N if negative) elements removed.

[DYNAMIC]
Syntax: FUNC f(p AS DYNAMIC) ...   |   DIM x AS DYNAMIC
Description: Tagged-mixed array, opt-in for FUNC params or DIM that
receive arrays built from `[m{"a"}, m{"b"}, ...]` (any array literal whose
elements are INDEX expressions). Stores per-cell JdTags so `p[i]` reads
return the correct type at runtime instead of bit-pun'ing every element
through a double. Without it, native compile drops every string element to
0 / loses every map handle.

The native compiler emits a `[warn]` diagnostic when a mixed-element array
literal is passed to a non-DYNAMIC parameter; annotate the param to fix.
Numeric arrays (e.g. `mem[]`, lookup tables) MUST stay un-annotated; AS
DYNAMIC on a plain numeric array forces the tagged-storage path and slows
reads with no benefit. Interpreter treats DYNAMIC like ARRAY.

[DROP_WHILE]
Syntax: DROP_WHILE(predicate@, array)
Description: Drops the longest prefix where predicate(elem) is TRUE, returning the remainder.

[DUMP]
Syntax: DUMP ["GLOBAL" | "LOCAL" | "STACK" | "REACT" | module_name$]
Description: Displays debugging information about the program's state.

[EACH]
Syntax: FOR EACH variable IN collection / FOR EACH index_or_key, variable IN collection
Description: Keyword used to begin a loop over the elements of an array, the UTF-8 characters of a string, the keys of a map, or the values of a channel (interpreter only). With two variables the first takes the 0-based position (array, string) or the key (map) and the second the element or value. The loop walks what the collection held when it started.

[EDIT]
Syntax: EDIT [name]
Description: Opens the built-in source code editor on a file, or on the program in memory. Ctrl-S save, Ctrl-R save and run (any key returns on the error line), F5 run without saving, Ctrl-F find, Ctrl-G/F3 find next, Ctrl-T replace, Ctrl-L go to line, Ctrl-A select all, Ctrl-D duplicate, Ctrl-K delete line, Tab/Shift-Tab indent, Ctrl-Z/Ctrl-Y undo/redo, F1 the key list, Ctrl-Q or Esc leave.

[ELLIPSE]
Syntax: ELLIPSE cx, cy, rx, ry, [fill], [r, g, b]
Description: Draws an ellipse on the graphics screen.

[ELSE]
Syntax: IF condition THEN ... ELSE ...
Description: The block of code that executes if an IF condition is false.

[ELSEIF]
Syntax: IF condition THEN ... ELSEIF condition THEN ...
Description: A subsequent condition to test if a prior IF or ELSEIF was false.

[END]
END [exit_code]
Immediately terminates the program, from wherever it stands. The optional expression becomes the process exit status (0 when omitted).

[ENDENUM]
Syntax: ENUM ... ENDENUM
Description: Marks the end of an ENUM block.

[ENDFUNC]
Syntax: FUNC ... ENDFUNC
Description: Marks the end of a user-defined function.

[ENDIF]
Syntax: IF ... ENDIF
Description: Marks the end of an IF...THEN...ELSE block.

[ENDSUB]
Syntax: SUB ... ENDSUB
Description: Marks the end of a user-defined subroutine.

[ENDSWITCH]
Syntax: SWITCH ... ENDSWITCH
Description: Marks the end of a SWITCH...CASE block.

[ENUMERATE]
Syntax: ENUMERATE(array)
Description: Pairs each element with its 0-based index, returning [[0, a0], [1, a1], ...].

[ENDTRY]
Syntax: TRY ... ENDTRY
Description: Marks the end of a TRY...CATCH error handling block.

[ENDTYPE]
Syntax: TYPE ... ENDTYPE
Description: Marks the end of a user-defined type block.

[ENUM]
Syntax: ENUM name ... ENDENUM
Description: Begins a block that defines a set of named integer constants.

[EVAL]
Syntax: EVAL(expression_string$)
Description: Evaluates a string as an expression and returns its result at runtime.

[EXECUTE]
Syntax: EXECUTE(code_string$)
Description: Executes a string of jdBasic code at runtime.

[EXITDO]
Syntax: EXITDO
Description: Exits the current DO...LOOP immediately.

[EXITFOR]
Syntax: EXITFOR
Description: Exits the current FOR...NEXT loop immediately.

[EXITFUNC]
Syntax: EXITFUNC
Description: Exits the current user-defined function immediately. The same statement as EXITSUB.

[EXITSUB]
Syntax: EXITSUB
Description: Exits the current SUB immediately. The same statement as EXITFUNC.

[EXITSWITCH]
Syntax: EXITSWITCH
Description: Exits the innermost SWITCH...CASE block immediately, also from a loop inside a CASE body. Outside a SWITCH it is a compile error.

[EXPORT]
Syntax: EXPORT MODULE
Description: Marks the current file as a module that can be imported by other files. A FUNC or SUB in a module that assigns a name it never declared writes the importing program's global of that name; with -c or OPTION "EXPLICIT" that is refused with the name and line. Declare it with DIM (or LET, or at module level).

[EXPLICIT]
Syntax: OPTION EXPLICIT
Description: Enforces that all variables must be declared with DIM before use.

[FAC]
Syntax: FAC(number)
Description: Returns the factorial of a number.

[FALSE]
Syntax: FALSE
Description: The boolean constant representing a false value.

[FILE.EXISTS]
Syntax: FILE.EXISTS(path$) -> boolean
Description: Returns TRUE if the file or directory at path$ exists, FALSE otherwise.

[FILE.ISDIR]
Syntax: FILE.ISDIR(path$) -> boolean
Description: Returns TRUE if path$ is an existing directory, FALSE otherwise.

[FILE.SIZE]
Syntax: FILE.SIZE(path$) -> integer
Description: Returns the size of the file in bytes, or -1 if the file does not exist.

[FILE.OPEN_LINES]
Syntax: FILE.OPEN_LINES(path$) -> handle
Description: Opens a file for line-by-line reading. Returns an i64 handle. Use FILE.READLINE$ to read each line; FILE.AT_EOF to check exhaustion; FILE.CLOSE to release. Throws if the file cannot be opened. Interp-only in Phase 1.

[FILE.OPEN_TAIL]
Syntax: FILE.OPEN_TAIL(path$) -> handle
Description: Like FILE.OPEN_LINES but READLINE$ blocks polling for newly-appended data, like `tail -f`. AT_EOF is only true after FILE.CLOSE.

[FILE.READLINE$]
Syntax: FILE.READLINE$(handle) -> string
Description: Returns the next line (LF and CRLF stripped). Tail-mode: blocks until data arrives or the handle is closed. Returns "" on EOF.

[FILE.AT_EOF]
Syntax: FILE.AT_EOF(handle) -> boolean
Description: Non-tail: TRUE after the last line. Tail: only TRUE after FILE.CLOSE.

[FILE.CLOSE]
Syntax: FILE.CLOSE(handle)
Description: Idempotent. Wakes any tail reader parked in its poll loop within ~50ms.

[FILE.STREAM_LINES]
Syntax: FILE.STREAM_LINES(path$, ch [, capacity])
Description: Spawns a producer thread that reads `path$` line by line and pushes each line into the channel `ch`. Closes `ch` on EOF (or when the consumer closes it from outside). Returns `ch`. Pair with CHAN.OPEN beforehand. Interp-only.

[FILE.STREAM_TAIL]
Syntax: FILE.STREAM_TAIL(path$, ch [, capacity])
Description: Like FILE.STREAM_LINES but follows growth (`tail -f`). Stops when the consumer closes the channel.

[FILE.MOVE]
Syntax: FILE.MOVE(source$, target$, [overwrite]) -> boolean
Description: Moves or renames a file or directory; a file also to another drive, a directory only within one. A target that is an existing directory receives the file under its own name. An existing target file is replaced only with overwrite TRUE; otherwise, and on any failure, raises an error. Returns TRUE.

[FILE.COPY]
Syntax: FILE.COPY(source$, target$, [overwrite]) -> boolean
Description: Copies a file, keeping its modification time. A target that is an existing directory receives the copy under the source's name. An existing target file is replaced only with overwrite TRUE; otherwise, and on any failure, raises an error. Returns TRUE.

[FILE.STAT]
Syntax: FILE.STAT(path$) -> map
Description: Returns a map with fields "exists", "size", "is_dir", "readonly", "hidden", "mtime" (last change in local time, string YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS). For missing files, "exists" is FALSE.

[FILE.SET_MTIME]
Syntax: FILE.SET_MTIME(path$, when) -> boolean
Description: Sets the modification time FILE.STAT reads back, which is what a program needs to test a rule about the age of a file. A string is read the way CDATE reads one, so in local time ("2020-01-02 03:04:05"); a number is epoch seconds, which is what CDATE and a DATE value carry. The file has to exist - this does not create one. Raises when the file cannot be opened or the time cannot be written.

[FILTER]
Syntax: FILTER(function@, array)
Description: Creates a new 1D array containing only the elements for which the provided function returns TRUE.

[FINALLY]
Syntax: TRY ... CATCH ... FINALLY
Description: A block of code that always executes after a TRY or CATCH block, regardless of errors.

[FIND_IN_ARRAY]
Syntax: FIND_IN_ARRAY(array, value)
Description: Returns the 0-based index of the first occurrence of a value in an array, or -1 if not found.

[FLOOR]
Syntax: FLOOR(number)
Description: Rounds a number down to the nearest integer.

[FOR]
Syntax: FOR counter = start TO end [STEP value] ... NEXT
Description: Begins a loop that repeats a specific number of times.

[FORMAT$]
Syntax: FORMAT$(format_string$, arg1, ...)
Description: Formats a string using C++20-style format specifiers: {}, {0}, {:spec} with spec = [[fill]align][sign][#][0][width][.precision][type]; type is d, f, e, E, g, G, x, X, s or % (the value times 100 with a % sign); sign + or a space marks positive numbers; # puts 0x before x and X; 0 pads a number with zeros after its sign, so FORMAT$("{:04X}", 375) is 0177. Any other spec is an error. A compiled program formats at most four values per call; more is a compile error.

[FORMAT_DATE$]
Syntax: FORMAT_DATE$(date, format_string$ [, tz_hours])
Description: Formats a DateTime using C strftime specifiers (%Y, %m, %d, %H, %M, %S, ...). Without tz_hours the wall-clock is local time; with tz_hours the output reflects the chosen UTC offset (0 = UTC, 2 = UTC+2, -5 = UTC-5, 5.5 = UTC+5:30). A specifier or a year the C library rejects raises an error.

[FORMAT_DATE]
Syntax: FORMAT_DATE(date, format_string$ [, tz_hours])
Description: Old name of FORMAT_DATE$, still accepted for one release; --lint, jdb_check and -c name FORMAT_DATE$, and tools/jdb-fix.jdb rewrites it.

[FRMV$]
Syntax: FRMV$(array, [format_string$])
Description: Formats a 1D or 2D array into a display-friendly string grid.

[FUNC]
Syntax: FUNC name(parameters) ... ENDFUNC
Description: Begins the definition of a user-defined function that returns a value.

[FUNCTION]
Syntax: FUNCTION name(parameters) ... END FUNCTION
Description: VB6-style spelling of FUNC; the same keyword, closed with ENDFUNC or END FUNCTION.

[GCD]
Syntax: GCD(a, b, ...)
Description: Greatest common divisor of two or more integers.

[GETENV$]
Syntax: GETENV$(variable_name$)
Description: Gets the value of a system environment variable.

[GETX]
Syntax: GETX()
Description: Returns the current column (X) position of the console cursor.

[GETY]
Syntax: GETY()
Description: Returns the current row (Y) position of the console cursor.

[GFX.BLEND]
Syntax: GFX.BLEND mode$
Description: Sets how drawing combines with the screen: "NONE" overwrites (the default), "BLEND" mixes by the DRAWCOLOR alpha, "ADD" adds the colour for glow effects.

[GFX.CAPTURE]
Syntax: GFX.CAPTURE() -> id
Description: Captures the current renderer contents as a reusable texture and returns its image id.

[GFX.CLOSE]
Syntax: GFX.CLOSE()
Description: Closes the graphics window and releases all graphics resources.

[GFX.COLOR_TO_ALPHA]
Syntax: GFX.COLOR_TO_ALPHA(id, [r], [g], [b], [tolerance])
Description: Flood-fills from the image edges to make the connected background color transparent, auto-detecting it from the top-left pixel unless an r,g,b color is given.

[GFX.DELAY]
Syntax: GFX.DELAY(ms)
Description: Pauses execution for the given number of milliseconds.

[GFX.DRAWIMAGE]
Syntax: GFX.DRAWIMAGE(id, x, [y], [w], [h])
Description: Draws a loaded image at the given position, using the texture's native size for any omitted width or height.

[GFX.DRAWIMAGE_EX]
Syntax: GFX.DRAWIMAGE_EX(id, x, y, [w], [h], [angle], [flip_h])
Description: Draws a loaded image with optional size, rotation angle in degrees and horizontal flip.

[GFX.DRAWIMAGE_REGION]
Syntax: GFX.DRAWIMAGE_REGION(id, sx, sy, sw, sh, dx, dy, [dw], [dh])

[GFX.DRAW_CAPTURE]
Syntax: GFX.DRAW_CAPTURE(id)

[GFX.FADE]
Syntax: GFX.FADE(direction, duration, [r], [g], [b])
Description: Blocks while fading the screen out to or in from a color (default black) over the given duration in seconds; direction 0 fades out, 1 fades in.

[GFX.FREEIMAGE]
Syntax: GFX.FREEIMAGE(id)
Description: Frees a loaded image and its GPU texture.

[GFX.HSV_RGB]
Syntax: GFX.HSV_RGB(h, s, v) -> [r,g,b]
Description: Converts an HSV color (hue in degrees, saturation and value 0-1) to an [r,g,b] array of 0-255 components.

[GFX.KEYSTATE]
Syntax: GFX.KEYSTATE(key) -> boolean
Description: Returns TRUE if the given key (scancode name string or number) is currently held down.

[GFX.LOADIMAGE]

Description: Loads an image file into a GPU texture and returns its image id.

[GFX.MOUSEBUTTON]
Syntax: GFX.MOUSEBUTTON([button]) -> boolean
Description: Returns TRUE if the given mouse button (default 1) is currently pressed.

[GFX.MOUSEX]
Syntax: GFX.MOUSEX() -> number
Description: Returns the current mouse x coordinate.

[GFX.MOUSEY]
Syntax: GFX.MOUSEY() -> number
Description: Returns the current mouse y coordinate.

[GFX.PLOT_POINTS]
Syntax: GFX.PLOT_POINTS(xs, ys, [rgb])
Description: Fast-plots many pixels from parallel x and y arrays, optionally colored by a single [r,g,b], a flat per-pixel rgb stream, or the current draw color.

[GFX.PLOT_POINTS_TEX]
Syntax: GFX.PLOT_POINTS_TEX(xs, ys, rgb_lut, [bg_rgb])
Description: Scatters many colored pixels into a streaming texture (with optional background fill) and uploads it in a single GPU call.

[GFX.POLLEVENT$]
Syntax: GFX.POLLEVENT$() -> string
Description: Polls one pending window event and returns it as a string: "QUIT", "KEYDOWN:Name", "KEYUP:Name" (Name is the SDL key name, such as "A" or "Space"), "MOUSEDOWN:n", "MOUSEUP:n" (n is the button number), "MOUSEMOVE:x,y", or "NONE" when no event of these kinds is pending.

[GFX.POLLEVENT]
Syntax: GFX.POLLEVENT() -> string
Description: Old name of GFX.POLLEVENT$, still accepted for one release; --lint, jdb_check and -c name GFX.POLLEVENT$, and tools/jdb-fix.jdb rewrites it.

[GFX.SAVE_IMAGE]
Syntax: GFX.SAVE_IMAGE(id, filename$)
Description: Saves a loaded (and possibly modified) image to a PNG file, preserving transparency.

[GFX.SAVE_SCREENSHOT]

Description: Saves the current screen, or a given rectangular region, to a PNG file, or a JPEG when the name ends in .jpg or .jpeg.

[GFX.TEXTSIZE]
Syntax: GFX.TEXTSIZE(text$) -> [w,h]
Description: Returns the pixel [width, height] the given text would occupy in the current font.

[GFX.TICKS]
Syntax: GFX.TICKS() -> number
Description: Returns the number of milliseconds since the graphics system started.

[GL.ATTRIB]
Syntax: GL.ATTRIB(index, components, stride_bytes, offset_bytes)
Description: Defines and enables a float vertex attribute on the bound VAO/VBO. Type is GL_FLOAT, not normalized; stride and offset are in bytes.

[GL.BUFFER.DELETE]
Syntax: GL.BUFFER.DELETE(buffer)
Description: Deletes a buffer object (works for a VBO or EBO id).

[GL.CLEAR]
Syntax: GL.CLEAR(r, g, b, [a=255])
Description: Clears the color and depth buffers. r/g/b/a are 0..255.

[GL.CLOSE]
Syntax: GL.CLOSE()
Description: Destroys the GL window and context.

[GL.DISABLE]
Syntax: GL.DISABLE(flag$)
Description: Disables a GL capability. flag$ is one of "DEPTH_TEST", "BLEND", "CULL_FACE".

[GL.DRAW.LINES]
Syntax: GL.DRAW.LINES(first, count)
Description: Draws GL_LINES from the bound arrays (glDrawArrays).

[GL.DRAW.TRIS]
Syntax: GL.DRAW.TRIS(first, count)
Description: Draws GL_TRIANGLES from the bound arrays (glDrawArrays).

[GL.DRAW.TRIS.IDX]
Syntax: GL.DRAW.TRIS.IDX(count)
Description: Draws GL_TRIANGLES using the bound EBO (glDrawElements, GL_UNSIGNED_INT indices, offset 0).

[GL.EBO]
Syntax: GL.EBO(indices) -> int
Description: Creates an element buffer from a numeric integer TENSOR/ARRAY (uploaded as GLuint), leaves it bound; returns the buffer id.

[GL.ENABLE]
Syntax: GL.ENABLE(flag$)
Description: Enables a GL capability. flag$ is one of "DEPTH_TEST", "BLEND", "CULL_FACE".

[GL.FLIP]
Syntax: GL.FLIP()
Description: Pumps SDL events into the gfx queue and swaps the double buffer (presents the frame).

[GL.SAVE_SCREENSHOT]
Syntax: GL.SAVE_SCREENSHOT(path$)
Description: Reads the GL back buffer and saves it as a top-down PNG. Call it BEFORE GL.FLIP (the swap leaves the back buffer undefined).

[GL.SHADER]
Syntax: GL.SHADER(vertexSrc$, fragmentSrc$) -> int
Description: Compiles and links a shader program from GLSL source strings; returns the program id. Throws on a compile or link error.

[GL.SHADER.DELETE]
Syntax: GL.SHADER.DELETE(program)
Description: Deletes a shader program (glDeleteProgram).

[GL.TEX.BIND]
Syntax: GL.TEX.BIND(tex, slot)
Description: Binds a texture to GL_TEXTURE0 + slot (slot is 0..N).

[GL.TEX.DELETE]
Syntax: GL.TEX.DELETE(tex)
Description: Deletes a texture (glDeleteTextures).

[GL.TEX.LOAD]
Syntax: GL.TEX.LOAD(path$) -> int
Description: Loads a PNG/JPG via SDL_image (RGBA32, LINEAR filter, REPEAT wrap); path resolves against the script dir. Returns the texture id.

[GL.UNIFORM.F1]
Syntax: GL.UNIFORM.F1(name$, x)
Description: Sets a float uniform on the current program. No-op if the name is absent.

[GL.UNIFORM.F3]
Syntax: GL.UNIFORM.F3(name$, x, y, z)
Description: Sets a vec3 uniform on the current program. No-op if the name is absent.

[GL.UNIFORM.F4]
Syntax: GL.UNIFORM.F4(name$, x, y, z, w)
Description: Sets a vec4 uniform on the current program. No-op if the name is absent.

[GL.UNIFORM.I1]
Syntax: GL.UNIFORM.I1(name$, i)
Description: Sets an int or sampler uniform on the current program. No-op if the name is absent.

[GL.UNIFORM.MAT4]
Syntax: GL.UNIFORM.MAT4(name$, mat4)
Description: Uploads a 16-element mat4 (column-major) as a mat4 uniform. No-op if the name is absent.

[GL.USE]
Syntax: GL.USE(program)
Description: Makes a shader program current (glUseProgram). Required before setting uniforms.

[GL.VAO]
Syntax: GL.VAO() -> int
Description: Creates a vertex array object and leaves it bound; returns the VAO id.

[GL.VAO.BIND]
Syntax: GL.VAO.BIND(vao)
Description: Binds a vertex array object (glBindVertexArray).

[GL.VAO.DELETE]
Syntax: GL.VAO.DELETE(vao)
Description: Deletes a vertex array object (glDeleteVertexArrays).

[GL.VBO]
Syntax: GL.VBO(data) -> int
Description: Creates a vertex buffer from a numeric TENSOR/ARRAY (uploaded as floats, GL_STATIC_DRAW), leaves it bound; returns the buffer id.

[GL.VBO.BIND]
Syntax: GL.VBO.BIND(vbo)
Description: Binds a vertex buffer to GL_ARRAY_BUFFER (glBindBuffer).

[GL.VIEWPORT]
Syntax: GL.VIEWPORT(x, y, width, height)
Description: Sets the GL viewport rectangle (integers).

[GL.WINDOW]
Syntax: GL.WINDOW(width, height, [title$="jdBasic GL"])
Description: Creates or replaces the SDL OpenGL 3.3-core window and makes it current.

[GOTO]
Syntax: GOTO label
Description: Unconditionally jumps program execution to a specified label:.

[GRADE]
Syntax: GRADE(vector)
Description: Returns a vector of indices that would sort the input vector.

[GROUPBY]
Syntax: GROUPBY(key_fn@, array)
Description: Buckets elements into a map keyed by key_fn(elem) coerced to string. Interpreter only.

[AGG]
Syntax: AGG(keys, values, fn@)
Description: Group-and-reduce in one O(n) pass (APL key). Groups values by the matching keys entry, applies fn to each group's value-array, returns [[key, fn(group)], ...] in first-seen order with key type preserved. E.g. AGG(months, nights, LAMBDA g -> SUM(g)).

[GUI.AVAIL_HEIGHT]
Syntax: GUI.AVAIL_HEIGHT() -> number
Description: Returns the remaining available content height in the current ImGui window or child region.

[GUI.AVAIL_WIDTH]
Syntax: GUI.AVAIL_WIDTH() -> number
Description: Returns the remaining available content width in the current ImGui window or child region.

[GUI.POP_STYLE_COLOR]
Syntax: GUI.POP_STYLE_COLOR([count])
Description: Pops the given number of pushed style colors (default 1) off the ImGui style stack.

[GUI.PUSH_STYLE_COLOR]
Syntax: GUI.PUSH_STYLE_COLOR(style_idx, rgba)
Description: Pushes a style color (given as an [r,g,b,a] 0-255 array) onto the ImGui style stack for the given style index.

[GUI.TEXT_WRAPPED]
Syntax: GUI.TEXT_WRAPPED(text$)
Description: Draws word-wrapped text that wraps at the right edge of the current ImGui window or child.

[GUI.WINDOW_HEIGHT]
Syntax: GUI.WINDOW_HEIGHT() -> number
Description: Returns the full height of the current ImGui window including title and padding.

[GUI.WINDOW_WIDTH]
Syntax: GUI.WINDOW_WIDTH() -> number
Description: Returns the full width of the current ImGui window including title and padding.

[HEX$]
Syntax: HEX$(n) -> string$
Description: Hexadecimal string representation of integer n.

[HISTEDGES]
Syntax: HISTEDGES(array, [bins]) -> array
Description: The bins + 1 edges HISTOGRAM counts between: bins equal steps from the smallest to the largest value (default 10 bins). HISTEDGES([1,2,3,4], 4) is [1, 1.75, 2.5, 3.25, 4].

[HISTOGRAM]
Syntax: HISTOGRAM(array, [bins]) -> array
Description: Counts the values in bins equal-width bins (default 10) spanning the smallest to the largest value; the largest value falls in the last bin. Returns the counts only; HISTEDGES gives the matching edges.

[HOUR]
Syntax: HOUR(date) -> number
Description: Extracts the hour (0-23) from a DateTime.

[HTTP.GET_ASYNC]
Syntax: HTTP.GET_ASYNC(url$) -> task_id
Description: Starts an asynchronous HTTP GET request and returns a task id whose result is the response body.

[HTTP.GET_ASYNC$]
Syntax: HTTP.GET_ASYNC$(url$) -> task_id
Description: Old name of HTTP.GET_ASYNC, still accepted for one release; --lint, jdb_check and -c name HTTP.GET_ASYNC, and tools/jdb-fix.jdb rewrites it.

[HTTP.POST_ASYNC]
Syntax: HTTP.POST_ASYNC(url$, data$, [content_type$]) -> task_id
Description: Starts an asynchronous HTTP POST request (default content type application/json) and returns a task id whose result is the response body.

[HTTP.POST_ASYNC$]
Syntax: HTTP.POST_ASYNC$(url$, data$, [content_type$]) -> task_id
Description: Old name of HTTP.POST_ASYNC, still accepted for one release; --lint, jdb_check and -c name HTTP.POST_ASYNC, and tools/jdb-fix.jdb rewrites it.

[HTTP.PUT_ASYNC]
Syntax: HTTP.PUT_ASYNC(url$, data$, [content_type$]) -> task_id
Description: Starts an asynchronous HTTP PUT request (default content type application/json) and returns a task id whose result is the response body.

[HTTP.PUT_ASYNC$]
Syntax: HTTP.PUT_ASYNC$(url$, data$, [content_type$]) -> task_id
Description: Old name of HTTP.PUT_ASYNC, still accepted for one release; --lint, jdb_check and -c name HTTP.PUT_ASYNC, and tools/jdb-fix.jdb rewrites it.

[HTTP.SERVER.WAIT]
Syntax: HTTP.SERVER.WAIT()
Description: Blocks until the running HTTP server stops, polling every 150 ms. Handlers run one at a time, never beside the program: while it waits here or in SLEEP, AWAIT, CHAN.RECV, INPUT, OS.EXEC or an HTTP client call, or between two instructions of the interpreter.

[IIF]
Syntax: IIF(condition, value_if_true, value_if_false) -> value or array
Description: Vectorized ternary: selects element-wise from the true/false values according to the condition.

[INDEXOF]
Syntax: INDEXOF(array, value) -> number
Description: Returns the first 0-based index of value in array, or -1 if not found (same as FIND_IN_ARRAY).

[INSERT$]
Syntax: INSERT$(target, text$, position) -> string or array
Description: Inserts text$ into target at the given 0-based position. Vectorizes when target/text/position are arrays.

[ISARR]
Syntax: ISARR(v) -> bool
Description: TRUE if v is an array.

[ISBOOL]
Syntax: ISBOOL(v) -> bool
Description: TRUE if v is a boolean.

[ISMAP]
Syntax: ISMAP(v) -> bool
Description: TRUE if v is a map/object.

[ISNONE]
Syntax: ISNONE(v) -> bool
Description: TRUE if v is the NONE value.

[ISNULL]
Syntax: ISNULL(v) -> bool
Description: TRUE if v is the NONE value (alias of ISNONE).

[ISNUM]
Syntax: ISNUM(v) -> bool
Description: TRUE if v is a number (integer or double).

[ISSTR]
Syntax: ISSTR(v) -> bool
Description: TRUE if v is a string.

[JDB.ALIASES]
Syntax: JDB.ALIASES() -> map
Description: The old names that still resolve, each key an old name and its value the name that replaced it. A program that uses an old name runs; --lint, jdb_check and -c warn about it, and tools/jdb-fix.jdb rewrites it.

[JDB.CHECK$]
Syntax: JDB.CHECK$(code$) -> string
Description: Lexes and parses a code snippet without executing it, returning an empty string if it is valid, "ok" followed by one warning per line if it is valid but uses old names, or the error message otherwise.

[JDB.GLOBAL_GET]
Syntax: JDB.GLOBAL_GET(name$) -> value
Description: Returns the value of a global variable by case-insensitive name, or NONE if the name is unknown.

[JDB.GLOBAL_SET]
Syntax: JDB.GLOBAL_SET(name$, value)
Description: Writes a value to a global variable by case-insensitive name, allocating the slot if it is new.

[LINSPACE]
Syntax: LINSPACE(start, stop, n) -> vector
Description: Returns n evenly spaced samples over [start, stop] inclusive.

[MEAN]
Syntax: MEAN(array) or MEAN(matrix, dimension) -> number or array
Description: Arithmetic mean (average) of an array.

[MEDIAN]
Syntax: MEDIAN(array) or MEDIAN(matrix, dimension) -> number or array
Description: Median (central value) of an array.

[MINUTE]
Syntax: MINUTE(date) -> number
Description: Extracts the minute (0-59) from a DateTime.

[MONTH]
Syntax: MONTH(date) -> number
Description: Extracts the month (1-12) from a DateTime.

[OCT$]
Syntax: OCT$(n) -> string$
Description: Octal string representation of integer n.

[ONES]
Syntax: ONES(shape_vector) -> array
Description: Creates an array of the given shape filled with ones.

[OS.GETOS$]
Syntax: OS.GETOS$() -> string
Description: Returns the host operating system name: "WINDOWS", "MACOS" or "LINUX".

[PARTICLE.CLEAR]
Syntax: PARTICLE.CLEAR()
Description: Removes all active particles.

[PARTICLE.COUNT]
Syntax: PARTICLE.COUNT() -> number
Description: Returns the number of currently active particles.

[PARTICLE.DRAW]
Syntax: PARTICLE.DRAW([cam_x], [cam_y])
Description: Draws all active particles with life-based fade, using the global camera offset when none is given.

[PARTICLE.EMIT]
Syntax: PARTICLE.EMIT(x, y, count, r, g, b, [speed], [life], [gravity], [size])
Description: Emits a burst of count particles at a position with the given color and optional speed, lifetime, gravity and size.

[POP]
Syntax: POP(array) -> value
Description: Removes and returns the last element of an array (stack pop).

[PUSH]
Syntax: PUSH(array, value)
Description: Appends value to the end of an array (stack push).

[RANGE]
Syntax: RANGE(start, stop, [step]) -> vector
Description: Python-style half-open range: [start, start+step, ..., stop). step defaults to 1.

[REACT_BIND]
Syntax: REACT_BIND(var_name$, formula$)
Description: Binds a global variable to a formula string at runtime, equivalent to writing var -> formula in source.

[REGEX_MATCH]
Syntax: REGEX_MATCH(pattern$, text$) -> boolean or array
Description: Back-compatible form of REGEX.MATCH. Returns TRUE/FALSE, or the captured groups if the pattern has any.

[REGEX_REPLACE$]
Syntax: REGEX_REPLACE$(text$, pattern$, replacement$) -> string$
Description: The older form of REGEX.REPLACE$ with the text first and the pattern second. Replaces all matches; $1, $2 backreferences are allowed.

[RELEASEALL]
Syntax: RELEASEALL
Description: Releases every COM object currently held by the runtime.

[RELEASEOBJECT]
Syntax: RELEASEOBJECT(com_obj)
Description: Explicitly releases a single COM object reference.

[SECOND]
Syntax: SECOND(date) -> number
Description: Extracts the second (0-59) from a DateTime.

[SGN]
Syntax: SGN(x)
Description: Returns -1, 0, or +1 depending on the sign of x.

[SHUFFLE]
Syntax: SHUFFLE(array) -> array
Description: Returns a new array with the elements randomly shuffled.

[SIGN]
Syntax: SIGN(x)
Description: Returns -1, 0, or +1 depending on the sign of x.

[SINH]
Syntax: SINH(x)
Description: Hyperbolic sine. Vectorizes element-wise over arrays.

[SORT]
Syntax: SORT(array [, descending]) -> array
Description: Returns a new 1D array sorted ascending, or descending when the flag is TRUE. Numbers compare numerically, strings by character code (upper case before lower case).

[SOUND.DEBUG]
Syntax: SOUND.DEBUG() -> object
Description: Returns a diagnostic object reporting sound init state, active voice count and other audio engine internals.

[SOUND.DELAYSEND]
Syntax: SOUND.DELAYSEND(track, amount)
Description: Sets how much of a track's signal is sent to the global delay bus.

[SOUND.GET_BUS_WAVE]
Syntax: SOUND.GET_BUS_WAVE(bus) -> array
Description: Returns the waveform sample array of an effect bus (0 = reverb bus, otherwise delay bus).

[SOUND.NOTE]
Syntax: SOUND.NOTE(pattern$, [loop], [debug])
Description: Parses and schedules a note pattern string into the sequencer, optionally looping it and printing debug info about the parsed tracks.

[SOUND.REVERBSEND]
Syntax: SOUND.REVERBSEND(track, amount)
Description: Sets how much of a track's signal is sent to the global reverb bus.

[SOUND.SIDECHAIN]
Syntax: SOUND.SIDECHAIN(target_track, source_track, amount)
Description: Sidechains a target track's level to a source track by the given amount.

[SOUND.STATS$]
Syntax: SOUND.STATS$() -> string
Description: Returns and resets a debug string of voice trigger and allocation-failure counters.

[SOUND.STATS]
Syntax: SOUND.STATS() -> string
Description: Old name of SOUND.STATS$, still accepted for one release; --lint, jdb_check and -c name SOUND.STATS$, and tools/jdb-fix.jdb rewrites it.

[SOUND.OSC2]
Syntax: SOUND.OSC2 track, wave$, [semitones], [mix], [cents]
Description: A second oscillator in every voice: wave SINE, SAW, SQUARE, TRIANGLE, NOISE,
or OFF to remove it. semitones (default 0) and cents from the first, mix 0.0-1.0 (default 0.5).
Example: SOUND.OSC2 6, "SQUARE", -12, 0.5

[SOUND.UNISON]
Syntax: SOUND.UNISON(track, voices, detune, spread)
Description: Configures unison on a track with the given voice count (clamped 1-16), detune and stereo spread.

[SPACE$]
Syntax: SPACE$(n) -> string$
Description: Returns a string of n spaces, handy for padding.

[SPRITE.ALPHA]
Syntax: SPRITE.ALPHA(id, alpha)
Description: Sets the per-sprite alpha transparency (0-255, clamped) of the given sprite instance.

[SPRITE.ANIM]
Syntax: SPRITE.ANIM(id, name$, frames_array, fps, [loop])
Description: Defines a named animation clip from an array of frame indices played at fps. loop defaults to TRUE. Start it with SPRITE.PLAY.

[SPRITE.COLLISIONS]
Syntax: SPRITE.COLLISIONS(group1$, group2$) -> array
Description: Returns all colliding pairs between two groups as [[id_a, id_b], ...] using an axis-aligned bounding-box test.

[SPRITE.COLLISION_FIRST]
Syntax: SPRITE.COLLISION_FIRST(id, group$) -> number
Description: Returns the id of the first visible sprite in group$ whose bounding box overlaps sprite id, or -1 if none.

[SPRITE.CREATE]
Syntax: SPRITE.CREATE(w, h) -> sprite_id
Description: Allocates a new transparent sprite texture of size w x h (1..4096) and returns its sprite id. Fill with SPRITE.SETPIXEL or SPRITE.SETBUFFER, persist via SPRITE.SAVE.

[SPRITE.DRAW]
Syntax: SPRITE.DRAW(id)
Description: Draws the given sprite instance to the screen if it is visible.

[SPRITE.FLIP]
Syntax: SPRITE.FLIP(id, flip_h, [flip_v])
Description: Sets the horizontal (and optional vertical) mirror state of a sprite.

[SPRITE.FRAME]
Syntax: SPRITE.FRAME(id, frame_index)
Description: Manually sets a sprite to a fixed frame, stopping any playing animation.

[SPRITE.GET_VX]
Syntax: SPRITE.GET_VX(id) -> number
Description: Returns the sprite's current horizontal velocity (pixels per second).

[SPRITE.GET_VY]
Syntax: SPRITE.GET_VY(id) -> number
Description: Returns the sprite's current vertical velocity (pixels per second).

[SPRITE.GRAVITY]
Syntax: SPRITE.GRAVITY(id, gravity)
Description: Sets the per-second vertical gravity acceleration applied to a sprite during SPRITE.UPDATE.

[SPRITE.GROUP]
Syntax: SPRITE.GROUP(id, group_name$)
Description: Assigns a sprite to a named collision group, used by SPRITE.COLLISIONS and SPRITE.COLLISION_FIRST.

[SPRITE.HEIGHT]
Syntax: SPRITE.HEIGHT(id) -> number
Description: Returns the scaled pixel height of the sprite instance.

[SPRITE.LAND]
Syntax: SPRITE.LAND(id, ground_y)
Description: Snaps a sprite to rest on a ground y-line, zeroing its vertical velocity and flagging it on-ground.

[SPRITE.ON_GROUND]
Syntax: SPRITE.ON_GROUND(id) -> boolean
Description: Returns TRUE if the sprite was flagged as resting on the ground by SPRITE.LAND.

[SPRITE.PLAY]
Syntax: SPRITE.PLAY(id, name$)
Description: Starts playing the named animation clip (defined via SPRITE.ANIM) on a sprite. Raises an error if the clip name is unknown.

[SPRITE.PLAYING]
Syntax: SPRITE.PLAYING(id) -> boolean
Description: Returns TRUE if the sprite's animation is currently playing.

[SPRITE.POS]
Syntax: SPRITE.POS(id, x, y)
Description: Sets the absolute position of the given sprite instance.

[SPRITE.ROTATE]
Syntax: SPRITE.ROTATE(id, angle)
Description: Sets the rotation angle (degrees) of the given sprite instance.

[SPRITE.SCALE]
Syntax: SPRITE.SCALE(id, scale_x, [scale_y])
Description: Sets the horizontal and vertical scale of a sprite; scale_y defaults to scale_x when omitted.

[SPRITE.SET_ORIGIN]
Syntax: SPRITE.SET_ORIGIN(id, origin_x, origin_y)
Description: Sets the rotation/scale origin point of the given sprite instance.

[SPRITE.STOP]
Syntax: SPRITE.STOP(id)
Description: Stops the sprite's current animation playback.

[SPRITE.VELOCITY]
Syntax: SPRITE.VELOCITY(id, vx, vy)
Description: Sets a sprite's velocity in pixels per second. SPRITE.UPDATE then advances its position; read back with SPRITE.GET_VX / SPRITE.GET_VY.

[SPRITE.VISIBLE]
Syntax: SPRITE.VISIBLE(id, visible)
Description: Sets whether the given sprite instance is drawn.

[SPRITE.WIDTH]
Syntax: SPRITE.WIDTH(id) -> number
Description: Returns the scaled pixel width of the sprite instance.

[SPRITE.ZORDER]
Syntax: SPRITE.ZORDER(id, z)
Description: Sets the draw z-order of the sprite, controlling its layering in SPRITE.DRAW_ALL.

[STARTSWITH]

Syntax: GUI.ITEM_DEACTIVATED_AFTER_EDIT()
Description: Returns TRUE if the last item became inactive after an edit (e.g., user pressed Enter/Esc or focus moved away). Useful to end in-cell editing.


[GUI.SET_CURSOR_SCREEN_POS]
Syntax: GUI.SET_CURSOR_SCREEN_POS(x, y)
Description: Sets the cursor position in screen coordinates for the next widget (useful for overlay editors).


[GUI.SET_NEXT_ITEM_WIDTH]
Syntax: GUI.SET_NEXT_ITEM_WIDTH(width)
Description: Sets the width of the next input widget.


[GUI.SET_KEYBOARD_FOCUS]
Syntax: GUI.SET_KEYBOARD_FOCUS
Description: Gives keyboard focus to the next input widget that is created.


[GUI.BEGIN_TABLE]
Syntax: GUI.BEGIN_TABLE(id$, columns, [flags], [outer_w], [outer_h])
Description: Starts an ImGui table. Returns TRUE if the table is visible and should be populated.


[GUI.END_TABLE]
Syntax: GUI.END_TABLE
Description: Ends a table started with GUI.BEGIN_TABLE.


[GUI.TABLE_SETUP_COLUMN]
Syntax: GUI.TABLE_SETUP_COLUMN(label$, [flags], [init_width_or_weight])
Description: Declares a table column. Call once per column before GUI.TABLE_HEADERS_ROW.


[GUI.TABLE_HEADERS_ROW]
Syntax: GUI.TABLE_HEADERS_ROW
Description: Submits a header row based on the columns configured with GUI.TABLE_SETUP_COLUMN.


[GUI.TABLE_NEXT_ROW]
Syntax: GUI.TABLE_NEXT_ROW([row_flags], [min_row_height])
Description: Advances to the next row in the current table.


[GUI.TABLE_SET_COLUMN_INDEX]
Syntax: GUI.TABLE_SET_COLUMN_INDEX(index)
Description: Switches the current table column. Returns TRUE if the column is visible.


[GUI.TABLE_NEXT_COLUMN]
Syntax: GUI.TABLE_NEXT_COLUMN()
Description: Switches to the next column in the current table. Returns TRUE if the column is visible.


[GUI.LISTBOX]
Syntax: GUI.LISTBOX(label$, current_index, items_array, [height])
Description: Displays a selectable list box. Returns the new selected index.

[GUI.MENU_ITEM]

Description: Creates a menu item. Returns TRUE if activated.

[GUI.OPEN_POPUP]
Syntax: GUI.OPEN_POPUP(str_id$)

[GUI.PLOT_HISTOGRAM]

[GUI.PLOT_LINES]

Description: Draws a line chart.

[GUI.POP_ID]
