Description: Pops the last ID pushed to the stack.

[GUI.PROGRESS]
Syntax: GUI.PROGRESS(fraction, [overlay_text$])
Description: Displays a progress bar (0.0 to 1.0).

[GUI.IMAGE]
Syntax: GUI.IMAGE(sprite_id, [width, height])
Description: Draws a SPRITE.LOAD'd texture (e.g. a flag/logo PNG) inside the current ImGui window. Defaults to native pixel size; pass width/height to scale. Returns FALSE for an unknown sprite id. Scrolls/clips with the ImGui layout, unlike SPRITE.DRAW.

[GUI.PUSH_ID]
Syntax: GUI.PUSH_ID(id)
Description: Pushes an integer or string ID to the stack to avoid collisions.

[GUI.RADIO]
Syntax: GUI.RADIO(label$, current_value, button_value)
Description: Displays a radio button. Returns button_value if selected, else current_value.

[GUI.SAME_LINE]
Syntax: GUI.SAME_LINE
Description: Places the next widget on the same line as the previous one.

[GUI.SELECTABLE]
Syntax: GUI.SELECTABLE(label$, [selected], [flags], [w], [h])
Description: Displays a selectable item (row). Returns TRUE if clicked.

[GUI.SEPARATOR]
Syntax: GUI.SEPARATOR
Description: Draws a horizontal line separator.

[GUI.SEPARATOR_TEXT]
Syntax: GUI.SEPARATOR_TEXT(text$)
Description: Draws a separator with centered text.

[GUI.SHOW_FONT_ATLAS]
Syntax: GUI.SHOW_FONT_ATLAS
Description: Opens the ImGui font visualizer for debugging.

[GUI.SLIDER]
Syntax: GUI.SLIDER(label$, value, min, max)
Description: Displays a slider. Returns the new value.

[GUI.TEXT]
Syntax: GUI.TEXT(text$)
Description: Displays text in the UI.

[GUI.THEME]
Syntax: GUI.THEME(theme_name$)
Description: Sets the UI theme ("DARK", "LIGHT", "CLASSIC").

[GUI.TOOLTIP]
Syntax: GUI.TOOLTIP(text$)
Description: Sets a tooltip for the previous item.

[GUI.TREE_NODE]
Syntax: GUI.TREE_NODE(label$)
Description: Displays a tree node. Returns TRUE if open (must call TREE_POP).

[GUI.TREE_POP]
Syntax: GUI.TREE_POP
Description: Ends a tree node.

[HELP]
Syntax: HELP [topic$]
Description: Displays help information. With no topic, lists all commands.

[HELP$]
Syntax: HELP$()
Description: Returns a 1D array of strings containing all available help topics.

[HTTP.CLEARCOOKIES]
Syntax: HTTP.CLEARCOOKIES
Description: Removes all stored client-side cookies.

[HTTP.CLEARHEADERS]
Syntax: HTTP.CLEARHEADERS
Description: Clears all custom headers set for subsequent HTTP requests.

[HTTP.CLEARPARAMS]
Syntax: HTTP.CLEARPARAMS
Description: Clears all URL query parameters set via HTTP.SETPARAM.

[HTTP.DELETE$]
Syntax: HTTP.DELETE$(url$)
Description: Performs an HTTP DELETE request. Status is available via HTTP.STATUSCODE().

[HTTP.FOLLOWREDIRECTS]
Syntax: HTTP.FOLLOWREDIRECTS(flag)
Description: Enables (default) or disables automatic redirect-following for subsequent HTTP client calls.

[HTTP.GET$]
Syntax: HTTP.GET$(url$)
Description: Performs an HTTP GET request and returns the response body as a string.

[HTTP.GETCOOKIE$]
Syntax: HTTP.GETCOOKIE$(name$)
Description: Returns the stored client-side cookie value for 'name$', or empty string if unknown.

[HTTP.POST$]
Syntax: HTTP.POST$(url$, data$, contentType$)
Description: Performs an HTTP POST request.

[HTTP.PUT$]
Syntax: HTTP.PUT$(url$, data$, contentType$)
Description: Performs an HTTP PUT request.

[HTTP.REQUEST]
Syntax: HTTP.REQUEST(method$, url$ [, body$ [, content_type$]])
Description: Generic HTTP call. Returns a map with 'status', 'body', 'headers'. Does NOT throw on HTTP-level 4xx/5xx; only transport failures throw. method$ is one of GET, DELETE, HEAD, POST, PUT, PATCH.

[HTTP.SERVER.ON_GET]
Syntax: HTTP.SERVER.ON_GET(path$, handler@)
Description: Registers a function to handle incoming HTTP GET requests for the built-in server.

[HTTP.SERVER.ON_POST]
Syntax: HTTP.SERVER.ON_POST(path$, handler@)
Description: Registers a function to handle incoming HTTP POST requests for the built-in server.

[HTTP.SERVER.ON_NOTFOUND]
Syntax: HTTP.SERVER.ON_NOTFOUND(handler@)
Description: Registers a function to render unmatched routes (HTTP 404). It receives the request map and returns HTML or a rich-response map. Fires only for 404. Call before HTTP.SERVER.START.

[HTTP.SERVER.START]
Syntax: HTTP.SERVER.START(port [, host$])
Description: Starts the built-in non-blocking HTTP server on a specified port. host$ defaults to "127.0.0.1" (loopback only); pass "0.0.0.0" to expose the server to the LAN.

[HTTP.SERVER.STOP]
Syntax: HTTP.SERVER.STOP
Description: Stops the built-in HTTP server.

[HTTP.SERVER.LOG]
Syntax: HTTP.SERVER.LOG(on)
Description: Turns a one-line console log of each request (method, path, the start of the body) on with TRUE or off with FALSE. Off by default, since a body can hold a password from a form; JDBASIC_HTTP_LOG=1 in the environment turns it on from the start.

[HTTP.SETCOOKIE]
Syntax: HTTP.SETCOOKIE(name$, value$)
Description: Stores a client-side cookie that will be sent on subsequent requests.

[HTTP.SETHEADER]
Syntax: HTTP.SETHEADER(name$, value$)
Description: Sets a custom HTTP header for subsequent requests.

[HTTP.SETPARAM]
Syntax: HTTP.SETPARAM(name$, value$)
Description: Sets (or updates) a URL query parameter applied to all subsequent client calls. Values are url-encoded.

[HTTP.SETTIMEOUT]
Syntax: HTTP.SETTIMEOUT(seconds)
Description: Sets the connection/read/write timeout in seconds for subsequent HTTP client calls. Default is 10.

[HTTP.STATUSCODE]
Syntax: HTTP.STATUSCODE()
Description: Returns the HTTP status code from the last request.

[IF]
Syntax: IF condition THEN ...
Description: Begins a block of code that executes conditionally.

[IMPORT]
Syntax: IMPORT module_name [, module_name ...]
Description: Loads one or more jdBasic module files, in the order given. Each name is looked for as NAME.jdb and name.jdb in the script's own directory, a modules/ subdirectory of it, the working directory, every directory in JDBASIC_PATH, <home>/.jdbasic/lib and finally <jdBasic.exe>/lib; the first hit wins, with no walk-up into parent directories. A file of the module's name beside the script therefore replaces a library of that name, and nothing the library defines exists any more - the importer writes one warning line to stderr naming both files, interpreted and under -c alike. Imports are resolved while the program is parsed, so for -c they are baked into the executable.

[IN]
Syntax: FOR EACH ... IN collection
Description: Keyword used in a FOR EACH loop to specify the collection to iterate over.

[IN_OPERATOR]
Syntax: value IN collection
Description: An operator that returns TRUE if a value exists within an array or as a key in a map.

[INPUT_HIDDEN$]
Syntax: INPUT_HIDDEN$([prompt$])
Description: Reads one line the terminal does not show, for a password or a token. The optional prompt is printed first. The console still does the line editing, so backspace and a pasted secret work as they do for INPUT; only the echo is off, and nothing is printed in its place - not even stars, which would tell a watcher the length. Returns what was typed, without the newline, as UTF-8. When standard input is not a terminal (a pipe, a file, a test harness) there is nothing to hide and the line is read the way INPUT reads it; end of input answers an empty string.

[INKEY$]
Syntax: INKEY$()
Description: Non-blocking check for a key press. Returns the key or an empty string. From the console it answers one character, which is more than one byte for anything past ASCII, and a function or arrow key arrives as two calls: CHR$(0) or CHR$(224) first, then the scan code. While a SCREEN window is open it reads the window's keys: the SDL key name ("A" for the A key, "Space", "Left"), CHR$(27) for Escape or for closing the window, CHR$(13) for Enter, CHR$(8) for Backspace, CHR$(9) for Tab. Only the last key since the previous call is kept.

[INPUT]
Syntax: INPUT [prompt$] [,|;] variable
Description: Pauses execution and waits for the user to enter data from the console.

[INSTR]
Syntax: INSTR([start_pos, ]haystack$, needle$)
Description: Returns the 0-based starting position of a substring within a string, or -1 when it is not there. The start position comes first.

[INSTR$]
Syntax: INSTR$([start_pos, ]haystack$, needle$)
Description: Old name of INSTR, still accepted for one release; --lint, jdb_check and -c name INSTR, and tools/jdb-fix.jdb rewrites it.

[INT]
Syntax: INT(number)
Description: Truncates a number to its integer part (classic floor behavior).

[INT16]
Syntax: DIM variable AS INT16
Description: Declares a variable to hold a 16-bit signed integer. SHORT is the classic-BASIC alias.

[INT32]
Syntax: DIM variable AS INT32
Description: Declares a variable to hold a 32-bit signed integer.

[INT64]
Syntax: DIM variable AS INT64
Description: Declares a variable to hold a 64-bit signed integer. INTEGER and LONG are the classic-BASIC aliases.

[INTEGER]
Syntax: DIM variable AS INTEGER
Description: Declares a variable to hold a 64-bit signed integer.

[FLOAT16]
Syntax: DIM variable AS FLOAT16
Description: Declares a variable to hold a 16-bit half-precision floating-point number.

[FLOAT32]
Syntax: DIM variable AS FLOAT32
Description: Declares a variable to hold a 32-bit floating-point number. SINGLE is the classic-BASIC alias.

[FLOAT64]
Syntax: DIM variable AS FLOAT64
Description: Declares a variable to hold a 64-bit floating-point number. DOUBLE is the classic-BASIC alias.

[LONG]
Syntax: DIM variable AS LONG
Description: Declares a variable to hold a 64-bit signed integer. Classic-BASIC alias of INT64.

[SHORT]
Syntax: DIM variable AS SHORT
Description: Declares a variable to hold a 16-bit signed integer. Classic-BASIC alias of INT16.

[SINGLE]
Syntax: DIM variable AS SINGLE
Description: Declares a variable to hold a 32-bit floating-point number. Classic-BASIC alias of FLOAT32.

[INTEGRATE]
Syntax: INTEGRATE(function@, limits_array, rule_order)
Description: Numerically integrates a function over a given domain.

[INVERT]
Syntax: INVERT(matrix)
Description: Computes the inverse of a square matrix.

[DET]
Syntax: DET(matrix)
Description: Determinant of a square matrix (Eigen).

[SVD]
Syntax: SVD(matrix)
Description: Singular Value Decomposition. Returns a map { "u", "s", "v" }: s is the singular-value vector, u and v the thin factor matrices (Eigen).

[QR]
Syntax: QR(matrix)
Description: Householder QR decomposition. Returns a map { "q", "r" } (Eigen).

[EIG]
Syntax: EIG(matrix)
Description: Eigen-decomposition of a square matrix. Returns { "eigenvalues", "eigenvectors" } as complex [real,imag] arrays (Eigen).

[FFT]
Syntax: FFT(signal)
Description: Fast Fourier transform of a 1-D array (reals or [real,imag] pairs). Returns an [N][2] array of complex [real,imag] pairs. Any length N (Eigen/kissfft).

[IFFT]
Syntax: IFFT(spectrum)
Description: Inverse FFT. Input/output are [N][2] complex arrays; round-trips FFT.

[IOTA]
Syntax: IOTA(N, [base=1], [step=1])
Description: Generates a 1D array of N numbers.

[JOIN]
Syntax: JOIN(array, [delimiter$])
Description: Concatenates the elements of an array into one string, with delimiter$ between them (none when omitted). Numbers are written as PRINT writes them. The inverse of SPLIT.

[JSON]
Syntax: DIM variable AS JSON
Description: Declares a variable to hold a parsed JSON object.

[JSON.PARSE]
Syntax: JSON.PARSE(json_string$)
Description: Parses a JSON string into a map or an array. The same function as JSON.PARSE$ - the plain name is the one to use, since the $ elsewhere in the language marks a function that answers a string and this one answers a container. Declaring the target AS MAP works only with the plain name; `DIM m AS MAP = JSON.PARSE$(..)` is a type error under -c.

[JSON.PARSE$]
Syntax: JSON.PARSE$(json_string$)
Description: Old name of JSON.PARSE, still accepted for one release; --lint, jdb_check and -c name JSON.PARSE, and tools/jdb-fix.jdb rewrites it.

[JSON.STRINGIFY$]
Syntax: JSON.STRINGIFY$(map_or_array)
Description: Converts a Map or Array into a JSON string representation.

[JOY.AXIS]
Syntax: JOY.AXIS(id, axis_index)
Description: Returns the axis position value between -1.0 and 1.0.

[JOY.BUTTON]
Syntax: JOY.BUTTON(id, button_index)
Description: Returns TRUE if the specified button is pressed.

[JOY.COUNT]
Syntax: JOY.COUNT()
Description: Returns the number of connected joysticks.

[JOY.HAT]
Syntax: JOY.HAT(id, hat_index)
Description: Returns the hat (D-Pad) state as a bitmask (1=Up, 2=Right, 4=Down, 8=Left).

[JOY.NAME$]
Syntax: JOY.NAME$(id)
Description: Returns the name of the joystick at index id.

[JOY.RAW$]
Syntax: JOY.RAW$(id)
Description: Returns the pad's last raw HID report as hex. Boards only, for
             working out an unknown pad's layout.

[DVI.LATE$]
Syntax: DVI.LATE$()
Description: Reports frames that ran long or short against the 16.7 ms the
             signal expects, with the worst of each. Fruit Jam only.

[DVI.CACHE$]
Syntax: DVI.CACHE$()
Description: Reports the scanline cache that feeds the display from PSRAM.
             Fruit Jam only.

[USB.TIME$]
Syntax: USB.TIME$()
Description: Reports how much time the USB host stack takes: calls, calls
             over 4 ms, worst and mean. Boards only.

[USB.DIAG$]
Syntax: USB.DIAG$()
Description: Lists the devices the USB host has enumerated with their
             vendor and product ids. Boards only.

[KILL]
Syntax: KILL "filename"
Description: Deletes a file from the disk.

[LAMBDA]
Syntax: LAMBDA params -> expression
Description: Defines a small, anonymous function.

[LCASE$]
Syntax: LCASE$(string$)
Description: Converts a string to lowercase.

[LCM]
Syntax: LCM(a, b, ...)
Description: Least common multiple of two or more integers.

[LOWER$]
Syntax: LOWER$(string$)
Description: Converts a string to lowercase. VB6-style alias of LCASE$.

[LTRIM$]
Syntax: LTRIM$(string$)
Description: Removes leading whitespace from a string. Companion to RTRIM$ and TRIM$.

[RTRIM$]
Syntax: RTRIM$(string$)
Description: Removes trailing whitespace from a string. Companion to LTRIM$ and TRIM$.

[UPPER$]
Syntax: UPPER$(string$)
Description: Converts a string to uppercase. VB6-style alias of UCASE$.

[LEFT$]
Syntax: LEFT$(string$, length)
Description: Returns the specified number of characters from the beginning of a string.

[LEN]
Syntax: LEN(expression)
Description: Returns a scalar length. For strings: byte count. For maps: number
of keys. For arrays: element count of the outermost dimension. Use LENV for the
full shape of a nested array.

[LENV]
Syntax: LENV(expression)
Description: Returns a shape vector [dim0, dim1, ...] describing the full
extent of a (possibly nested) array. For 1D arrays returns [n]; for strings
returns [byte_count].

[LERP]
Syntax: LERP(start, end, alpha)
Description: Performs linear interpolation between two values or arrays.

[LINT]
Syntax: LINT
Description: Static analysis over the loaded buffer. Reports parse stats, which files have OPTION "EXPLICIT"/"STRICT" active, and any assignment or reference to an undeclared name under EXPLICIT. Also lists any variable, parameter or loop variable whose name a builtin already carries, which runs but costs a debugging session when a statement-shaped builtin such as CD swallows the line that indexes it. Also usable from the command line via `jdBasic --lint file.jdb`.

[LIST]
Syntax: LIST
Description: Displays the current source code in the console.

[LIST_RECUR]
Syntax: LIST_RECUR() -> array
Description: Returns the active recurring tasks, each with its id, interval_ms and code.

[LOAD]
Syntax: LOAD "filename"
Description: Loads a source code file into memory.

[LPAD$]
Syntax: LPAD$(string$, width [, pad$])
Description: Left-pads string$ to width characters using pad$ (default " "). Multi-character pad$ cycles.

[LOADWS]
Syntax: LOADWS "workspacename"
Description: Loads a source code and variable workspace from a file.

[LOCATE]

Description: Moves the console cursor to a specified position.

[LOG]

Description: Returns the natural logarithm of a number.

[LOG10]

Description: Returns the base-10 logarithm of a number.

[LOOP]

Description: Marks the end of a DO loop.

[MAP]
Syntax: DIM variable AS MAP
Description: Declares a variable as a key-value dictionary.

[MAP.CLEAR]

Description: Removes all items from a map.

MAP.FROM(json_string$) -> map
Creates a Map directly from a JSON object formatted string.

[MAT4.IDENTITY]
Syntax: MAT4.IDENTITY() -> mat4
Description: Returns a 4x4 identity matrix as a 16-element column-major tensor.

[MAT4.LOOKAT]
Syntax: MAT4.LOOKAT(ex, ey, ez, tx, ty, tz, ux, uy, uz) -> mat4
Description: Builds a view matrix from eye (e), target (t) and up (u) vectors (9 scalar args).

[MAT4.MUL]
Syntax: MAT4.MUL(a, b) -> mat4
Description: Returns the matrix product a * b.

[MAT4.PERSPECTIVE]
Syntax: MAT4.PERSPECTIVE(fov_deg, aspect, near, far) -> mat4
Description: Perspective projection matrix. fov_deg is the field of view in DEGREES.

[MAT4.ROTATE]
Syntax: MAT4.ROTATE(m, angle_deg, ax, ay, az) -> mat4
Description: Returns m * Rotation(angle about axis ax,ay,az). The angle is in degrees, like every graphics angle; MAT4.ROTATE_RAD takes radians.

[MAT4.ROTATE_RAD]
Syntax: MAT4.ROTATE_RAD(m, angle_rad, ax, ay, az) -> mat4
Description: Returns m * Rotation(angle about axis ax,ay,az) with the angle in radians. Until 2.0 this was MAT4.ROTATE.

[MAT4.SCALE]
Syntax: MAT4.SCALE(m, sx, sy, sz) -> mat4
Description: Returns m * Scale(sx, sy, sz).

[MAT4.TRANSLATE]
Syntax: MAT4.TRANSLATE(m, x, y, z) -> mat4
Description: Returns m * Translation(x, y, z).

[MATMUL]
Syntax: MATMUL(a, b)
Description: The matrix product: a is [M,K], b is [K,N], the answer [M,N]. A flat
array on the right is a column of K cells and answers a flat array of M; one
on the left is a row and answers a flat array of N. Shapes that do not fit are
an error; the dot product of two vectors is SUM(a * b).

[MATMUL_T]
Syntax: MATMUL_T(a, b)
Description: MATMUL(TRANSPOSE(a), b) without the transposed copy: a is [K,M],
b is [K,N], the answer [M,N]. The gradient step x^T * delta and the Gram
matrix h^T * h.

[MAX]
Syntax: MAX(array) or MAX(array, axis)
Description: Returns the maximum value from an array, every cell of every
depth. Given an axis, answers the array with that axis taken out: for a
matrix axis 0 reduces down the rows (one value per column), axis 1 across
each row; a 3-D array [B][M][K] gives [M][K] for axis 0 and [B][M] for axis
2. An axis the array does not have is an error. The second argument is never
a second value to compare; write MAX([a, b]) for that.

[MID$]
Syntax: MID$(string$, start, [length])
Description: Returns a substring from a string.

[MIN]
Syntax: MIN(array) or MIN(array, axis)
Description: Returns the minimum value from an array, every cell of every
depth. Given an axis, answers the array with that axis taken out, as MAX
does. An axis the array does not have is an error. The second argument is
never a second value to compare; write MIN([a, b]) for that.

[MKDIR]
Syntax: MKDIR "directory_name"
Description: Creates a new directory, and any missing parent directories on the way (like mkdir -p). An existing directory is fine; a path that cannot be created raises an error.

[MKTEMP$]
Syntax: MKTEMP$([prefix$])
Description: A file path in the OS temp directory that nothing else is using. The file itself does not exist when you get the path - write to it to create it. On Windows only the first three characters of the prefix are used, so MKTEMP$("probe") gives a name beginning "pro". Default prefix is "jdb".

[MOD]
Syntax: number MOD number
Description: Returns the remainder of an integer division.

[MODULE]
Syntax: EXPORT MODULE
Description: Keyword used in conjunction with EXPORT.

[MOUSEB]
Syntax: MOUSEB(button_index)
Description: Returns TRUE if the specified mouse button (1=L, 2=M, 3=R) is pressed.

[MOUSEX]
Syntax: MOUSEX()
Description: Returns the current X coordinate of the mouse in the graphics window.

[MOUSEY]
Syntax: MOUSEY()
Description: Returns the current Y coordinate of the mouse in the graphics window.

[MUSIC.PLAY]
Syntax: MUSIC.PLAY(sound_id, [looping_bool])
Description: Plays a loaded sound as looping background music.

[MUSIC.STOP]
Syntax: MUSIC.STOP
Description: Stops the currently playing background music.

[MVLET]
Syntax: MVLET(matrix, dimension, index, vector)
Description: Returns a new matrix with a specified row or column replaced by a vector.

[MVINS]
Syntax: MVINS(matrix, dimension, index, value)
Description: Returns a new matrix with a row (dimension 0) or column (dimension 1)
INSERTED at index. Use index = the current row/column count to append at the end.
value is a vector (one entry per row/column) or a scalar broadcast to fill it.
The original matrix is not modified.
Example: m2 = MVINS(m, 1, 6, nights)   ' append a computed 7th column
Example: m3 = MVINS(m, 1, 0, 0)        ' insert a leading column of zeros

[NET.ACCEPT]
Syntax: NET.ACCEPT(listener, [timeout_ms]) -> handle
Description: Takes the next waiting TCP connection on a NET.LISTEN socket. Returns 0 on timeout; timeout_ms defaults to -1 (wait).

[NET.ALIVE]
Syntax: NET.ALIVE(handle) -> bool
Description: TRUE while the socket is open and, for TCP, the peer has not closed or unread data is left.

[NET.CLOSE]
Syntax: NET.CLOSE(handle) -> bool
Description: Closes a socket. FALSE when the handle was not open.

[NET.CONNECT]
Syntax: NET.CONNECT(host$, port, [timeout_ms]) -> handle
Description: Opens a TCP connection. timeout_ms defaults to 5000. Returns 0 on failure, NET.ERROR$() says why.

[NET.ERROR$]
Syntax: NET.ERROR$() -> string$
Description: The message of the last failed NET call.

[NET.LISTEN]
Syntax: NET.LISTEN(port, [bind$]) -> handle
Description: Opens a listening TCP socket. bind$ defaults to "0.0.0.0". Port 0 picks a free port, read it with NET.PORT. Returns 0 on failure.

[NET.PEER$]
Syntax: NET.PEER$(handle) -> string$
Description: "host:port" of the other end of a TCP connection.

[NET.PORT]
Syntax: NET.PORT(handle) -> number
Description: The local port of a socket.

[NET.RECV$]
Syntax: NET.RECV$(handle, [max_bytes], [timeout_ms]) -> string$
Description: Returns the bytes that have arrived, at most max_bytes (default 65536). "" on timeout or after the peer closed and everything is read.

[NET.RECVFROM]
Syntax: NET.RECVFROM(handle, [timeout_ms]) -> map
Description: Returns the next UDP datagram as {"data", "host", "port"}, or NONE on timeout.

[NET.RECVLINE$]
Syntax: NET.RECVLINE$(handle, [timeout_ms]) -> string$
Description: Returns the next line without its LF or CR LF. "" on timeout.

[NET.SEND]
Syntax: NET.SEND(handle, data$) -> bytes
Description: Sends all of data$ on a TCP connection. Returns the bytes sent, -1 when nothing could be sent.

[NET.SENDTO]
Syntax: NET.SENDTO(handle, host$, port, data$) -> bytes
Description: Sends one UDP datagram. Returns -1 on error.

[NET.UDP]
Syntax: NET.UDP([port], [bind$]) -> handle
Description: Opens a UDP socket. port defaults to 0, bind$ to "0.0.0.0". Returns 0 on failure.

[NEW]
Syntax: NEW
Description: Clears the current source code from memory.

[NEXT]
Syntax: FOR ... NEXT
Description: Marks the end of a FOR loop and increments the counter.

[NORMALIZE]
Syntax: NORMALIZE(array)
Description: Scales the elements of a numeric array to the range [0.0, 1.0].

[NOT]
Syntax: NOT expression
Description: Performs a logical NOT operation.

[NOW]
Syntax: NOW()
Description: Returns a DateTime object representing the current moment.

[NOW_EPOCH]
Syntax: NOW_EPOCH()
Description: Returns the current wallclock time as seconds since 1970-01-01 UTC (a plain number, monotonic across program runs). Available in both interpreter and native -c.

[ON]
Syntax: ON "event" CALL handler@
Description: Registers a SUB as the handler of an event. The handler without @ still works for one release; --lint names the funcref. Deprecated for error handling.

[OPTION]
Syntax: OPTION "option_name"
Description: Sets a compiler or runtime option. "EXPLICIT" and "STRICT" (off again with "EXPLICITOFF" and "NOSTRICT") control the checks of the native compiler: EXPLICIT makes an assignment to a name never declared with DIM a compile error, STRICT checks types (see STRICT). With EXPLICIT the interpreter also refuses to run a file that reads or assigns an undeclared name (error 20, with the line); --lint lists such names. "NOCOLOR" and "COLOR" switch colored error messages, "AUTOINDENT" and "NOAUTOINDENT" the editor's indentation.

[OR]
Syntax: expression OR expression
Description: Performs a logical OR operation.

[ORELSE]
Syntax: expression ORELSE expression
Description: Performs a short-circuiting logical OR operation.

[OS.ARGS]
Syntax: OS.ARGS()
Description: Returns a 1D array of command-line arguments.

[OS.EXEC]
Syntax: OS.EXEC(command$, [args_array$])
Description: Executes an external command and captures its output. Without args_array$ the command line goes to the shell (cmd /c, sh) as written. With args_array$ command$ names the program and each element reaches it as one argument, read by no shell, so & | > ; and $ in an argument stay text; a .cmd or .bat file runs under cmd with every argument quoted, and an argument holding % or a double quote is refused there. On Windows the output arrives as UTF-8: output in the OEM codepage of console tools such as schtasks is converted, UTF-8 output stays as it is.

[OS.GETOS]
Syntax: OS.GETOS()
Description: Old name of OS.GETOS$, still accepted for one release; --lint, jdb_check and -c name OS.GETOS$, and tools/jdb-fix.jdb rewrites it.

[OS.SPAWN]
Syntax: OS.SPAWN(command$, [args_array$], [options]) -> pid
Description: Starts a program and returns its process id at once. With args_array$ the program runs without a shell and gets each element as one argument; without it command$ is a shell line. options map: "cwd" working directory, "env" map of extra variables, "output" file for stdout and stderr, "hidden" TRUE for no console window (Windows).

[OS.WAIT]
Syntax: OS.WAIT(pid, [timeout_ms]) -> exit code or NONE
Description: Waits for a child started by OS.SPAWN and returns its exit code, or NONE when it still runs after timeout_ms.

[OS.ALIVE]
Syntax: OS.ALIVE(pid) -> boolean
Description: TRUE while the process runs. Works for any process id.

[OS.KILL]
Syntax: OS.KILL(pid) -> boolean
Description: Ends the process at once. FALSE when it was gone, may not be ended, or is the program itself.

[OS.PID]
Syntax: OS.PID() -> number
Description: The process id of the running program.

[OS.SELF$]
Syntax: OS.SELF$() -> string$
Description: The full path of the running executable: jdBasic for a script, the program itself when compiled.

[OS.HOSTNAME$]
Syntax: OS.HOSTNAME$()
Description: Returns the network hostname of the local machine.

[OS.IP$]
Syntax: OS.IP$()
Description: Returns the primary local IPv4 address of the machine.

[OS.LOAD]
Syntax: OS.LOAD() -> number
Description: The CPU load of the whole machine in percent (0 to 100), measured since the previous call; the first call measures over a tenth of a second. Windows, Linux and macOS.

[OS.FEATURE]
Syntax: OS.FEATURE(name$) -> BOOLEAN
Description: TRUE iff the running binary advertises the named build feature.
Use to gate VM-only paths in programs that may run from a --compile'd .exe.
Names: NATIVEC, INTERPRETER, COM, HTTP, NET, SERIAL, GFX, IMGUI, FORMS, OPENGL,
MINIAUDIO, FX, MIDI, LLM, ONNX, SQLITE, PYTHON, MCPSERVER, LLVMC.
Example: IF NOT OS.FEATURE("NATIVEC") THEN ... ENDIF

[OS.SCREENSHOT]
Syntax: OS.SCREENSHOT(path$, [mode$], [caption$]) -> INTEGER
Description: Capture the screen or a window to an image file (Windows only;
returns -100 elsewhere). Returns 0 on success, negative on error. The image
format is taken from the extension: .png .jpg/.jpeg .bmp .tif/.tiff .gif
(encoded via the Windows Imaging Component).
mode$: "screen" (default) = whole desktop; "window" = window incl. frame;
"client" = window content only. caption$: optional FindWindow title for
window/client; empty = foreground window.
Example: OS.SCREENSHOT("shot.png")
Example: OS.SCREENSHOT("calc.jpg", "client", "Calculator")

[OUTER]
Syntax: OUTER(vectorA, vectorB, operator)
Description: Creates an outer product table from two vectors and an operator.

[OUTPUT.CAPTURE_BEGIN]
Syntax: OUTPUT.CAPTURE_BEGIN
Description: Begins capturing all subsequent PRINT/script output to a fresh in-memory buffer. Captures stack: each BEGIN saves the previous output handler so nested captures restore correctly.

[OUTPUT.CAPTURE_END$]
Syntax: OUTPUT.CAPTURE_END$() -> string$
Description: Stops the most recent capture and returns the buffered text. Errors if no capture is active.

[OUTPUT.CAPTURE_PEEK$]
Syntax: OUTPUT.CAPTURE_PEEK$() -> string$
Description: Returns the current capture buffer's contents without stopping capture. Errors if no capture is active.

[PACK$]
Syntax: PACK$(format$, v1, v2, ...)
Description: Packs values into a binary string. Format codes (case-insensitive): "<" little endian (default), ">" big endian, "b" 8-bit, "s" 16-bit, "i" 32-bit, "l" 64-bit, "f" float, "d" double, "c" "h" "n" the signed 8/16/32-bit codes, "a" fixed-length string (NUL padded or cut), "x" zero pad byte. A count before a code repeats it ("3i" = "iii"); for "a" it is the string length, for "x" the number of pad bytes. Whitespace is ignored.
Example: PACK$("<4ai4a", "RIFF", 36, "WAVE")

[PACKSIZE]
Syntax: PACKSIZE(format$) -> number
Description: The number of bytes PACK$ writes and UNPACK reads for format$. PACKSIZE("<4ai4a") is 12.

[PATH.ABS$]
Syntax: PATH.ABS$(path$) -> string
Description: The same place named from the root. A relative path is read against the current directory; . and .. are resolved either way, and the file does not have to exist. PATH.ABS$(".") answers the current directory as a string.

[PATH.BASENAME$]
Syntax: PATH.BASENAME$(path$)
Description: Returns the filename part of a path (e.g., "file.txt" from "/dir/file.txt").

[PATH.DIRNAME$]
Syntax: PATH.DIRNAME$(path$)
Description: Returns the directory part of a path (e.g., "a/b" from "a/b/c.txt"). Returns "" for a bare filename and "/" for a root-level path like "/x".

[PATH.EXT$]
Syntax: PATH.EXT$(path$)
Description: Returns the file extension of a path (e.g., ".png").

[PATH.ISABS]
Syntax: PATH.ISABS(path$) -> boolean
Description: Whether a path names a place on its own, without a current directory to read it against. On Windows that is a drive ("D:\x"), a UNC share ("\\host\share") or a path rooted on the current drive ("\x"); elsewhere a leading "/". An empty string is not absolute.

[PATH.JOIN$]
Syntax: PATH.JOIN$(part1$, part2$, ...)
Description: Joins path components using the operating system's separator.

[PATH.NORMALIZE$]
Syntax: PATH.NORMALIZE$(path$)
Description: Normalizes a path by resolving "." and ".." segments and converting to the OS-native separator. Preserves drive prefixes on Windows.

[MATH.E]
Syntax: MATH.E
Description: A constant holding Euler's number, approx. 2.718281828459045. MATH.E() reads it too.

[MATH.PI]
Syntax: MATH.PI
Description: A constant holding the value of Pi, approx. 3.141592653589793. MATH.PI() reads it too.

[PLACE]
Syntax: PLACE(destination_array, source_array, coordinates)
Description: Places a source array into a destination array at a given location.

[PLOTRAW]
Syntax: PLOTRAW x, y, matrix, [scaleX, scaleY]
Description: Draws a matrix of color values directly to the graphics screen.

[PRETTY]
Syntax: PRETTY [PREVIEW] [STYLE UPPER|VB]
Description: Reformats the loaded source: 4-space indent, normalized keyword casing.
  PREVIEW    show the result on screen without overwriting the buffer
  STYLE VB   Pascal-cased keywords (For, Print, Next) instead of UPPER (the default)
  Strings and ' / REM comments are passed through verbatim.
  Same formatting is available at the CLI via `jdbasic --pretty file.jdb` (or --pretty-vb).

[PRINT]
PRINT [expressionlist] [{; | ,}]
Outputs text or variable values to the console. In the REPL a line that starts with ? is a PRINT (? x * 2); program code has no such shorthand.

[PRODUCT]
Syntax: PRODUCT(array) or PRODUCT(matrix, dimension)
Description: Returns the product of all elements in an array.

[PSET]
Syntax: PSET x, y, [r, g, b]
Description: Draws a single pixel on the graphics screen.

[PWD]
Syntax: PWD
Description: Prints the current working directory.

[RAISEEVENT]
Syntax: RAISEEVENT "event_name", data
Description: Triggers a custom event that can be handled by an ON...CALL statement.

[RANDOM]
Syntax: RANDOM([lo], [hi])
Description: Uniform random double in [lo, hi], hi inclusive. RANDOM() gives [0, 1], RANDOM(hi) gives [0, hi]. All arities work in interpreter and native -c.

[RANDOMSEED]
Syntax: RANDOMSEED(seed)
Description: Seeds the PRNG that RND and RANDOM draw from. The same seed reproduces the same sequence, and without a call the sequence is the same on every run - RANDOMSEED(NOW_EPOCH()) picks a different one each time.

[REACT]
Syntax: DIM variable AS REACT type
Description: Declares a reactive variable whose value automatically updates when its dependencies change.

[RECT]
Syntax: RECT x, y, w, h, [fill], [r, g, b]
Description: Draws a rectangle on the graphics screen.

[RECUR]
Syntax: RECUR(interval_ms, code_string$) -> task_id
Description: Starts a background task that executes code_string$ every interval_ms milliseconds. Returns the task id for CLEAR_RECUR.

[REDUCE]
Syntax: REDUCE(function@, array, [initial_value])
Description: Performs a cumulative reduction on an array using a custom function.

[REGEX.FINDALL]
Syntax: REGEX.FINDALL(pattern$, text$)
Description: Every match of a pattern in a string. Without capture groups the answer is one string per match; with groups it is one array per match, holding the whole match and then each group. The pattern syntax is ECMAScript; a leading (?i) asks for case-insensitive matching.

[REGEX.MATCH]
Syntax: REGEX.MATCH(pattern$, text$)
Description: Whether a string matches a pattern in full. The pattern syntax is ECMAScript; a leading (?i) asks for case-insensitive matching. Answers the captured groups instead of TRUE when the pattern has any.

[REGEX.REPLACE$]
Syntax: REGEX.REPLACE$(pattern$, text$, replacement$)
Description: Replaces every match of a pattern in a string. In the replacement text $1 to $9 stand for the capture groups, $& for the whole match, and $$ for a single dollar; a dollar that stands alone is kept as it is. The pattern syntax is ECMAScript; a leading (?i) asks for case-insensitive matching.

[REGEX.REPLACE]
Syntax: REGEX.REPLACE(pattern$, text$, replacement$)
Description: Old name of REGEX.REPLACE$, still accepted for one release; --lint, jdb_check and -c name REGEX.REPLACE$, and tools/jdb-fix.jdb rewrites it.

[REM]
Syntax: REM comment_text
Description: Marks the rest of the line as a comment. An apostrophe (') is a shorthand.

[REPLACE$]
REPLACE$(source$, find$, replace$) -> string_or_array
Replaces all occurrences of find$ with replace$.

[RESHAPE]
Syntax: RESHAPE(array, shape)
Description: The cells of the array, in order and again from the start when
they run out, in the dimensions of the shape: RESHAPE(IOTA(6), [2, 3]) is a
2 by 3 matrix, RESHAPE(m, 6) lays a matrix flat, RESHAPE(IOTA(8), [2, 2, 2])
is 3-D, RESHAPE(7, [3]) is [7, 7, 7]. A nested array is read row by row. An
empty array is an error.

[RESUME]
Syntax: RESUME
Description: Continues execution after a program has been halted with STOP.

[RETURN]
Syntax: RETURN [value]
Description: Returns a value from a function or exits a subroutine.

[REVERSE]
Syntax: REVERSE(array)
Description: Reverses the elements of an array.

[REVERSE$]
Syntax: REVERSE$(string$)
Description: Reverses the characters in a string.

[REPEAT$]
Syntax: REPEAT$(string$, count)
Description: Returns string$ concatenated count times. Returns "" for count <= 0 or empty input.

[RIGHT$]
Syntax: RIGHT$(string$, length)
Description: Returns the specified number of characters from the end of a string.

[RMDIR]
Syntax: RMDIR "path"
Description: Removes an empty directory.

[RND]
Syntax: RND()
Description: Returns a random double in [0, 1], both ends inclusive. Arguments are ignored. For an integer in [1, n] use INT(RND() * n) MOD n + 1. Unseeded the sequence is the same on every run, which is what makes a test repeatable; call RANDOMSEED to pick a different one, for instance RANDOMSEED(NOW_EPOCH()).

[RNG.NEW]
Syntax: RNG.NEW(seed) -> handle
Description: Creates an independent pseudo-random generator (xoshiro256** seeded through splitmix64). The same seed gives the same sequence in the interpreter, in native -c and in other xoshiro256** implementations. Generators do not touch RND/RANDOMSEED. Not for secrets; use CODEC.RANDOMBYTES$ there.

[RNG.NEXT]
Syntax: RNG.NEXT(handle) -> number
Description: The next double in [0, 1), 1 excluded, with 53 random bits.

[RNG.INT]
Syntax: RNG.INT(handle, lo, hi) -> number
Description: A uniformly distributed integer in lo..hi, both ends included, without modulo bias. lo greater than hi is an error.

[RNG.FILL]
Syntax: RNG.FILL(handle, n) -> array
Description: An array of the next n doubles in [0, 1), the same values n RNG.NEXT calls give.

[RNG.FREE]
Syntax: RNG.FREE(handle)
Description: Releases a generator. Using the handle afterwards is an error.

[ROTATE]
Syntax: ROTATE(array, shift_vector)
Description: Cyclically shifts an N-dimensional array. One entry of shift_vector per axis, outermost first; more entries than the array has axes is an error. ROTATE(m, [1, 0]) turns the rows, ROTATE(m, [0, 1]) the columns, ROTATE(m, [1, 1]) both. A positive shift pulls from ahead, out[i] = in[i + k], so ROTATE([1,2,3,4,5], [1]) is 2 3 4 5 1.

[ROTL]
Syntax: ROTL(x, n [, bits])
Description: Bit rotation left of integer x by n positions. Optional bits argument sets the width (default 64).

[ROTR]
Syntax: ROTR(x, n [, bits])
Description: Bit rotation right of integer x by n positions. Optional bits argument sets the width (default 64).

[RPAD$]
Syntax: RPAD$(string$, width [, pad$])
Description: Right-pads string$ to width characters using pad$ (default " "). Multi-character pad$ cycles.

[ROUND]
Syntax: ROUND(number, [decimals])
Description: Rounds a number to a specified number of decimal places.

[ROUNDED_RECT]
Syntax: ROUNDED_RECT x, y, w, h, radius, [fill], [r, g, b]
Description: Draws a rectangle with rounded corners.

[RUN]
Syntax: RUN
Description: Compiles and runs the program currently in memory.

[SAVE]
Syntax: SAVE "filename"
Description: Saves the current source code to a file.

[SAVEWS]
Syntax: SAVEWS "workspacename"
Description: Saves the current source code and all variables to a workspace file.

[SCAN]
Syntax: SCAN(operator, array)
Description: Performs a cumulative scan (prefix sum) operation on an array.

[SCREEN]
Syntax: SCREEN width, height, [title$], [scalefactor]
Description: Initializes a graphics window. Drawing uses width x height logical pixels; scalefactor (default 1) multiplies the window size, so SCREEN 320, 200, "Game", 3 opens a 960 x 600 window showing 320 x 200 pixels.

[SCREENFLIP]
Syntax: SCREENFLIP
Description: Updates the graphics screen to show all drawing operations.

[SCREENHEIGHT]
Syntax: SCREENHEIGHT()
Description: Returns the height of the current graphics screen in pixels.

[SCREENWIDTH]
Syntax: SCREENWIDTH()
Description: Returns the width of the current graphics screen in pixels.

[SELECT]
Syntax: SELECT(function@, array)
Description: Applies a function to each element of an array, returning a new array of the results.

[SETFONT]
Syntax: SETFONT filename$, size
Description: Sets the font and size for subsequent TEXT drawing commands.

[SETENV]
Syntax: SETENV name$, value$
Description: Sets an environment variable for the current process. An empty value$ removes the variable.

[SETLOCALE]
Syntax: SETLOCALE("locale_string")
Description: Sets the locale for number and date formatting (e.g., "en-US").

[SERIAL.AVAILABLE]
Syntax: SERIAL.AVAILABLE(handle)
Description: Returns the number of bytes currently waiting in the input buffer.

[SERIAL.CLOSE]
Syntax: SERIAL.CLOSE(handle)
Description: Closes an open serial port.

[SERIAL.FLUSH]
Syntax: SERIAL.FLUSH(handle)
Description: Clears the input and output buffers.

[SERIAL.OPEN]
Syntax: SERIAL.OPEN(port$, baud_rate)
Description: Opens a serial port (e.g., "COM3" on Windows, "/dev/ttyUSB0" on Linux) and returns a handle.

[SERIAL.READ$]
Syntax: SERIAL.READ$(handle, max_bytes)
Description: Reads up to max_bytes from the port. Returns an empty string if no data is available (non-blocking).

[SERIAL.WRITE]
Syntax: SERIAL.WRITE(handle, data$)
Description: Writes a string (or binary bytes) to the serial port.

[SFX.LOAD]
Syntax: SFX.LOAD(sound_id, "filepath.wav")
Description: Loads a WAV sound file into a sound effect slot.

[SFX.PLAY]
Syntax: SFX.PLAY(sound_id)
Description: Plays a loaded sound effect.

[SHIFT]
Syntax: SHIFT(array, shift_vector, [fill_value])
Description: Like ROTATE but without the wraparound: what moves in from outside is fill_value (default 0), and a whole row shifted off the edge comes back as a row of fill_value. Same per-axis rule as ROTATE, but note the opposite sign convention: a positive shift pushes along like a shift register, out[i] = in[i - k], so SHIFT([1,2,3,4,5], [1], 0) is 0 1 2 3 4. A shift at least as large as the axis leaves nothing but the fill.

[SHL]
Syntax: value SHL bits         (infix)
        SHL(value, bits)       (function form, also vectorises over arrays)
Description: Bitwise left shift. Operands are coerced to 64-bit signed
integers. Precedence is looser than +/- and tighter than comparison
and BAND/BOR/BXOR.

[SHR]
Syntax: value SHR bits         (infix)
        SHR(value, bits)       (function form, also vectorises over arrays)
Description: Arithmetic (sign-preserving) bitwise right shift. Operands
are coerced to 64-bit signed integers. Same precedence as SHL.

[RADIANS]
Syntax: RADIANS(degrees)
Description: Converts an angle from degrees to radians. Element-wise on arrays. Math builtins take radians, graphics builtins degrees.

[DEGREES]
Syntax: DEGREES(radians)
Description: Converts an angle from radians to degrees. Element-wise on arrays. Math builtins take radians, graphics builtins degrees.

[SIN]
Syntax: SIN(angle_in_radians)
Description: Returns the sine of an angle.

[SLEEP]
Syntax: SLEEP milliseconds
Description: Pauses program execution for a specified duration. The wait is measured against a deadline and sliced so events still get polled, so it does not overshoot by a multiple; what remains is one tick of the platform timer per slice, which is about 15.6 ms on Windows and under a millisecond elsewhere. Twenty SLEEP 10 in a row therefore take longer than 200 ms on Windows.

[SLICE]
Syntax: SLICE(matrix, dimension, index)
        SLICE(matrix, dimension, start, count)
Description: Extracts a row (dim=0) or column (dim=1) from a 2D matrix. With start and count, a band of rows (dim=0) or of columns out of every row (dim=1), stopping at the edge. A flat array, an axis other than 0 or 1 and an index outside the matrix are errors.

[SOLVE]
Syntax: SOLVE(matrixA, vectorB)
Description: Solves the linear system Ax = b for the unknown vector x.

[SOUND.INIT]
Syntax: SOUND.INIT [mode$]
Description: Initializes the audio system for synthesized sound.
mode$ "PULL" opens no audio device: SOUND.RENDER is then the only clock, so a render is reproducible.

[SOUND.KIT]
Syntax: SOUND.KIT track, [kit]
Description: Turns a track into a drum kit: pattern atoms name sounds ("bd sd hh"), name:n picks the n-th sample.
kit is "SYNTH" (built-in analog-style drums, no files: bd sd hh oh cr cp lt mt ht rim cb cl sh),
a kit file (one line per sound: name, WAV files, optional gain= and choke=) or a MAP name -> WAV path, SFX id or array.
Each hit plays its whole sample; a hit cuts its choke group (hh stops oh). SOUND.KIT track alone removes the kit.
Example: SOUND.KIT 0, "SYNTH" : SOUND.SEQ 0, "bd*4, ~ cp, [hh oh]*4", "VOICE"

[SOUND.PENDING]
Syntax: SOUND.PENDING() -> number
Description: Returns how many commands SOUND.AT has queued that the mixer has not applied yet.

[SOUND.SEEK]
Syntax: SOUND.SEEK [cycle]
Description: Moves the clock to cycle (no argument: keeps it) and drops the queue. Commands queued after it are
held, passed ones too, until SOUND.AT with no argument; the mixer then applies the passed ones at once, in order.

[SOUND.MUTE]
Syntax: SOUND.MUTE track, flag
Description: Silences a track (and its sends) while its patterns keep running. SOUND.RESET lifts all mutes.

[SOUND.LEVELS]
Syntax: SOUND.LEVELS() -> Array
Description: The highest level of each of the 16 tracks since the last call, for meters.

[SOUND.RECORD]
Syntax: SOUND.RECORD [path$]
Description: Writes the mixer output from now on into a 16-bit stereo WAV; no argument or "" finishes the file. Works for the device and for SOUND.RENDER in PULL mode.

[SOUND.PLAY]
Syntax: SOUND.PLAY(track, frequency)
Description: Plays a note at a specific frequency on a given synthesizer track.

[SOUND.RELEASE]
Syntax: SOUND.RELEASE(track)
Description: Starts the release phase of the ADSR envelope for a note.

[SOUND.STOP]
Syntax: SOUND.STOP(track)
Description: Immediately stops a note on a synthesizer track.

[SOUND.PLAYBUFFER]
Syntax: SOUND.PLAYBUFFER samples, [sample_rate], [channels]
Description: Pushes raw float samples (-1..1) onto a PCM stream that mixes alongside the synth. Use for hand-drawn waveforms or emulator audio. Defaults: sample_rate=44100, channels=1.

[SOUND.RENDER]
Syntax: SOUND.RENDER(frames)
Description: Renders the next 'frames' stereo frames of the live sequencer and returns them interleaved as [L0, R0, L1, R1, ...] (length frames*2), advancing the sequencer at 44100 Hz. For embed hosts built without an audio device (SOUND build flag) that feed their own engine, e.g. a Godot AudioStreamGenerator.

[SOUND.QUEUED]
Syntax: SOUND.QUEUED()
Description: Returns the number of bytes still waiting in the PLAYBUFFER queue. Useful for pacing pushes to avoid underrun/overflow.

[SOUND.VOICE]
Syntax: SOUND.VOICE track, waveform$, attack, decay, sustain, release
Description: Configures the ADSR envelope and waveform for a synthesizer track.

[SOUND.AT]
Syntax: SOUND.AT [cycle]
Description: Queues the following track and mix commands (SEQ, MOD, FILTER, GAIN, VOICE, ...) for the given sequencer cycle; the mixer applies them on the frame the clock reaches it. No argument or a negative cycle applies commands at once again.

[SOUND.BITCRUSH]
Syntax: SOUND.BITCRUSH track, bits, rate
Description: Applies a lo-fi bitcrusher effect to a track.
Bits: 1-16 (Resolution). Rate: 0.0-1.0 (Sample Rate Reduction).

[SOUND.BPM]
Syntax: SOUND.BPM(beats_per_minute)
Description: Sets the global tempo for the sequencer.

[SOUND.DELAY]
Syntax: SOUND.DELAY active_bool, time, feedback, mix, [orbit], [pingpong]
Description: Activates a global stereo delay (echo) effect.
time: milliseconds, or a note value locked to SOUND.BPM: "1/4", "1/8." (dotted), "1/8t" (triplet).
Feedback: 0.0-0.9. Mix: 0.0-1.0. orbit (0-3, default 0) picks the effect bus; see SOUND.ORBIT.
pingpong TRUE bounces each repeat between left and right.

[SOUND.DISTORTION]
Syntax: SOUND.DISTORTION amount
Description: Applies a master saturation/overdrive effect. Amount > 0.0.

[SOUND.FILTER]
Syntax: SOUND.FILTER track, cutoff_hz, [resonance], [mode$]
Description: Filters a track. With two arguments a gentle one-pole low-pass.
A resonance (0.0-1.0) or a mode selects the resonant state-variable filter.
Modes: "LP" low-pass, "HP" high-pass, "BP" band-pass, "LP1" the one-pole low-pass.

[SOUND.FENV]
Syntax: SOUND.FENV track, octaves, attack, decay, [sustain], [release]
Description: Filter envelope: each note opens the cutoff by up to `octaves` and closes it again.
sustain defaults to 0, release to 0.1 seconds.

[SOUND.MOD]
Syntax: SOUND.MOD track, param$, shape$, [lo], [hi], [cycles], [offset]
Description: Moves a track parameter between lo and hi, one period every `cycles` sequencer cycles.
Parameters: CUTOFF, RESONANCE, GAIN, PAN, DETUNE, FM, CRUSH, REVERB, DELAY, FENV,
VOWEL (0 a .. 4 u, see SOUND.FORMANT), PITCH (semitones).
Shapes: SINE, COSINE, SAW, ISAW, TRI, SQUARE, RAND, PERLIN. "OFF" stops it and restores the value.
Example: SOUND.MOD 1, "CUTOFF", "SINE", 300, 3000, 8

[SOUND.FM]
Syntax: SOUND.FM track, amount, ratio
Description: Applies Frequency Modulation synthesis.
Amount: Modulation depth. Ratio: Frequency multiplier relative to carrier.

[SOUND.GAIN]
Syntax: SOUND.GAIN track, volume
Description: Sets the volume gain for a specific track (0.0 to 1.0+).

[SOUND.GET_WAVE]
Syntax: SOUND.GET_WAVE()
Description: Returns the last 1024 samples of the master output, oldest first (a scope).

[SOUND.CYCLE]
Syntax: SOUND.CYCLE()
Description: The sequencer clock in cycles (bars): the whole part is the bar, the fraction the position in it.

[SOUND.CLOCK]
Syntax: SOUND.CLOCK()
Description: When the song is heard: {"cycle", "t", "cps"}: cycle "cycle" leaves the speaker at "t" (nanoseconds on the NODE.TIME clock, device latency included) and the song moves on at CPS cycles per second. Now heard: CYCLE + (NODE.TIME() - T) / 1E9 * CPS.

[SOUND.NUDGE]
Syntax: SOUND.NUDGE track, ms
Description: Starts every note of the track ms milliseconds late (0 to 1000).

[SOUND.ORBIT]
Syntax: SOUND.ORBIT track, orbit
Description: Sends the track's reverb and delay sends to effect bus 0-3. Each orbit has its own SOUND.REVERB / SOUND.DELAY.

[SOUND.LFO]
Syntax: SOUND.LFO track, frequency_hz, depth
Description: Applies a Low Frequency Oscillator to modulate pitch (Vibrato).

[SOUND.PAN]
Syntax: SOUND.PAN track, pan_value
Description: Sets the stereo panning for a track.
0.0 = Left, 0.5 = Center, 1.0 = Right.

[SOUND.RESET]
Syntax: SOUND.RESET
Description: Immediately silences all tracks, clears the sequencer, and resets effects.

[SOUND.RINGMOD]
Syntax: SOUND.RINGMOD track, frequency_hz, mix
Description: Applies Ring Modulation (multiplies signal by a sine wave).
Mix: 0.0 (Dry) to 1.0 (Wet).

[SOUND.FORMANT]
Syntax: SOUND.FORMANT track, vowel$, mix, [breath]
Description: Three band-passes on the formants of a sung vowel: "a" "e" "i" "o" "u"
(also "ah" "eh" "ee" "oh" "oo") or a position 0 (a) to 4 (u). mix 0.0-1.0 is the wet share,
breath 0.0-1.0 adds noise before the filters. SOUND.MOD track, "VOWEL", ... morphs the vowel.
Example: SOUND.FORMANT 6, "oo", 1, 0.08

[SOUND.GLIDE]
Syntax: SOUND.GLIDE track, ms, [mode$]
Description: Portamento from the track's previous note. Mode "ALL" (default) glides into
every note, "SLIDE" only into notes marked ^ in the pattern: "c2 c2 c3^ c2". 0 turns it off.

[SOUND.CHORUS]
Syntax: SOUND.CHORUS track, mix, [rate], [depth]
Description: Stereo chorus on the sum of the track's voices. rate in Hz (default 0.8),
depth in ms (default 3). mix 0 turns it off.

[SOUND.WIDTH]
Syntax: SOUND.WIDTH track, width
Description: Stereo width of the track after its chorus: 0 mono, 1 unchanged, up to 2 wider.

[SOUND.SCALE]
Syntax: SOUND.SCALE root_note$, scale_mode$
Description: Sets the musical scale for the sequencer's number notation.
Modes: MAJOR, MINOR, PENT_MIN, BLUES, ARABIC, etc.

[SOUND.SEQ]
Syntax: SOUND.SEQ layer, pattern$, waveform$
Description: Programs a rhythmic pattern for the sequencer.
Waveform can be "SINE", "SQUARE", "SAW", "TRIANGLE", "NOISE", or "VOICE".
A layer that is playing switches to the new pattern at the start of the next cycle; a switch queued with SOUND.AT applies on its own frame, also inside a cycle.
Pattern: a b (steps)  [a b] (group)  a,b (together)  <a b> (one per cycle)  a|b (random)
~ (rest)  _ (hold)  a*2 a/2 (faster/slower)  a!3 (repeat)  a@3 (weight)  a?0.3 (chance)  a(3,8) (euclid)
Chords: an upper-case root is a chord, voice-led in order: "<Am F C G>", Cmaj7 G7 Dm9 Esus4 Am/E F#m Bb
Numerals on the track's SOUND.SCALE: "<i VI III VII>", V7. Notes stay lower case (c4).
Transforms, pattern last: rev(p) palindrome(p) fast(n,p) slow(n,p) ply(n,p) iter(n,p) add(n,p) arp(up|down|updown|downup,p)
degrade(p) degradeBy(x,p) every(n,F,p) off(t,F,p) jux(F,p) juxBy(w,F,p) sometimes(F,p) often rarely sometimesBy(x,F,p)
F is a transform without its pattern: rev, add(12), fast(2). Example: "every(4, rev, c3 e3 g3)"
gain(v,p) legato(v,p) pan(v,p): v a number or number pattern read at each onset, e.g. gain([1 0.5]*4, hh*8)
swing(n,p) swingBy(x,n,p): the second half of each of n slices plays x slices late

[SOUND.EVENTS$]
Syntax: SOUND.EVENTS$(pattern$, [cycles], [first])
Description: Lists the events a pattern plays, one line each: "start duration note".
Times are in cycles. Needs no SOUND.INIT.

[SOUND.COMPRESSOR]
Syntax: SOUND.COMPRESSOR threshold, ratio, attack, release, gain
Description: Applies master dynamic range compression.
Threshold: 0.0-1.0. Ratio: 1.0-20.0. Attack/Release: ms. Gain: 1.0+.

[SOUND.LIMITER]
Syntax: SOUND.LIMITER [ceiling_db], [drive_db], [release_ms]
Description: Lookahead peak limiter at the end of the master. drive_db (-24..24, default 0) lifts the mix into it,
no sample passes ceiling_db (-24..0), release_ms defaults to 80. No argument switches it off.

[SOUND.LOUDNESS]
Syntax: SOUND.LOUDNESS([reset]) -> Map
Description: Loudness of the output since init, reset or the last SOUND.LOUDNESS(TRUE), after EBU R128:
INTEGRATED, MOMENTARY, SHORT, SHORT_MAX (LUFS), PEAK (dBFS), REDUCTION, REDUCTION_MAX (limiter, dB), SECONDS.

[SOUND.MASTER]
Syntax: SOUND.MASTER mode$, [headroom]
Description: Sets how the master sums the voices. "AUTO" (default) divides the mix by sqrt(sounding voices).
"FIXED" scales every voice by headroom (default 0.5), so a track keeps its level whatever else plays.
The output soft-clips above 0.8 in both modes. SOUND.RESET returns to "AUTO".

[SOUND.EQ]
Syntax: SOUND.EQ track, low_gain, mid_gain, high_gain
Description: Sets the 3-band equalizer gains for a track.
1.0 is flat, 0.0 cuts the band, >1.0 boosts it.

[SOUND.REVERB]
Syntax: SOUND.REVERB room_size, damping, width, wet, [orbit]
Description: Activates the master reverb effect.
Room: 0.7-0.99. Damp: 0.0-1.0. Width: 0.0-1.0. Wet: 0.0-1.0. orbit (0-3, default 0) picks the effect bus; see SOUND.ORBIT.

[SOUND.SAMPLE]
Syntax: SOUND.SAMPLE track, sample_id, base_note$, loop_bool
Description: Assigns a loaded SFX sample to a synth track for melodic playback.
Base note (e.g., "C3") sets the pitch of the original WAV.

[SOUND.SHUTDOWN]
Syntax: SOUND.SHUTDOWN
Description: Closes the audio stream and releases the audio device.

[SPLIT]
Syntax: SPLIT(source$, delimiter$)
Description: Splits a string by a delimiter and returns a 1D array of strings.

[SQL.OPEN]
Syntax: SQL.OPEN(path$)
Description: Opens or creates a SQLite database file, returns an integer handle (0 = failure). Needs the SQLITE build flag; check OS.FEATURE("SQLITE").

[SQL.CLOSE]
Syntax: SQL.CLOSE(handle)
Description: Closes a SQLite database handle.

[SQL.EXEC]
Syntax: SQL.EXEC(handle, sql$)
Description: Runs a non-query SQL statement. Returns affected rows, -1 on error (see SQL.ERRMSG$).

[SQL.QUERY]
Syntax: SQL.QUERY(handle, sql$)
Description: Runs a SELECT and returns an array of row maps keyed by column name, with typed cells. Interpreter only; use SQL.TABLE + SQL.COLUMNS in compiled programs.

[SQL.TABLE]
Syntax: SQL.TABLE(handle, sql$)
Description: Runs a SELECT and returns a 2D array of typed row values. Works in interpreter and native -c.

[SQL.COLUMNS]
Syntax: SQL.COLUMNS(handle, sql$)
Description: Returns the result column names of a query as a string array.

[SQL.ERRMSG$]
Syntax: SQL.ERRMSG$(handle)
Description: Last SQLite error message for the handle (handle 0 = last failed SQL.OPEN).

[PYTHON$]
Syntax: PYTHON$(code$)
Description: Runs a multi-line Python code block in the persistent namespace and returns its captured stdout. Needs the PYTHON build flag; check OS.FEATURE("PYTHON"). Use CHR$(10) for line breaks. Interpreter only.

[PY.EVAL]
Syntax: PY.EVAL(expr$)
Description: Evaluates a single Python expression and returns the result as a native jdBasic value (list->array, dict->object, numpy/array.array via tolist()->array). Interpreter only.

[PY.SET]
Syntax: PY.SET(name$, value)
Description: Injects a jdBasic value into the Python namespace under name$. Interpreter only.

[PY.GET]
Syntax: PY.GET(name$)
Description: Reads a Python variable back as a jdBasic value (errors if undefined). Interpreter only.

[PY.DIR$]
Syntax: PY.DIR$([target$])
Description: Lists the namespace's own names, or the public members of a target object/module, as a comma-separated string. Interpreter only.

[PY.HELP$]
Syntax: PY.HELP$(target$)
Description: Returns inspect.getdoc(target) for a Python module or function. Interpreter only.

[SPRITE.COLLISION]
Syntax: SPRITE.COLLISION(id1, id2)
Description: Checks if two sprite instances are colliding.

[SPRITE.DELETE]
Syntax: SPRITE.DELETE(instance_id)
Description: Removes a sprite instance.

[SPRITE.DRAW_ALL]
Syntax: SPRITE.DRAW_ALL([world_x, world_y])
Description: Draws all active sprite instances, optionally offsetting by a camera position.

[SPRITE.GET_X]
Syntax: SPRITE.GET_X(instance_id)
Description: Returns the X coordinate of a sprite instance.

[SPRITE.GET_Y]
Syntax: SPRITE.GET_Y(instance_id)
Description: Returns the Y coordinate of a sprite instance.

[SPRITE.LOAD]
Syntax: SPRITE.LOAD("filename.png"[, frame_w, frame_h]) -> sprite_id
Description: Loads a sprite image (optionally as a spritesheet with the given frame size) and returns its sprite id.

[SPRITE.SETPIXEL]
Syntax: SPRITE.SETPIXEL(id, x, y, r, g, b, a)
Description: Writes one RGBA pixel into a SPRITE.CREATE'd sprite. Uploads the texture after the write; use SPRITE.SETBUFFER for bulk fills.

[SPRITE.SETBUFFER]
Syntax: SPRITE.SETBUFFER(id, rgba_array)
Description: Bulk RGBA-fill from a flat array of length width*height*4. Length mismatch raises an error; values clamped to 0..255.

[SPRITE.SAVE]
Syntax: SPRITE.SAVE(id, path$)
Description: Writes the CPU RGBA buffer of a SPRITE.CREATE'd sprite to a PNG file. For SPRITE.LOAD'd images, use GFX.SAVE_IMAGE instead.

[SPRITE.MOVE]
Syntax: SPRITE.MOVE(instance_id, x, y)
Description: Moves a sprite instance to a new position.

[SPRITE.UPDATE]
Syntax: SPRITE.UPDATE
Description: Updates the positions and animations of all sprites based on their velocities. Takes no arguments: the time step is the real time since the previous call, capped at 0.1 seconds.

[SQR]
Syntax: SQR(number)
Description: Returns the square root of a number.

[STACK]
Syntax: STACK(dimension, array1, array2, ...)
Description: Stacks 1D vectors along a new dimension to create a 2D matrix.

[STATIC]
Syntax: STATIC DIM name [AS type] [= initializer]
Description: Declares a function-scoped persistent variable inside a FUNC or SUB. The initializer runs once on the first execution of the line; the slot keeps its value across subsequent calls. All recursive depths and cross-module callers share the same slot.

[STEP]
Syntax: FOR ... STEP value
Description: Specifies the increment value for a FOR loop counter.

[STOP]
Syntax: STOP
Description: Halts program execution and enters a break state.

[STR$]
Syntax: STR$(number)
Description: Converts a number to its string representation.

[STRICT]
Syntax: OPTION "STRICT"
Description: Type checking for the native compiler (-c). Under STRICT an assignment, call or return whose value does not fit the declared type is a compile error, and every error is listed with its line before the compile stops. -c turns STRICT and EXPLICIT on for the main file by default; OPTION "NOSTRICT" and OPTION "EXPLICITOFF" switch them off. An IMPORTed module is checked only when it says OPTION "STRICT" or "EXPLICIT" itself. The interpreter does not check types. Under EXPLICIT it refuses to run a file that reads or assigns an undeclared name (error 20); --lint lists undeclared names whatever the options say. The bare form OPTION STRICT is accepted too.

[STRING]
Syntax: DIM variable AS STRING
Description: Declares a variable to hold a string of text.

[SUB]
Syntax: SUB name(parameters) ... ENDSUB
Description: Begins the definition of a user-defined subroutine.

[SUM]
Syntax: SUM(array) or SUM(array, axis)
Description: Returns the sum of all cells in an array, of every depth. Given
an axis, answers the array with that axis taken out: for a matrix axis 0
reduces down the rows (one value per column), axis 1 across each row; a 3-D
array [B][M][K] gives [M][K] for axis 0 and [B][M] for axis 2. An axis the
array does not have is an error. PRODUCT, MEAN, MEDIAN, VARIANCE, STDEV, ANY
and ALL take the same axis.

[SWITCH]
Syntax: SWITCH expression ... ENDSWITCH
Description: Begins a block that executes different code based on the value of an expression.

[TAKE]
Syntax: TAKE(N, array)
Description: Returns a new array with the first N (or last N if negative) elements.

[TAKE_WHILE]
Syntax: TAKE_WHILE(predicate@, array)
Description: Returns the longest prefix of array for which predicate(elem) is TRUE. Stops at the first FALSE.

[TAN]
Syntax: TAN(angle_in_radians)
Description: Returns the tangent of an angle.

[TANH]
Syntax: TANH(x)
Description: Hyperbolic tangent. Vectorizes element-wise over arrays.

[TEXT]
Syntax: TEXT x, y, content$, [r, g, b]
Description: Draws a string of text on the graphics screen.

[THEN]
Syntax: IF condition THEN ...
Description: Keyword following an IF condition.

[THREAD]
Syntax: THREAD function_call()
Description: Executes a function call in a separate, parallel background thread.

[THREAD.GETRESULT]
Syntax: THREAD.GETRESULT(handle)
Description: Waits for a background thread to finish and retrieves its return value.

[THREAD.ISDONE]
Syntax: THREAD.ISDONE(handle)
Description: Checks if a background thread has finished executing without blocking.

[THROW]
Syntax: THROW [error_data]
Description: Manually raises a user-defined error that can be caught by a TRY...CATCH block.

[TICK]
Syntax: TICK()
Description: Returns the number of milliseconds elapsed since the program started.

[TILED.COLLIDES]
Syntax: TILED.COLLIDES(sprite_id, name$, layer$) -> boolean
Description: Returns TRUE if the sprite's bounding box collides with a non-empty tile in the named Tiled map layer.

[TILED.DRAW]
Syntax: TILED.DRAW(name$, [cam_x], [cam_y])
Description: Draws all layers of a loaded Tiled map in order, using the global camera offset when none is given.

[TILED.DRAW_LAYER]
Syntax: TILED.DRAW_LAYER(name$, layer$, [cam_x], [cam_y])
Description: Draws a single named layer of a loaded Tiled map, using the global camera offset when none is given.

[TILED.FREE]
Syntax: TILED.FREE(name$)
Description: Frees a loaded Tiled map and its resources.

[TILED.LAYERS]
Syntax: TILED.LAYERS(name$) -> array
Description: Returns an array of the layer name strings of a Tiled map in draw order.

[TILED.LAYERS$]
Syntax: TILED.LAYERS$(name$) -> array
Description: Old name of TILED.LAYERS, still accepted for one release; --lint, jdb_check and -c name TILED.LAYERS, and tools/jdb-fix.jdb rewrites it.

[TILED.LOAD]
Syntax: TILED.LOAD(name$, filename$) -> boolean
Description: Loads a Tiled (.tmx) map file under the given name and returns TRUE on success.

[TILED.OBJECTS]
Syntax: TILED.OBJECTS(name$, layer$) -> array
Description: Returns an array of objects from a Tiled object layer, each with id, name, type, x, y, width, height, gid and any custom properties.

[TILED.PROPERTIES]
Syntax: TILED.PROPERTIES(name$) -> object
Description: Returns an object of the map-level custom properties of a Tiled map.

[TILED.SIZE]
Syntax: TILED.SIZE(name$) -> [w,h]
Description: Returns the [pixel_width, pixel_height] of a Tiled map.

[TILED.TILE_AT]
Syntax: TILED.TILE_AT(name$, layer$, pixel_x, pixel_y) -> gid
Description: Returns the tile gid at a pixel position in a Tiled map layer (0 = empty).

[TILED.TILE_SIZE]
Syntax: TILED.TILE_SIZE(name$) -> [tile_w,tile_h]
Description: Returns the [tile_width, tile_height] of a Tiled map.

[TILED.UPDATE]
Syntax: TILED.UPDATE(dt)
Description: Advances the animated tiles of all loaded Tiled maps by dt seconds.

[TILEMAP.COLLIDES]
Syntax: TILEMAP.COLLIDES(sprite_id, name$) -> boolean
Description: Returns TRUE if the sprite's bounding box overlaps any non-empty tile in the named array tilemap.

[TILEMAP.CREATE]
Syntax: TILEMAP.CREATE(name$, tileset_image_id, data, tile_w, tile_h)
Description: Creates a named tilemap from a 2D array of 1-based tile ids drawn from a tileset image (0 = empty).

[TILEMAP.DRAW]
Syntax: TILEMAP.DRAW(name$, [cam_x], [cam_y])
Description: Draws a named tilemap, using the global camera offset when none is given.

[TILEMAP.GET]
Syntax: TILEMAP.GET(name$, col, row) -> tile_id
Description: Returns the tile id at the given column and row of a tilemap, or 0 if out of range.

[TILEMAP.SET]
Syntax: TILEMAP.SET(name$, col, row, tile_id)
Description: Sets the tile id at the given column and row of a tilemap.

[TILEMAP.SIZE]
Syntax: TILEMAP.SIZE(name$) -> [cols,rows]
Description: Returns the [columns, rows] dimensions of a tilemap.

[TILEMAP.TILE_AT]
Syntax: TILEMAP.TILE_AT(name$, pixel_x, pixel_y) -> tile_id
Description: Returns the tile id at a pixel position in a tilemap, or 0 if out of range.

[TIME$]
Syntax: TIME$
Description: Returns the current system time as a string in "HH:MM:SS" format.

[TO]
Syntax: FOR counter = start TO end
Description: Specifies the ending value for a FOR loop counter.

[GFX.DISPLAYS]
Syntax: GFX.DISPLAYS()
Description: One map per connected display: INDEX (from 1), NAME, X, Y, W, H and PRIMARY.

[GFX.DISPLAY]
Syntax: GFX.DISPLAY n
Description: The display the next SCREEN opens on (an INDEX of GFX.DISPLAYS, 0 for the primary). An open window moves there; TOGGLE_FULLSCREEN then fills that display.

[TOGGLE_FULLSCREEN]
Syntax: TOGGLE_FULLSCREEN
Description: Toggles the graphics window between fullscreen and windowed mode.

[TONUM]
Syntax: TONUM(string$)
Description: Parses a string as a number. Synonym for VAL.

[TOSTR]

Description: Old name of STR$, still accepted for one release; --lint, jdb_check and -c name STR$, and tools/jdb-fix.jdb rewrites it.

[TRANSPOSE]
Syntax: TRANSPOSE(matrix)
Description: Transposes a 2D matrix (swaps rows and columns).

[TRIM$]
Syntax: TRIM$(string$)
Description: Removes leading and trailing whitespace from a string.

[TROFF]
Syntax: TROFF
Description: Turns instruction tracing off.

[TRON]
Syntax: TRON
Description: Turns instruction tracing on for debugging.

[TRUE]
Syntax: TRUE
Description: The boolean constant representing a true value.

[TRUNC]
Syntax: TRUNC(number)
Description: Truncates the decimal part of a number, rounding towards zero.

[TRY]
Syntax: TRY ... CATCH ... ENDTRY
Description: Begins a block of code with structured error handling.

[TURTLE.BACKWARD]

[TUI.BEGIN]

[TUI.RENDER]

[TUI.LINK]

[TUI.SEPARATOR]

[TUI.SIZE]
