[TUI.SAME_LINE]
Syntax: TUI.SAME_LINE
Description: Join the next emitted element with the previous one in an hbox.

[TUI.BUTTON]
Syntax: TUI.BUTTON(label$) -> bool
Description: A clickable label. Returns TRUE on the frame the focused button is activated with Enter.

[TUI.CHECKBOX]
Syntax: TUI.CHECKBOX(label$, checked) -> int
Description: Toggleable checkbox. Returns the new state (0 or 1).

[TUI.RADIO]
Syntax: TUI.RADIO(label$, options[], selected) -> int
Description: Vertical radio-group. Up/Down cycles when focused; returns the (possibly changed) selection index.

[TUI.INPUT$]
Syntax: TUI.INPUT$(label$, text$, [width]) -> string
Description: Single-line text input. Returns the (edited) text. Type characters / Backspace when focused.

[TUI.INPUT]
Syntax: TUI.INPUT(label$, text$, [width]) -> string
Description: Old name of TUI.INPUT$, still accepted for one release; --lint, jdb_check and -c name TUI.INPUT$, and tools/jdb-fix.jdb rewrites it.

[TUI.INPUT_INT]
Syntax: TUI.INPUT_INT(label$, value, [width]) -> int
Description: Integer input. Digits append, Backspace deletes a digit, Up/Down adjust by 1.

[TUI.INPUT_DOUBLE]
Syntax: TUI.INPUT_DOUBLE(label$, value, [width]) -> double
Description: Double input. Left/Right adjust by 0.1, Up/Down by 1.0.

[TUI.SLIDER]
Syntax: TUI.SLIDER(label$, value, min, max, [step]) -> double
Description: Horizontal slider. Left/Right adjust by step.

[TUI.MENU]
Syntax: TUI.MENU(label$, options[], selected) -> int
Description: Vertical menu list. Like RADIO but without the (*) glyph.

[TUI.DROPDOWN]
Syntax: TUI.DROPDOWN(label$, options[], selected) -> int
Description: Compact single-line option picker. Left/Right cycles.

[TUI.SELECTABLE]
Syntax: TUI.SELECTABLE(label$, selected) -> bool
Description: Row-style clickable item. Returns TRUE the frame Enter fires on it.

[TUI.PROGRESS]
Syntax: TUI.PROGRESS(fraction, [label$])
Description: Horizontal progress bar with optional inline label. Fraction clamped to [0..1].

[TUI.GAUGE]
Syntax: TUI.GAUGE(fraction, [label$])
Description: Same bar as PROGRESS but wrapped in a window/border.

[TUI.SPINNER]
Syntax: TUI.SPINNER(frame, [variant])
Description: One of 22 spinner styles (variant 0-21). `frame` advances the animation.

[TUI.CANVAS_BEGIN]
Syntax: TUI.CANVAS_BEGIN(w, h)
Description: Begin a braille-resolution canvas of width × height cells (2x4 sub-pixels per cell).

[TUI.CANVAS_END]
Syntax: TUI.CANVAS_END
Description: Close the canvas; emits one element replaying every queued LINE/PIXEL.

[TUI.LINE]
Syntax: TUI.LINE(x1, y1, x2, y2, color)
Description: Draw a line on the active canvas. `color` is a Palette16 index (0-15).

[TUI.PIXEL]
Syntax: TUI.PIXEL(x, y, color)
Description: Draw a single point on the active canvas.

[TUI.TABLE_BEGIN]
Syntax: TUI.TABLE_BEGIN(headers[])
Description: Start a table. headers[] seeds row 0 (bold, double-line bottom).

[TUI.TABLE_ROW]
Syntax: TUI.TABLE_ROW(cells[])
Description: Append a row of cells; short rows are padded.

[TUI.TABLE_END]
Syntax: TUI.TABLE_END
Description: Close the table; emits the rendered grid (LIGHT outer border).

[TUI.MODAL_OPEN]
Syntax: TUI.MODAL_OPEN(id$)
Description: Mark a modal as active. The next frame's TUI.MODAL_BEGIN(id$) returns TRUE.

[TUI.MODAL_BEGIN]
Syntax: TUI.MODAL_BEGIN(id$, [title$]) -> bool
Description: Begin a modal body block. Returns TRUE iff this modal is active; only then is MODAL_END expected.

[TUI.MODAL_END]
Syntax: TUI.MODAL_END
Description: Seal the modal body. The overlay is centred over the main frame in TUI.RENDER.

[TUI.MODAL_CLOSE]
Syntax: TUI.MODAL_CLOSE
Description: Clear the active modal (Esc also does this).

[TUI.MENUBAR_BEGIN]
Syntax: TUI.MENUBAR_BEGIN
Description: Begin a horizontal menubar.

[TUI.MENUBAR_END]
Syntax: TUI.MENUBAR_END
Description: Close the menubar; emits the menu row and any popup body.

[TUI.SUBMENU_BEGIN]
Syntax: TUI.SUBMENU_BEGIN(label$) -> bool
Description: Begin a submenu; each gets an implicit F-key (F1, F2, ...). Returns TRUE if currently open.

[TUI.SUBMENU_END]
Syntax: TUI.SUBMENU_END
Description: Close the submenu.

[TUI.MENUITEM]
Syntax: TUI.MENUITEM(label$, [hint$]) -> bool
Description: Menu entry. Returns TRUE the frame Enter fires on it (also closes the menu).

[TUI.TAB_BAR_BEGIN]
Syntax: TUI.TAB_BAR_BEGIN(labels[], active_idx)
Description: Paint a tab strip and set the active tab index.

[TUI.TAB_BAR_END]
Syntax: TUI.TAB_BAR_END
Description: Close the tab bar.

[TUI.TAB_BEGIN]
Syntax: TUI.TAB_BEGIN(label$) -> bool
Description: Begin a tab body. Returns TRUE iff this label matches the active tab; only then is TAB_END expected.

[TUI.TAB_END]
Syntax: TUI.TAB_END
Description: Close the current tab body.

[TUI.COLOR]
Syntax: TUI.COLOR(r, g, b)
Description: Push an RGB foreground colour onto the style stack. Applies to subsequent elements until popped.

[TUI.BG_COLOR]
Syntax: TUI.BG_COLOR(r, g, b)
Description: Push an RGB background colour onto the style stack.

[TUI.POP_COLOR]
Syntax: TUI.POP_COLOR
Description: Pop the top of the style stack.

[TUI.STYLE_PUSH]
Syntax: TUI.STYLE_PUSH(name$)
Description: Push a named style: "bold", "dim", "italic", "underlined", or "inverted".

[TUI.STYLE_POP]
Syntax: TUI.STYLE_POP
Description: Pop the top of the style stack.

[TUI.THEME]
Syntax: TUI.THEME(name$)
Description: Set the title-bar tint: "cool", "warm", "neon", "cyber", or "gold".

[TUI.KEY$]
Syntax: TUI.KEY$
Description: Returns the last drained key name (e.g. "Enter", "Up", "F1", "C-t", " ", "a").

[TUI.MOUSE_X]
Syntax: TUI.MOUSE_X
Description: Mouse column (0-based) at the most recent input poll.

[TUI.MOUSE_Y]
Syntax: TUI.MOUSE_Y
Description: Last seen mouse row.

[TUI.MOUSE_BTN]
Syntax: TUI.MOUSE_BTN
Description: Bitmask of mouse buttons pressed.

[TUI.MOUSE_WHEEL]
Syntax: TUI.MOUSE_WHEEL
Description: Mouse wheel delta accumulator.

[TUI.ON]
Syntax: TUI.ON(event$, handler@)
Description: Register a callback FUNC/SUB as a funcref (record-only for now; dispatch comes with mouse events).

[TUI.WIDTH]
Syntax: TUI.WIDTH
Description: Terminal width in cells (live).

[TUI.HEIGHT]
Syntax: TUI.HEIGHT
Description: Terminal height in cells (live).

[TUI.LAST_RENDER_MS]
Syntax: TUI.LAST_RENDER_MS
Description: Wall-clock milliseconds the previous TUI.RENDER took.

[TUI.VERSION$]
Syntax: TUI.VERSION$
Description: TUI namespace version string.

[TXTREADER$]
TXTREADER$(filename$, [encoding$]) -> string$
Reads the entire contents of a text file into a string. If `encoding$` is given, the file's bytes are decoded from that codepage to UTF-8. Default (no arg / "" / "utf-8") is byte-pass-through; "utf-8-bom" drops a leading byte order mark (TXTWRITER writes one). TXTENCODING$ guesses the right name for a file. Supported: "cp1252"/"windows-1252"/"latin1", "cp850", "cp437", "cp1250", "cp1251", "cp936", "cp932". Codepage decode is Windows-only.

[TXTENCODING$]
TXTENCODING$(filename$) -> string$
Guesses a text file's encoding like Windows Notepad: "utf-8-bom", "utf-16le" or "utf-16be" from a byte order mark or the UTF-16 NUL pattern, "utf-8" for well-formed UTF-8 (ASCII included), otherwise "cp1252". The answer is a name TXTREADER$ and TXTWRITER take, so a file can be opened and saved in its own encoding.

[TXTWRITER]
TXTWRITER filename$, content$, [append], [encoding$]
Writes a string to a text file. The optional 3rd arg `append` (TRUE = append, default FALSE = overwrite). The optional 4th arg `encoding$` re-encodes the UTF-8 jdBasic string to the named codepage on disk; same name set as TXTREADER$. Binary mode, no newline translation. Roundtrip example:
    DIM src$ = TXTREADER$("export.bas", "cp1252")
    TXTWRITER "export.bas", src$, FALSE, "cp1252"

[TYPE]
Syntax: TYPE name ... ENDTYPE
Description: Begins the definition of a user-defined data type (struct).
May contain field declarations, methods (SUB/FUNC), an optional
SUB INIT(params) constructor, and an optional SUB DISPOSE() destructor.

[THIS]
Syntax: THIS.field   |   THIS.Method()   (inside a TYPE method)
Description: Refers to the object instance a method was called on. Only valid inside a SUB or FUNC declared within a TYPE.

[INIT]
Syntax: SUB INIT([params]) ... ENDSUB   (inside TYPE)
Description: Optional constructor for a user-defined type. Runs after
the implicit field defaults whenever an instance is created via
DIM x AS TypeName(args). If INIT takes no parameters, the bare form
DIM x AS TypeName also auto-calls it. For arrays:
DIM arr[N] AS TypeName(vec1, vec2) runs INIT once per slot with
the vectors indexed element-wise.

[DISPOSE]
Syntax: SUB DISPOSE() ... ENDSUB   (inside TYPE)
Description: Optional destructor for a user-defined type. Takes no
parameters. The interpreter calls DISPOSE when the object loses its
last reference (scope exit, reassignment, last copy released). The
native compiler calls DISPOSE for locals at function return and
program end; reassignment does not trigger DISPOSE in native (no
refcount).

[TYPEOF]
Syntax: TYPEOF(variable)
Description: Returns the type name of a value: "INT64", "FLOAT64", "STRING", "BOOLEAN", "ARRAY", "OBJECT" (every map), "DATE", "FUNCREF" or "NONE". There is no "NUMBER"; test numbers with ISNUM or against both INT64 and FLOAT64.

[UCASE$]
Syntax: UCASE$(string$)
Description: Converts a string to uppercase.

[UNIQUE]
Syntax: UNIQUE(array)
Description: Returns a new array containing only the unique elements from the source array.

[UNPACK]
Syntax: UNPACK(format$, binary_data$, [offset]) -> array
Description: Reads binary_data$ from the 0-based offset (default 0) with the PACK$ format codes and returns one element per value. "b" "s" "i" read unsigned, "c" "h" "n" and "l" signed, "f" "d" as doubles, "a" as a string of its count bytes; "x" skips. Data shorter than PACKSIZE(format$) from the offset is an error.
Example: DIM channels = UNPACK("<s", wav$, 22)

[UNREACT]
Syntax: UNREACT(variable_name$)
Description: Removes the reactive properties from a variable.

[UNTIL]
Syntax: DO ... LOOP UNTIL condition
Description: Specifies the condition that will end a DO loop.

[VAL]
Syntax: VAL(string$)
Description: Converts a string to a number: the number at the start of the string. Given a number, it answers that number.

[VARIANCE]
Syntax: VARIANCE(array) or VARIANCE(matrix, dimension) -> number or array
Description: Variance (dispersion) of an array.

[VARS]
Syntax: VARS() -> array
Description: Returns the names of all currently defined global variables.

[VBCRLF]
Syntax: VBCRLF
Description: A constant representing the carriage return and line feed characters (CRLF). VB6-style spelling of VBNEWLINE.

[VBNEWLINE]
Syntax: VBNEWLINE
Description: A constant representing the carriage return and line feed characters (CRLF).

[VBTAB]
Syntax: VBTAB
Description: A constant representing the tab character, CHR$(9).

[WAITKEY$]
Syntax: WAITKEY$()
Description: Blocks execution and waits for one key press, returning it as one character - which is more than one byte for anything past ASCII, so an o-umlaut answers two. A function or arrow key arrives as two calls: CHR$(0) or CHR$(224) first, then the scan code ("H" for arrow-up). While a SCREEN window is open it reads the window's keys and answers the SDL key name, as INKEY$ does.

[WEEKDAY]
Syntax: WEEKDAY(date) -> number
Description: Returns the day of the week (0=Sunday ... 6=Saturday).

[WEND]
Syntax: WHILE condition ... WEND
Description: Ends a WHILE loop. See WHILE.

[WHILE]
Syntax: WHILE condition ... WEND  or  DO WHILE condition ... LOOP
Description: Repeats the loop body as long as the condition is true. WHILE ... WEND and DO WHILE ... LOOP are the same loop; EXITDO and CONTINUEDO work in both.

[XSORT]
Syntax: XSORT(array, [dimension], [descending]) -> array
Description: High-performance sort that can order the rows of a 2D matrix by a chosen column. In mixed arrays numbers order before strings.

[YEAR]
Syntax: YEAR(date) -> number
Description: Extracts the four-digit year from a DateTime.

[YIELD]
YIELD
Pauses execution and yields to the host environment's event loop for one frame.

[ZEROS]
Syntax: ZEROS(shape_vector) -> array
Description: Creates an array of the given shape filled with zeros.

[ZIP]
Syntax: ZIP(arr1, arr2, ...) -> matrix
Description: Combines vectors into a matrix where each row is [arr1[i], arr2[i], ...].

[ZIP.WRITE]
Syntax: ZIP.WRITE(path$, entries)
Description: Writes a map of entry name to content as a ZIP archive. Each entry is deflated when that makes it smaller and the packed bytes read back unchanged, and stored otherwise. Returns the entry count.

[ZIP.READ]
Syntax: ZIP.READ(path$)
Description: Reads a ZIP archive into a map of entry name to content. Handles stored and deflated entries.

[ZIP.LIST]
Syntax: ZIP.LIST(path$)
Description: Returns an array of the entry names in a ZIP archive.

[WAV.WRITE]
Syntax: WAV.WRITE(path$, samples[], [rate=44100], [channels=1]) -> bool
Description: Write interleaved float samples in [-1,1] to a 16-bit PCM WAV file. Needs the FX build flag.

[WAV.READ]
Syntax: WAV.READ(path$) -> { samples, rate, channels, frames } or NONE
Description: Read a WAV into interleaved floats in [-1,1]: frame f channel c is samples[f * channels + c]. Accepts PCM 8/16/24/32-bit, IEEE float 32/64 and WAVE_FORMAT_EXTENSIBLE; unsupported encodings return NONE. Needs the FX build flag.

[WAV.INFO]
Syntax: WAV.INFO(path$) -> { rate, channels, bits, frames } or NONE
Description: Read a WAV header without loading the audio data.

[WAV.RECORD]
Syntax: WAV.RECORD(seconds, [opts{}]) -> { samples, rate, channels, frames } or NONE
Description: Record from a capture device, blocking until the buffer is full. Returns the same map WAV.READ does. opts: channels, rate, device (index into MON.DEVICES().capture), play (samples output while capturing, which switches the device to duplex so both run off one clock), playchannels, playdevice. Needs the MINIAUDIO build flag.

[WAV.RECSTART]
Syntax: WAV.RECSTART([opts{}]) -> bool
Description: Start recording without blocking. Same options as WAV.RECORD, with seconds as the buffer cap (default 60). Needs the MINIAUDIO build flag.

[WAV.RECLEN]
Syntax: WAV.RECLEN() -> seconds
Description: Seconds captured so far by WAV.RECSTART. Needs the MINIAUDIO build flag.

[WAV.RECSTOP]
Syntax: WAV.RECSTOP() -> { samples, rate, channels, frames } or NONE
Description: Stop a recording started with WAV.RECSTART and return it. Needs the MINIAUDIO build flag.

[FX.NEW]
Syntax: FX.NEW() -> chain
Description: Create an empty FX chain and return its handle.

[FX.ADD]
Syntax: FX.ADD(chain, type$, params{}, [bus=0]) -> bool
Description: Append an effect node to a bus (0 = common section, 1 and 2 = the split branches). Types: gain, drive, lowpass, highpass, delay, compressor, cabinet, chorus, flanger, vibrato, phaser, tremolo, fuzz, bitcrush, octave, autowah, noisegate, eq, reverb.

[FX.PROCESS]
Syntax: FX.PROCESS(chain, samples[], [rate=44100], [channels=1]) -> samples[]
Description: Run a mono float buffer through the chain offline; returns the processed buffer. With channels 2 the result is interleaved stereo and a split chain renders both branches into it.

[FX.SET]
Syntax: FX.SET(chain, nodeIndex, param$, value, [bus=0]) -> bool
Description: Live-tweak one existing parameter of a node; race-safe while the chain is monitoring. nodeIndex counts within its own bus.

[FX.SPLIT]
Syntax: FX.SPLIT(chain, on) -> bool
Description: Feed the two branch buses from the common section instead of a single signal path, so one input can drive two separate amps.

[FX.MIX]
Syntax: FX.MIX(chain, bus, level, pan) -> bool
Description: Set level and stereo position of a split branch (bus 1 or 2). pan -1 is hard left, +1 hard right.

[FX.DUMP$]
Syntax: FX.DUMP$(chain) -> string
Description: Readable listing of the chain's nodes and their current parameters.

[FX.FREE]
Syntax: FX.FREE(chain)
Description: Free an FX chain. Use the paren form: FX.FREE(ch).

[MIDI.PORTS]
Syntax: MIDI.PORTS() -> { in:[names], out:[names] }
Description: List available MIDI input and output ports. Needs the MIDI build flag.

[MIDI.OPEN_IN]
Syntax: MIDI.OPEN_IN(portIndex) -> handle or -1
Description: Open a MIDI input port for polling.

[MIDI.OPEN_OUT]
Syntax: MIDI.OPEN_OUT(portIndex) -> handle or -1
Description: Open a MIDI output port for sending.

[MIDI.SEND]
Syntax: MIDI.SEND(handle, status, [data1], [data2]) -> bool
Description: Send a raw MIDI message.

[MIDI.NOTEON]
Syntax: MIDI.NOTEON(handle, channel, note, velocity) -> bool
Description: Send a Note On (channel 0-15).

[MIDI.NOTEOFF]
Syntax: MIDI.NOTEOFF(handle, channel, note) -> bool
Description: Send a Note Off.

[MIDI.CC]
Syntax: MIDI.CC(handle, channel, cc, value) -> bool
Description: Send a Control Change message.

[MIDI.POLL]
Syntax: MIDI.POLL(handle) -> [[status, data1, data2], ...]
Description: Drain buffered incoming MIDI events (lock-free); empty array if none.

[MIDI.CLOSE]
Syntax: MIDI.CLOSE(handle)
Description: Close a MIDI port.

[MON.DEVICES]
Syntax: MON.DEVICES() -> { playback:[names], capture:[names] }
Description: List audio playback and capture devices. Needs the MINIAUDIO build flag.

[MON.BACKEND$]
Syntax: MON.BACKEND$() -> string
Description: The audio backend in use (WASAPI / CoreAudio / ALSA).

[MON.START]
Syntax: MON.START([captureIdx], [playbackIdx]) -> bool
Description: Start live input -> FX -> output monitoring. Use headphones with a line/instrument input.

[MON.STOP]
Syntax: MON.STOP()
Description: Stop live monitoring.

[MON.GAIN]
Syntax: MON.GAIN(g)
Description: Set the monitor output gain, applied lock-free in the audio callback.

[MON.RUNNING]
Syntax: MON.RUNNING() -> bool
Description: Whether live monitoring is currently active.

[MON.FX]
Syntax: MON.FX(chain)
Description: Route the live monitor through an FX chain (0 = bypass). Cabinet nodes are skipped on the live path.

[MON.LEVEL]
Syntax: MON.LEVEL() -> { in, out }
Description: Decaying input/output peak levels for VU metering.

[MON.SCOPE]
Syntax: MON.SCOPE([count=1024]) -> [floats]
Description: The last output samples for an oscilloscope or FFT spectrum.

[MON.PITCH]
Syntax: MON.PITCH() -> Hz
Description: Detected fundamental of the dry input via autocorrelation, or 0 if no clear note.

[MON.RECSTART]
Syntax: MON.RECSTART() -> bool
Description: Start tapping the wet output into the record buffer (up to 3 minutes).

[MON.RECSTOP]
Syntax: MON.RECSTOP(path$) -> seconds
Description: Stop recording and save a 16-bit mono 48k WAV; returns seconds written.

[MON.RECLEN]
Syntax: MON.RECLEN() -> seconds
Description: Seconds captured so far (for a recording indicator).

[FORM.CREATE]
Syntax: FORM.CREATE(title$, width, height, [name$]) -> handle
Description: Create a native Windows form (Win32 window). Events fire as NAME_LOAD, NAME_UNLOAD, NAME_RESIZE. Needs the FORMS build flag.

[FORM.BUTTON]
Syntax: FORM.BUTTON(frm, name$, caption$, x, y, w, h) -> handle
Description: Add a push button. Fires NAME_CLICK.

[FORM.LABEL]
Syntax: FORM.LABEL(frm, name$, caption$, x, y, w, h) -> handle
Description: Add a static text label.

[FORM.TEXTBOX]
Syntax: FORM.TEXTBOX(frm, name$, text$, x, y, w, h, [multiline]) -> handle
Description: Add an edit control. Fires NAME_CHANGE on every text change.

[FORM.CHECKBOX]
Syntax: FORM.CHECKBOX(frm, name$, caption$, x, y, w, h) -> handle
Description: Add a checkbox. Fires NAME_CLICK; read the state with FORM.GET(h, "CHECKED").

[FORM.RADIO]
Syntax: FORM.RADIO(frm, name$, caption$, x, y, w, h, [new_group]) -> handle
Description: Add a radio button; new_group=TRUE starts a new exclusive group. Fires NAME_CLICK.

[FORM.FRAME]
Syntax: FORM.FRAME(frm, name$, caption$, x, y, w, h) -> handle
Description: Add a group box frame.

[FORM.LISTBOX]
Syntax: FORM.LISTBOX(frm, name$, x, y, w, h) -> handle
Description: Add a list box. Fires NAME_CLICK on selection and NAME_DBLCLICK on double click.

[FORM.COMBO]
Syntax: FORM.COMBO(frm, name$, x, y, w, h) -> handle
Description: Add a drop-down combo box. Fires NAME_CHANGE on selection.

[FORM.TIMER]
Syntax: FORM.TIMER(frm, name$, interval_ms) -> handle
Description: Add a timer that fires NAME_TICK every interval_ms; 0 creates it disabled. Change with FORM.SET(h, "INTERVAL", ms).

[FORM.PAGESETUP]
Syntax: FORM.PAGESETUP() -> bool
Description: Page setup dialog (paper, orientation, margins); the choice is kept for FORM.PRINT. FALSE when cancelled.

[FORM.PRINT]
Syntax: FORM.PRINT(text$, [title$], [font], [printer$], [outfile$]) -> bool
Description: Prints plain text like Notepad: page setup margins, title$ centred on top, "Page n" at the bottom, long lines wrapped, tabs every 8 columns; font is a FONT-style map (default Consolas 10). Without printer$ the print dialog asks first (cancel answers FALSE); with it the job goes straight to that printer and outfile$ names the file for one that writes files, e.g. "Microsoft Print to PDF".

[FORM.SET]
Syntax: FORM.SET(handle, prop$, value)
Description: Set a property: TEXT, ENABLED, VISIBLE, CHECKED, ITEMS (array), ADDITEM, CLEAR, SELINDEX, FOCUS, X, Y, WIDTH, HEIGHT, INTERVAL (timer), VALUE (TRUE clicks a button), BORDERSTYLE (forms: 0 none, 1 fixed single, 2 sizable, 3 fixed dialog, 4 fixed tool window, 5 sizable tool window; client size kept), OWNER (forms: owning form handle or 0; an owned form stays above its owner and has no taskbar button), DROPFILES (TRUE accepts files dropped from Explorer; fires NAME_DROPFILES with files = array of paths, x, y). Appearance and behaviour: FORECOLOR, BACKCOLOR (0xRRGGBB; a form paints its own background with BACKCOLOR, a themed push button ignores both), FONT (map of name/size/bold/italic/underline/strike, absent keys stay at the system UI font), TAG (any value, the VB6 scratch slot), TOOLTIP, ALIGN (LEFT/CENTER/RIGHT, labels and edit fields), MAXLENGTH, PASSWORD (a character, TRUE for *, FALSE to undo), LOCKED, TABSTOP, TABINDEX (moves the control to that position in the tab order), CURSOR (ARROW/WAIT/HAND/IBEAM/CROSS/SIZEALL/NO). FONT, ALIGN, CURSOR, PASSWORD and TABINDEX are set-only. Edit fields (TEXTBOX, RICHTEXT): SELSTART, SELLENGTH (UTF-8 byte offsets into TEXT, the units of INSTR/MID$), SELTEXT (replaces the selection, undoable), MODIFIED, and the set-only actions UNDO, CUT, COPY, PASTE (TRUE runs them); WORDWRAP (multiline TEXTBOX; FALSE adds a horizontal scrollbar, the control is rebuilt under the same handle), HIDESELECTION (default TRUE; FALSE keeps the selection visible without focus, e.g. behind a Find dialog), ACCEPTSTAB (Tab types a tab), TABWIDTH (characters). RICHTEXT also: PLAINTEXT, REDO, ZOOM (percent), SPELLCHECK. Forms: DARKMODE (dark caption and scroll bars).

[FORM.GET]
Syntax: FORM.GET(handle, prop$) -> value
Description: Read a property: TEXT, BORDERSTYLE, OWNER, ENABLED, VISIBLE, CHECKED, SELINDEX, SELTEXT, COUNT, NAME, KIND, HWND, X, Y, WIDTH, HEIGHT, FORECOLOR, BACKCOLOR (-1 when never set), TAG (NONE when never set), TOOLTIP, MAXLENGTH, LOCKED, TABSTOP. DROPFILES. Edit fields also: SELSTART, SELLENGTH, SELTEXT, MODIFIED, CANUNDO, WORDWRAP, HIDESELECTION, LINECOUNT, CARETLINE and CARETCOL (1-based, at the end of the selection, lines of the text), ACCEPTSTAB, TABWIDTH; RICHTEXT also PLAINTEXT, CANREDO, ZOOM, SPELLCHECK; forms DARKMODE.

[FORM.RUN]
Syntax: FORM.RUN(frm)
Description: Show the form and run the message loop until every form is closed. Fires NAME_LOAD first; handlers run on the main thread. Forms fire LOAD, UNLOAD, RESIZE and the mouse events; every control that takes input fires GOTFOCUS, LOSTFOCUS, KEYDOWN, KEYUP, KEYPRESS, MOUSEDOWN, MOUSEUP and MOUSEMOVE on top of its own (CLICK, CHANGE, DBLCLICK, TICK). Keyboard events carry key (the virtual key, or the character for KEYPRESS), mouse events button (1 left, 2 right, 0 for a move) and x/y in logical units; both carry shift, ctrl and alt. All bind by name without an ON.

[FORM.SHOW]
Syntax: FORM.SHOW(frm)
Description: Show a (secondary) form without blocking and fire its NAME_LOAD event.

[FORM.DOEVENTS]
Syntax: FORM.DOEVENTS() -> bool
Description: Pump pending window messages once; TRUE while any form is open. For DO...LOOP style programs instead of FORM.RUN.

[FORM.CLOSE]
Syntax: FORM.CLOSE(frm)
Description: Close a form. When the last form closes, FORM.RUN returns. NAME_UNLOAD runs synchronously while the window still exists, so the handler can read its own controls one last time and can call the close off with e[0]{"cancel"} = TRUE (the VB6 Form_QueryUnload pattern) for the window cross, Alt+F4 and FORM.CLOSE alike.

[MSGBOX]
Syntax: MSGBOX(text$, [flags], [title$]) -> button
Description: Show a message box. Flags follow VB6/Win32: 1=OKCancel 4=YesNo 16=Critical 32=Question 48=Exclamation 64=Information. Returns 1=OK 2=Cancel 6=Yes 7=No.

[INPUTBOX$]
Syntax: INPUTBOX$(prompt$, [title$], [default$]) -> string
Description: Modal text input dialog. Returns the entered text, or "" on Cancel.

[FORM.LOAD]
Syntax: FORM.LOAD(path$) -> handle
Description: Instantiate a .jdform file (JSON layout) and auto-bind every SUB named CONTROL_EVENT in the program. Relative paths resolve against the script directory.

[FORM.FIND]
Syntax: FORM.FIND(frm, name$) -> handle
Description: Look up a control of a form by name (case-insensitive); 0 if absent. Companion to FORM.LOAD for code-behind property access.

[FORM.MENU]
Syntax: FORM.MENU(frm, spec)
Description: Build or replace the form's menu bar. Spec = array of maps: text (& = Alt key, "-" = separator), items (submenu), name (clickable -> NAME_CLICK), key ("Ctrl+O", "F5"; a real accelerator). Items support FORM.SET ENABLED/CHECKED/TEXT/VALUE.

[FORM.POPUP]
Syntax: FORM.POPUP(frm, spec, [x], [y])
Description: Show a context menu at the mouse, or at logical form coordinates when x/y are given, and return when it closes. Spec has the same shape as FORM.MENU, and a chosen item dispatches its NAME_CLICK exactly like a menu-bar item. The handles from the form's previous popup are dropped on each call. Pairs with NAME_MOUSEDOWN and button = 2.

[FORM.MDI]
Syntax: FORM.MDI(title$, width, height, [name$]) -> handle
Description: Create an MDI frame window (multi-document parent). Combine with FORM.MENU and FORM.CHILD; run with FORM.RUN.

[FORM.CHILD]
Syntax: FORM.CHILD(frame, title$, width, height, [name$]) -> handle
Description: Create an MDI child document inside a frame. Hosts controls like a form; closing children never ends the program, closing the frame does.

[FORM.TOOLBAR]
Syntax: FORM.TOOLBAR(frm, name$, spec) -> handle
Description: Flat icon toolbar along the top (one per form). Spec = array of maps: name (-> NAME_CLICK), text (tooltip), icon (NEW/OPEN/SAVE/CUT/COPY/PASTE/UNDO/REDO/DELETE/PRINT/FIND/REPLACE/PROPERTIES/HELP), check (toggle); "-" = separator. Buttons take FORM.SET ENABLED/CHECKED/VALUE.

[FORM.STATUSBAR]
Syntax: FORM.STATUSBAR(frm, name$, [part_widths]) -> handle
Description: Status bar along the bottom (one per form). part_widths = array of logical widths, -1 stretches the last part; omitted = one part. SET TEXT takes a string (part 0) or an array (all parts).

[FORM.LINE]
Syntax: FORM.LINE(frm, name$, x, y, length, [vertical]) -> handle
Description: Etched divider line, horizontal by default.

[FORM.SHAPE]
Syntax: FORM.SHAPE(frm, name$, x, y, w, h, [rgb]) -> handle
Description: Filled rectangle. COLOR property (0xRRGGBB) via FORM.SET/GET.

[FORM.PICTURE]
Syntax: FORM.PICTURE(frm, name$, path$, x, y, w, h) -> handle
Description: Image control (PNG/JPG/BMP/GIF), scaled to the control. Swap via FORM.SET PICTURE.

[FORM.PROGRESS]
Syntax: FORM.PROGRESS(frm, name$, x, y, w, h) -> handle
Description: Progress bar; VALUE and MAX properties (default 0..100).

[FORM.SLIDER]
Syntax: FORM.SLIDER(frm, name$, x, y, w, h, [max], [vertical]) -> handle
Description: Trackbar; VALUE/MIN/MAX; fires NAME_CHANGE with value while dragging.

[FORM.UPDOWN]
Syntax: FORM.UPDOWN(frm, name$, x, y, w, h, [min], [max]) -> handle
Description: Numeric edit with spin arrows; VALUE/MIN/MAX/TEXT; fires NAME_CHANGE.

[FORM.LISTVIEW]
Syntax: FORM.LISTVIEW(frm, name$, x, y, w, h) -> handle
Description: Report list with columns and grid lines. COLUMNS (array of maps or strings), ITEMS (array of row-arrays), ADDITEM, CLEAR, SELINDEX, SELTEXT, COUNT; cells via FORM.GET(h, "CELL", row, col). Fires NAME_CLICK/NAME_DBLCLICK.

[FORM.TREEVIEW]
Syntax: FORM.TREEVIEW(frm, name$, x, y, w, h) -> handle
Description: Hierarchy control; add nodes with FORM.NODE. SELNODE/SELTEXT/COUNT/EXPAND/CLEAR; fires NAME_CLICK on selection change.

[FORM.NODE]
Syntax: FORM.NODE(tree, parent, text$) -> node
Description: Insert a tree node under parent (0 = root level); returns the node id.

[FORM.TABS]
Syntax: FORM.TABS(frm, name$, x, y, w, h, titles) -> handle
Description: Tab strip from an array of titles. Assign controls to pages with FORM.TABPAGE; SELINDEX/COUNT; fires NAME_CHANGE.

[FORM.TABPAGE]
Syntax: FORM.TABPAGE(tab, page, ctl)
Description: Put a control on a tab page; its visibility follows the selected tab.

[FORM.DATETIME]
Syntax: FORM.DATETIME(frm, name$, x, y, w, h) -> handle
Description: Date picker. VALUE is an epoch (use CVDATE/YEAR/MONTH/DAY); fires NAME_CHANGE.

[FORM.RICHTEXT]
Syntax: FORM.RICHTEXT(frm, name$, x, y, w, h) -> handle
Description: Rich-edit box; TEXT get/set; fires NAME_CHANGE.

[FILEOPEN$]
Syntax: FILEOPEN$([filter$], [title$], [initial_dir$]) -> path
Description: Open-file dialog. Filter "Text files|*.txt|All files|*.*"; returns "" on cancel.

[FILESAVE$]
Syntax: FILESAVE$([filter$], [title$], [default_name$]) -> path
Description: Save-file dialog with overwrite prompt; returns "" on cancel.

[COLORDIALOG]
Syntax: COLORDIALOG([initial_rgb]) -> rgb
Description: Color picker; returns 0xRRGGBB, or -1 on cancel.

[FONTDIALOG$]
Syntax: FONTDIALOG$([face$], [size]) -> "face,size,bold,italic"
Description: Font picker; returns "" on cancel.

[FORM.TOPMOST]
Syntax: FORM.SET(frm, "TOPMOST", bool)
Description: Keep a form above all normal windows (always on top); FALSE releases it. FORM.GET reads the state.

[??]
Syntax: expression ?? expression
Description: The left side unless it is absent, in which case the right. Asks about absence, not truth, so 0 and "" keep their place where ORELSE would replace them. The right side is only evaluated when it is needed, and a chain of fallbacks may be written as a chain. Both backends.

[?.]
Syntax: object?.field | object?{key} | object?[index]
Description: Reads into something that may not be there. A missing map key already reads as NONE; it is the step after that faults, and this guards it: with nothing to read into, the read does not happen and the answer is absent, so the chain stops. Not a bounds check: an index out of range is still an error. Not allowed before a method call.

[$"]
Syntax: $"text {{ expression }} text"
Description: A string with expressions in it, using the same {{ }} the template engine speaks. Single braces and angle brackets stay text, which is what building JSON and HTML need. Inside, the ordinary string rules hold, so a quote is doubled: $"{{m{""key""}}}". Becomes text + FORMAT$("{}", expr) + text at parse time, so it compiles exactly as it interprets.

[OPTIONAL PARAMETERS]
Syntax: FUNC Name(required, optional = default) ... ENDFUNC
Description: A trailing parameter may carry a default, and a call that leaves it out gets that value. Optional parameters come last, because arguments are matched left to right. A default is a literal (a number, a string, TRUE or FALSE), since a function is declared before any scope exists to evaluate one in. NONE is not one: it reads as absent only because an undeclared name does, which the interpreter allows and -c refuses. For a computed default pick a value the caller would never pass and decide in the body. SUB takes them too, lambdas do not.

[GPIO.MODE]
Syntax: GPIO.MODE(pin, is_output)
Description: Sets a pin to output (1) or input (0). Boards only. On the ESP32-S3 the pins carrying flash (26-32), PSRAM (33-37) and the console UART are refused by name before the write, because touching one takes the board down with no diagnostic; PIN.FREE lists what is left.

[GPIO.WRITE]
Syntax: GPIO.WRITE(pin, level)
Description: Drives an output pin high (non-zero) or low. Boards only.

[GPIO.READ]
Syntax: GPIO.READ(pin) -> 0 | 1
Description: Reads an input pin. Boards only.

[GPIO.PULLUP]
Syntax: GPIO.PULLUP(pin [, on])
Description: Enables (default) or releases the pin's internal pull-up. Boards only.

[GPIO.WATCH]
Syntax: GPIO.WATCH(pin, edge)
Description: Raises the "PIN" event on a pin edge: 1 rising, 2 falling, 3 both, 0 stops watching. Use with ON "PIN" CALL Handler: the SUB takes one array d, with d[0] the pin and d[1] the level. The interrupt only records; the handler runs between statements. Boards only.

[PIN.DIAG$]
Syntax: PIN.DIAG$ -> text$
Description: What the pin interrupt has seen so far: raw count and queue positions. Boards only.

[PIN.FREE]
Syntax: PIN.FREE -> text$
Description: The GPIO numbers this build will let you use, with flash, PSRAM and the console pins left out. ESP32-S3 only.

[ADC.READ]
Syntax: ADC.READ(pin) -> raw
Description: One analogue conversion. On the ESP32-S3 the converter sits on GPIO 1 to 10 in order, so the argument is the pin; on the RP2350 it is the channel. Boards only.

[ADC.TEMP]
Syntax: ADC.TEMP -> degrees
Description: The chip's own temperature sensor, in degrees Celsius. Boards only.

[PWM.SET]
Syntax: PWM.SET(pin, hz [, duty_percent])
Description: A square wave on a pin, duty in percent (default 50). Eight channels, handed out per pin in order of first use. Boards only.

[PWM.OFF]
Syntax: PWM.OFF(pin)
Description: Stops the wave and frees the channel. Boards only.

[I2C.SETUP]
Syntax: I2C.SETUP(bus, sda, scl [, hz])
Description: Opens an I2C bus (0 or 1) on two pins. On the ESP32-S3 the speed belongs to the device rather than the bus, so it is named at the transfer instead. Boards only.

[I2C.WRITE]
Syntax: I2C.WRITE(bus, address, data [, hz]) -> bytes_written
Description: Writes an array of byte values or a string to a device. Returns the count, or -1. Boards only.

[I2C.READ]
Syntax: I2C.READ(bus, address, count [, hz]) -> array
Description: Reads count bytes from a device. Returns an empty array on failure. Boards only.

[I2C.SCAN]
Syntax: I2C.SCAN(bus) -> array
Description: The addresses that answered on the bus. Boards only.

[SPI.SETUP]
Syntax: SPI.SETUP(bus, sck, mosi, miso [, hz])
Description: Opens an SPI bus. Chip select is left alone: drive it with GPIO.WRITE, which is what a display or a card needs anyway. Boards only.

[SPI.XFER]
Syntax: SPI.XFER(bus, data) -> array
Description: Full duplex: as many bytes come back as went out. Takes an array of byte values or a string. Boards only.

[TIMER.EVERY]
Syntax: TIMER.EVERY(ms) -> 0 | -1
Description: Raises the "TICK" event every ms milliseconds; 0 stops. Use with ON "TICK" CALL Handler. Handlers run between statements, never inside the interrupt, and do not nest: a tick arriving while one is still running is dropped rather than queued, so a slow handler cannot build a backlog. Boards only.

[TIMER.STOP]
Syntax: TIMER.STOP
Description: Stops the periodic tick. Boards only.

[KEY.WATCH]
Syntax: KEY.WATCH(on)
Description: Raises the "KEY" event for each key that arrives. Use with ON "KEY" CALL Handler: the SUB takes one array d, with d[0] the key code. Boards only.

[SYS.FREE]
Syntax: SYS.FREE -> bytes
Description: Free heap. It is the total across scattered pieces, so it is not what a single allocation can have; watch SYS.LARGEST for that. Boards only.

[SYS.LARGEST]
Syntax: SYS.LARGEST -> bytes
Description: The biggest single block the heap will hand over. A growing array asks for one of these, and a heap holding plenty in scattered pieces still says no, which is what a program hits long before the total runs out. Boards only.

[SYS.INTERNAL]
Syntax: SYS.INTERNAL -> bytes
Description: Free internal RAM, the scarce pool. ESP32-S3 only.

[SYS.PSRAM]
Syntax: SYS.PSRAM -> bytes
Description: The PSRAM this board has. Zero on a part without it. On the ESP32-S3 it is free PSRAM, and arrays and programs live there. On the Fruit Jam it is the size mapped on the QMI bus, which is not yet part of the heap: the window can be read and written directly, but malloc still hands out SRAM.

[SYS.MEM]
Syntax: SYS.MEM -> text$
Description: Both pools with their totals and largest blocks, plus the low-water mark: the smallest the heap has been since boot, which is what a program actually survived rather than what it happens to hold now. ESP32-S3 only.

[SYS.CHUNKS]
Syntax: SYS.CHUNKS -> text$
Description: Where the memory a loaded program never gives back actually went, component by component: code, line table, names, constants, inline caches, prototypes, and the slack the vectors keep. RP2350 only.

[SYS.NATIVES]
Syntax: SYS.NATIVES -> text$
Description: How many builtins this build registered, how many bytes of name that is, and what registering them cost. ESP32-S3 only.

[SYS.DF$]
Syntax: SYS.DF$([path$]) -> text$
Description: The volume a path lies on as a line: bytes free of bytes total. Without a path, the working directory volume. On a board it answers for the flash store and takes no argument.

[SYS.DF]
Syntax: SYS.DF([path$]) -> text$
Description: Old name of SYS.DF$, still accepted for one release; --lint, jdb_check and -c name SYS.DF$, and tools/jdb-fix.jdb rewrites it.

[SYS.FREEDISK]
Syntax: SYS.FREEDISK([path$]) -> bytes
Description: Free space on the volume a path lies on, as a number of bytes. Without a path, the working directory volume. The number is what this user may still write, which on a volume with quotas is less than the volume free space. On a board it answers for the flash store and takes no argument.

[SYS.HEAP]
Syntax: SYS.HEAP() -> bytes
Description: Bytes the C heap holds for the process right now, both backends, the runtime DLL and the libraries together. Read it after N and after 3N passes of the same work; a figure that grows with the passes is a leak. Windows, Linux (glibc 2.33+) and macOS.

[SYS.MEMORY]
Syntax: SYS.MEMORY() -> map
Description: The physical memory of the machine in bytes: "total", and "free" for what programs can still have without the system swapping. Windows, Linux and macOS.

[WIFI.AP]
Syntax: WIFI.AP(ssid$ [, password$ [, channel]]) -> 0 | -1
Description: Raises the board's own network on 192.168.4.1 with a DHCP server behind it. Open with no password, WPA2 with one of at least eight characters. ESP32-S3 only.

[WIFI.CONNECT]
Syntax: WIFI.CONNECT(ssid$, password$ [, timeout_ms]) -> 0 | negative
Description: Joins a network and waits for an address. Zero on success. Boards only.

[WIFI.AUTO]
Syntax: WIFI.AUTO -> 0 | negative
Description: Joins using the two lines in wifi.txt on the flash store: ssid, then password. Boards only.

[WIFI.OFF]
Syntax: WIFI.OFF
Description: Stops the radio and gives its memory back. A started radio costs most of what the interpreter has, so it is a mode rather than a state. ESP32-S3 and Fruit Jam; on the Fruit Jam it disconnects from the network.

[WIFI.STATUS]
Syntax: WIFI.STATUS -> code
Description: The state of the radio. The codes differ by board. ESP32-S3: 0 down, 1 serving as an access point, 2 joined with an address. RP2350 W boards: the radio chip's link status, 3 joined with an address, 0 down, 1 joining, 2 joined without an address, negative a failure. Fruit Jam: the radio firmware's status, 3 connected. Boards with a radio only.

[WIFI.IP$]
Syntax: WIFI.IP$ -> text$
Description: The address of whichever interface is carrying traffic, or "". Boards only.

[WIFI.MAC$]
Syntax: WIFI.MAC$ -> text$
Description: The hardware address of the interface in use. ESP32-S3 only.

[WIFI.CLIENTS]
Syntax: WIFI.CLIENTS -> count
Description: How many stations are connected to this board's own network. ESP32-S3 only.

[WIFI.DIAG$]
Syntax: WIFI.DIAG$ -> text$
Description: Mode, network, address, and either the signal strength or the number of clients. Boards only.
[BEEP]
Syntax: BEEP [freq [, ms]]
Description: A tone for a while, then silence. Boards only. Defaults to 880 Hz for 200 ms. The program keeps running; the note ends on its own.

[TONE]
Syntax: TONE(freq)
Description: A tone held until told otherwise. Boards only. TONE 0 stops it, as does PLAY.STOP.

[PLAY]
Syntax: PLAY(score$)
Description: A melody in the background, in the classic BASIC notation. Boards only. A-G with # or + for sharp and - for flat, O<n> for the octave and < > to step it, L<n> for the default length (4 is a quarter note), T<n> for the tempo in quarter notes per minute, P or R for a rest, and . after a note to hold it half again as long. The program keeps running while it sounds; PLAY.BUSY says whether it still is.

[PLAY.STOP]
Syntax: PLAY.STOP
Description: Stops a score or a held tone. Boards only.

[PLAY.BUSY]
Syntax: PLAY.BUSY
Description: TRUE while a score is still sounding. Boards only.

[PLAY.VOLUME]
Syntax: PLAY.VOLUME(pct)
Description: Loudness from 0 to 100. Boards only.

[GFX.CLEAR]
Syntax: GFX.CLEAR [r, g, b]
Description: Fills the whole panel, black without a colour. Boards with a panel only. Writes the framebuffer; SCREENFLIP puts it on the glass.

[GFX.LIGHT]
Syntax: GFX.LIGHT(on)
Description: The panel backlight. Boards with a panel only.

[GFX.WIDTH]
Syntax: GFX.WIDTH
Description: The panel width in pixels. Boards with a panel only.

[GFX.HEIGHT]
Syntax: GFX.HEIGHT
Description: The panel height in pixels. Boards with a panel only.

[GFX.CONSOLE]
Syntax: GFX.CONSOLE(on)
Description: Turns the panel into a text console, or gives it back to a program that wants to draw. Boards with a panel only. While it is on, everything printed goes to both the serial line and the glass. On the ES3C28P it starts with the board unless CONSOLE OFF said otherwise at the prompt.

[GFX.CONSIZE]
Syntax: GFX.CONSIZE
Description: The console as [columns, rows]. Boards with a panel only. 40 by 30 on the 2.8 inch board.

[GFX.PEEK]
Syntax: GFX.PEEK(x, y)
Description: What the framebuffer holds at a point, as [r, g, b]. Boards with a screen only, and empty outside it. This asks the memory rather than the glass, which on a panel board is a real distinction; GFX.READBACK asks the glass there. On the Fruit Jam the two are the same thing, because the framebuffer is what the wire is reading.

[GFX.READBACK]
Syntax: GFX.READBACK(x, y)
Description: What the panel itself holds at a point, as [r, g, b], read back over its own wire. Boards with a panel only. Agrees with GFX.PEEK to within the quantisation between the framebuffer's 5-6-5 and the panel's 6-6-6.

[GFX.PANELSTATE]
Syntax: GFX.PANELSTATE
Description: What the panel says about itself, as [power_mode, awake, displaying]. Boards with a panel only. A live ILI9341 reports 156, which is booster on, sleep out, normal mode and display on.

[GFX.PANELREG]
Syntax: GFX.PANELREG(cmd [, n])
Description: The raw bytes a panel read command answers with, up to eight. Boards with a panel only. For finding out what a wire is carrying when a value looks wrong, rather than reasoning about the protocol.

[GFX.PANELREGAT]
Syntax: GFX.PANELREGAT(cmd, x, y [, n])
Description: The same as GFX.PANELREG, after pointing the panel at one pixel. Boards with a panel only.

[GFX.DIAG]
Syntax: GFX.DIAG
Description: What the panel transport did, as [transfers, failures, last_error]. Boards with a panel only. A driver that discards its return codes cannot tell "the panel ignored us" from "nothing was ever sent".

[TOUCH]
Syntax: TOUCH
Description: The touch screen as [count, x, y] in screen coordinates. Boards with a touch panel only. Count is 0 when nothing is touching, and x and y are -1 then.

[TOUCH.RAW]
Syntax: TOUCH.RAW
Description: The touch controller's own numbers, before the mapping to screen coordinates. Boards with a touch panel only. The controller reports in the panel's native orientation, which is not the screen's.

[TOUCH.ID]
Syntax: TOUCH.ID
Description: The touch controller's identity as [chip, vendor, 0]. Boards with a touch panel only. A FocalTech FT6336 answers 100 and 17.

[MIC]
Syntax: MIC([ms])
Description: The microphone over a window in milliseconds, as [peak, mean], both 0 to 100. Boards with a microphone only. Peak says whether something happened, mean how loud it is now: a clap detector wants the first, a level meter the second.

[MIC.GAIN]
Syntax: MIC.GAIN(step)
Description: Microphone gain, 0 to 7 in steps of six decibels. Boards with a microphone only.

[SD.MOUNT]
Syntax: SD.MOUNT
Description: Mounts the card and answers its size in megabytes. Boards with a card slot only. It appears at /sd; a bare name still means the flash store. A card that will not mount is not formatted.

[SD.UNMOUNT]
Syntax: SD.UNMOUNT
Description: Lets go of the card. Boards with a card slot only.

[SD.INFO]
Syntax: SD.INFO
Description: The mounted card as [name$, megabytes, bus_width]. Boards with a card slot only. Four is the width this slot is wired for.

[LINE]
Syntax: LINE x1, y1, x2, y2 [, r, g, b]
Description: A straight line between two points. The colour is optional and, when given, stays in force for later drawing the way DRAWCOLOR does.

[GFX.PALETTE]
Syntax: GFX.PALETTE(index, r, g, b)
Description: Sets one of the sixteen palette entries a buffered screen draws through. Boards only.

[GFX.BUFFER]
Syntax: GFX.BUFFER(x, y, w, h) -> bytes | GFX.BUFFER(0)
Description: Keeps that rectangle in memory at four bits a pixel, so drawing goes to RAM and SCREENFLIP sends only what changed. Answers with the bytes it took, or -1 if there was no room. GFX.BUFFER(0) gives it back. RP2350 with a panel only; a whole 320 by 320 screen is 51 KB, so check SYS.LARGEST first.

[GFX.BUFFERED]
Syntax: GFX.BUFFERED -> TRUE | FALSE
Description: Whether a buffer is being held. Boards with a panel only.

[LED]
Syntax: LED(on)
Description: The board's own LED. RP2350 only. On a W board it hangs off the radio chip, so it needs the radio started.

[KEY.GET]
Syntax: KEY.GET -> code
Description: One key code from the console, waiting for one if none has arrived. Boards only. The codes are the PicoCalc keyboard controller's: ESC is 177 and the arrows are 180 to 183, and a terminal's escape sequences fold into the same values.

[KBD.RAW$]
Syntax: KBD.RAW$ -> text$
Description: What the keyboard controller actually sent, byte for byte. PicoCalc only, for when a key does not arrive as expected.

[KBD.LAYOUT]
Syntax: KBD.LAYOUT [(layout$)] -> text$
Description: The keyboard layout, US or DE, and with an argument it sets it. Fruit Jam only. German swaps y and z, the digit row and the punctuation. It starts as US at every power-on, so a program calling KBD.LAYOUT with DE behind AUTORUN is what makes it stick.

[LCD.STAT$]
Syntax: LCD.STAT$ -> text$
Description: The panel's scroll offset and cursor position. PicoCalc only.

[LCD.ROW$]
Syntax: LCD.ROW$(y) -> text$
Description: One row of the text console as it stands on the glass. PicoCalc only.

[LCD.TAP$]
Syntax: LCD.TAP$ -> text$
Description: The bytes the display bus last carried. PicoCalc only.

[LCD.TAPARM]
Syntax: LCD.TAPARM -> count
Description: Arms the display-bus tap for the next transfer. PicoCalc only.

[BUTTON.GET]
Syntax: BUTTON.GET(n) -> TRUE | FALSE
Description: Whether button n is held down. Fruit Jam only, where 1 is the BOOT button and 2 and 3 are the pair beside it. BOOT is only a boot function while the chip is coming up; afterwards it is an ordinary button.

[BUTTON.COUNT]
Syntax: BUTTON.COUNT -> count
Description: How many buttons this board has. Fruit Jam only.

[NEOPIXEL.SET]
Syntax: NEOPIXEL.SET(index, r, g, b)
Description: Sets one addressable LED. Fruit Jam only. Nothing reaches the strip until NEOPIXEL.SHOW, so a whole pattern arrives at once rather than crawling across.

[NEOPIXEL.SHOW]
Syntax: NEOPIXEL.SHOW
Description: Sends what NEOPIXEL.SET has set. Fruit Jam only.

[NEOPIXEL.CLEAR]
Syntax: NEOPIXEL.CLEAR
Description: All of them off, and sends it. Fruit Jam only.

[NEOPIXEL.COUNT]
Syntax: NEOPIXEL.COUNT -> count
Description: How many LEDs the strip has. Fruit Jam only; five on this board.

[IR.RAW]
Syntax: IR.RAW -> 0 | 1
Description: The infrared receiver's pin as it stands. Fruit Jam only. This is the raw level, not a decoded command: a remote's carrier shows as the pin going busy.

[SND.OUT]
Syntax: SND.OUT(to_speaker)
Description: Routes the codec to the speaker amplifier (1) or the headphone jack (0). Fruit Jam only. The routing bits carry one or the other, never both.

[SND.PROBE]
Syntax: SND.PROBE -> text$
Description: What the codec answers on the I2C bus, register by register. Fruit Jam only.

[SND.STAT]
Syntax: SND.STAT -> text$
Description: The converter's own status flags: powered, running, and what it thinks it is being fed. Fruit Jam only.

[SND.PINS]
Syntax: SND.PINS -> text$
Description: The state of the three I2S pins and the rate the state machine is clocking them at. Fruit Jam only, for telling a line that carries nothing from one that carries something nobody hears.

[USB.START]
Syntax: USB.START -> TRUE | FALSE
Description: Brings the USB host up if it is not already running. Fruit Jam only; it starts with the board, so this is for after a USB verb says it did not.

[USB.KEYBOARDS]
Syntax: USB.KEYBOARDS -> count
Description: How many keyboards have enumerated. Fruit Jam only.

[USB.DEVICES]
Syntax: USB.DEVICES -> count
Description: How many USB devices of any kind have enumerated. Fruit Jam only.

[USB.KEYS]
Syntax: USB.KEYS -> count
Description: How many keystrokes the host has delivered since boot. Fruit Jam only.

[USB.PENDING]
Syntax: USB.PENDING -> TRUE | FALSE
Description: Whether a keystroke is waiting to be read. Fruit Jam only.

[DVI.FRAMES]
Syntax: DVI.FRAMES -> count
Description: Completed fields since boot. Fruit Jam only. A program can measure what drawing costs by watching how many go by, and a count that stops moving says the signal has.

[DVI.FRAMEUS]
Syntax: DVI.FRAMEUS -> microseconds
Description: How long the last field took. Fruit Jam only. 16666 is 60 Hz exactly.

[DVI.IRQS]
Syntax: DVI.IRQS -> count
Description: How often the scanout interrupt has run. Fruit Jam only. One per field; more than that means the command list is restarting early.

[DVI.CLOCK]
Syntax: DVI.CLOCK -> hertz
Description: The HSTX serialiser clock. Fruit Jam only. 480p60 needs exactly 126 MHz, because the serialiser puts out two bits a cycle.

[DVI.DIAG$]
Syntax: DVI.DIAG$ -> text$
Description: The scanout's registers in one line: the two HSTX words, the DMA control word, and both clocks as the counter measured them rather than as they were asked for. Fruit Jam only.

[SYS.CLOCK]
Syntax: SYS.CLOCK -> hertz
Description: The system clock as it is actually running. Boards only.

[SD.TEST]
Syntax: SD.TEST -> text$
Description: Probes the card slot and reports what answered: the card's response to each initialisation step, and the first bytes it returned. RP2350 with a card slot only. A card that will not mount is usually not formatted.

[SD.BB]
Syntax: SD.BB -> text$
Description: Drives the card's wires by hand rather than through the SPI block, which separates a card that is not answering from a bus that is not being driven. RP2350 with a card slot only.

[FS.TEST]
Syntax: FS.TEST -> text$
Description: Writes, reads back and erases in the flash store, and reports what each step returned. Boards only. Non-zero error codes on the erase and program steps mean the other core is running without having called into the flash-safety contract.

[FS.ALIAS]
Syntax: FS.ALIAS -> text$
Description: Where the flash store is actually mapped, and what the same bytes look like through the other address windows. RP2350 only.

[FS.ATRANS]
Syntax: FS.ATRANS -> text$
Description: The four address-translation registers as they stand. RP2350 only. A uf2 that boots through translation reads its own flash somewhere other than zero.

[FS.NUKEPT]
Syntax: FS.NUKEPT
Description: Erases the partition table at the physical start of flash and drops to BOOTSEL. RP2350 only, and one-way: the next uf2 lands at zero and boots without address translation.

[PSRAM.ID$]
Syntax: PSRAM.ID$ -> text$
Description: The PSRAM chip's identity as it answers it. RP2350 only; empty on a board without one.

[PIO.LOAD]
Syntax: PIO.LOAD(words) -> offset
Description: Loads an assembled PIO program (an array of 16-bit instruction words) and answers where it landed. RP2350 only.

[PIO.START]
Syntax: PIO.START(sm, offset, len, pin [, divider])
Description: Starts state machine sm on the program at that offset, with the pin as its first output. RP2350 only.

[PIO.PUT]
Syntax: PIO.PUT(sm, value)
Description: Puts a word in the state machine's transmit queue. RP2350 only. Does not block: a full queue drops the word.

[PIO.GET]
Syntax: PIO.GET(sm) -> value
Description: Takes a word from the state machine's receive queue, or -1 when there is none. RP2350 only.

[PIO.STOP]
Syntax: PIO.STOP(sm)
Description: Stops the state machine and lets go of its pins. RP2350 only.

[NTP.SYNC]
Syntax: NTP.SYNC([server$] [, hours_from_utc]) -> seconds | 0
Description: Sets the board's clock from a time server, so DATE$, TIME$ and NOW mean something, and returns the local time it set as epoch seconds. Zero means nothing answered. RP2350 W boards, ESP32-S3 and Fruit Jam. The RP2350 W boards ask server$ (default pool.ntp.org) and time.google.com when it does not answer; the ESP32-S3 always asks pool.ntp.org and the Fruit Jam takes the radio's own clock, and on those two a single argument is the hour offset. The offset is yours to give: the protocol carries UTC and knows nothing about where the board is.

[WIFI.DNS$]
Syntax: WIFI.DNS$ -> text$
Description: The name server currently in use. RP2350 W boards only.

[WIFI.DNS]
Syntax: WIFI.DNS(address$) -> 0 | -1
Description: Sets the name server by address. RP2350 W boards only, for a network whose DHCP hands out one that does not answer.

[WIFI.SCAN]
Syntax: WIFI.SCAN([ms]) -> array
Description: The networks the radio can hear, strongest first, each as ssid, signal, channel and whether it is open. ESP32-S3 only. Hidden networks come back with an empty name rather than being left out.

[HTTP.STATUS]
Syntax: HTTP.STATUS -> code
Description: The status code the last HTTP.GET$ or HTTP.POST$ came back with. Boards with a radio only. Both answer with an empty string on failure, and this says whether that was a 404 or no answer at all.

[HTTP.SERVER.POLL]
Syntax: HTTP.SERVER.POLL -> count
Description: One pass of the server: hands over whatever requests have arrived and returns how many it served. Boards only. For a program that runs its own loop; HTTP.SERVER.WAIT is the same thing kept up.

[HTTP.SERVER.SERVED]
Syntax: HTTP.SERVER.SERVED -> count
Description: How many requests this server has answered since it started. Boards only.

[PSRAM.TEST$]
Syntax: PSRAM.TEST$ -> text$
Description: Writes a pattern at each end of the PSRAM window and reads it back, answering with the size, the address it is mapped at, and whether it survived. RP2350 boards whose PSRAM is on the QMI bus only; the Fruit Jam is one.

[KEY.NOW]
Syntax: KEY.NOW -> code | -1
Description: One key code if one is waiting, -1 if none is. Boards only. The one a game loop needs, where KEY.GET waits. Reads whatever console the board has, so the same loop works on the board's own keyboard and over the serial line.

[KEY.LOCAL]
Syntax: KEY.LOCAL [(now)] -> TRUE | FALSE
Description: Whether a keyboard on the board's I2C connector answered. ES3C28P only, for an M5Stack CardKB at 0x5F. While absent it is probed again after two seconds, then at doubling intervals up to half a minute, so one plugged in after boot turns this true on its own. A true argument probes now instead of waiting out that backoff.

[KEY.RAW]
Syntax: KEY.RAW -> [code, ...]
Description: The codes the I2C keyboard sent, before the Fn layer was folded into control codes and editor keys. ES3C28P only, and the reading empties it. For settling what a key actually sends rather than trusting a table.

[SYS.PSRAMLARGEST]
Syntax: SYS.PSRAMLARGEST -> bytes
Description: The biggest single block the PSRAM heap will hand over. Fruit Jam only. The companion to SYS.LARGEST, and the number that matters when a program grows one large array.

[PSRAM.TORTURE$]
Syntax: PSRAM.TORTURE$([rounds=2000]) -> text$
Description: Allocates, fills, verifies and frees blocks in the PSRAM pool while the scanout and the USB host are running, and says how many it got through and whether anything came back changed. Fruit Jam only. The desktop cannot reproduce the part that matters here, which is the traffic on the same memory controller.

[SYS.HEAP$]
Syntax: SYS.HEAP$ -> text$
Description: Where the heap stands, in the allocator's own terms: arena is what it has taken off the break so far, used and free divide that, frags counts the free pieces, and ground is the stretch below the stack that nobody has claimed yet. RP2350 only. SYS.FREE adds the last two together; this says which of them a program is actually short of.

[SYS.PEEKB]
Syntax: SYS.PEEKB(addr) -> number
Description: Reads 8 bits from physical memory. Kernel target only (--target=kernel); runs in ring 0.

[SYS.PEEKW]
Syntax: SYS.PEEKW(addr) -> number
Description: Reads 16 bits from physical memory. Kernel target only.

[SYS.PEEK]
Syntax: SYS.PEEK(addr) -> number
Description: Reads 32 bits from physical memory. Kernel target only.

[SYS.POKEB]
Syntax: SYS.POKEB(addr, value)
Description: Writes 8 bits to physical memory. Kernel target only; a wrong address can hang the machine.

[SYS.POKEW]
Syntax: SYS.POKEW(addr, value)
Description: Writes 16 bits to physical memory, for example a character cell of the VGA text screen at $B8000. Kernel target only.

[SYS.POKE]
Syntax: SYS.POKE(addr, value)
Description: Writes 32 bits to physical memory. Kernel target only.

[SYS.INB]
Syntax: SYS.INB(port) -> number
Description: Reads a byte from an x86 I/O port, for example 96 for the keyboard controller. Kernel target only.

[SYS.OUTB]
Syntax: SYS.OUTB(port, value)
Description: Writes a byte to an x86 I/O port. Kernel target only.

[SYS.CALL]
Syntax: SYS.CALL(addr) -> number
Description: Calls machine code the program wrote into memory at addr. The code takes no arguments, follows the System V calling convention and returns its result in rax. Kernel target only.
